body: PRESS STATEMENT May 31, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation – Human Trafficking Division arrested Roberto G. Albaña Jr., Avelino D. Gueta Jr., Junroso E. Bansil and Danilo P. Abacaro for Robbery Extortion in Pasay City on May 27, 2024. The case stemmed from a complaint of a South Korean National alleging that a group is demanding money in the amount of Php 2,000,000.00, and threatened the complainant’s cousin with deportation charges unless payment is made. The complainant said that the group is led by a certain “Atty. Mark Barizo” and introduced themselves as officers from the Office of the President and Bureau of Immigration. Upon verifying from the Supreme Court’s website, the name “Mark Barizo” does not appear on the list of lawyers. Hence, an entrapment operation was then conducted together with the assistance of NBI-Homicide Division and International Operations Division which resulted in the arrest of the Subjects. Several firearms, rounds of ammunition, and IDs under the National Intelligence Coordinating Agency (NICA) were found in the Subjects’ possession. Arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceeding before the Office of the Prosecutor’s Office on Wednesday.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT March 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NCR), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in Paranaque City for sexually molesting his three (3) biological daughters. On March 6, 2025, minor complainants filed a complaint before the NBI-NCR against their biological father. In complainants’ sworn statements, they alleged that their father had raped them multiple times which started in 2022. They were threatened not to tell anyone about the incidents as something bad will happen to them. Victims reported the incident to their mother but she refused to believe them, dismissing the children’s claim as made up story, and instead sided with their father. On March 10, 2025, the brother of the female victims executed his sworn statement stating that he received text messages from the Subject, threatening and intimidating him and his younger siblings after they reported the incident to the NBI-NCR. Part of the text message includes a threat that Subject will kill them if they would further report the matter. The text messages prompted NCR Agents to proceed to Baclaran, Paranaque City to conduct hot pursuit operation against the Subject on March 11, 2025, anchored on the ongoing grave threats to the minor victims. Upon arrival in Baclaran, Paranaque City, the NCR Agents approached the Subject and introduced themselves as operatives, informed him of the complaint against him and that he will be arrested. Subject resisted arrest and acted violently, thus a scuffle ensued. Eventually, Subject was subdued, placed under arrest, and was informed of his constitutional rights. Subject was brought to NBI-NCR, Taft Avenue, Manila where he underwent the standard booking procedures. He was presented for inquest proceedings for violations of Republic Act No. 8353 (Anti-Rape Law) in relation to Section 5(b) of Republic Act No. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI THROWBACK Ito na ata ang pinaka-toxic na “I love you” sa kasaysayan ng mundo. 💔💻😂 Noong May 2000, may isang Pinoy computer student na gumawa ng email na may subject na “ILOVEYOU.” Akala ng mundo , Mensaheng sweet… yun pala virus na pagkaraming nakasungkit. Boom. Millions of computers down. Billions ang damage. Global panic. Nangarag ang mga IT experts. Yes, this is about the then NBI – Anti-Fraud and Computer Crimes Division investigating Onel de Guzman, the guy linked to the legendary ILOVEYOU worm. Ang plot twist? Walang nakulong. Why? Kasi noong time na ‘yon, wala pang malinaw na cybercrime law sa Pilipinas. Even the Federal Bureau of Investigation got involved kasi pati ang United States of A, tinamaan. The virus spread through Microsoft Outlook emails na may attachment na kunwari love letter. Pag-click mo… goodbye files, hello chaos. Damage? Around $8.7 BILLION worldwide Lesson? Hindi lahat ng “I love you” , message, safe buksan. Pero dahil sa incident na ‘to, napilitan gumawa ng mas malinaw na cybercrime laws ang Pilipinas after. So in a weird way… 💘 Isang “ILOVEYOU” na email ➡️ naging dahilan para seryosohin ang cybersecurity Kaya this Valentine’s: If someone emails you “ILOVEYOU”… kilalanin mo muna wag basta mag -click mas safe pa rin yung may flowers, or may chocolate o kaya may suman sa latik.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT July 24, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI, ARESTADO ANG ISANG INDIBIDWAL SA PAGGAWA NG PEKENG BIRTH CERTIFICATE SA QUEZON CITY Lungsod ng Pasay – Sa ilalim ng pamumuno ni NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag, mas pinaigting ng NBI-Counter Terrorism Division (NBI-CTD) ang kampanya laban sa pagkalat ng mga pekeng dokumento, na nagresulta sa pagkaaresto ng isang indibidwal sa isang entrapment operation sa Quezon City. Inaresto ang suspek dahil sa paglabag sa Artikulo 172 ng Revised Penal Code (Falsification of Public Document by Private Individual) na may kaugnayan sa Artikulo 191. Ang operasyon ay nagmula sa impormasyon na ang suspek ay nagpoproseso ng mga pekeng birth certificate kapalit ng bayad, gamit ang mga papel, tinta, at QR Codes ng Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) na matatagpuan sa PSA Main Office, East Avenue, Quezon City. Agad na nakipag-ugnayan ang NBI-CTD sa suspek. Nagkasundo ang undercover agents at ang suspek na magkita noong Hulyo 14, 2026, ngunit inilipat ito ng suspek sa umaga ng Hulyo 15, 2026. Hiningi ng suspek ang pangalan, petsa ng kapanganakan, lugar ng kapanganakan, at pangalan ng ama at ina na ilalagay sa birth certificate. Nagkakahalaga ang bawat kopya ng Php5,000.00. Umorder ang undercover agent ng dalawang (2) pekeng birth certificate at nagpadala ng Php1,000.00 down payment sa GCash number ng suspek. Noong Hulyo 15, 2026, nagsagawa ng entrapment operation ang NBI-CTD sa Quezon City. Inaresto ang suspek matapos nitong ibigay ang dalawang (2) pekeng birth certificate at tanggapin ang markadong pera. Pinuri ni NBI Director Matibag ang mga ahente ng NBI-CTD sa kanilang masusing imbestigasyon na humantong sa pagkaaresto ng suspek. Binigyang-diin niya na ang paglaganap ng mga pekeng dokumento ay malaking banta sa kaligtasan at tiwala ng publiko. https://www.facebook.com/reel/883882578118326

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A man long wanted by the law for killing the budget officer of a Nueva Vizcaya university in 2011 was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya. The suspect is REONEL MARTINEZ, 42, a resident of Dullao, Nueva Vizcaya. Investigation by the NBI Bayombong District Office (BAYDO) disclosed that Arlyne Fernandez, budget officer of the Nueva Vizcaya State University, (NVSU) was fatally shot by two unidentified suspects in the morning of August 15, 2011 while on board a tricycle inside the university compound. The victim died of multiple gunshot wounds while the two suspects casually fled after the incident. Several witnesses pointed to Martinez as the gunman. He and his companion are believed to be members of a gun-for-hire group. In June, 2012, the NBI received the complaint about said case. Thereafter, a parallel investigation was conducted with the police. While the case of Murder is being prepared against the suspect, the NBI office received a tip that the suspect was seen loitering in the vicinity of Bambang, Nueva Vizcaya carrying an unlicensed firearms for reportedly intending to commit another crime. A surveillance was conducted on Martinez. In the morning of March 21, 2013, suspect was spotted by NBI operatives at a gasoline station along the Heroes Highway in said town. He was immediately accosted and taken by surprise, he did not resist arrest. Found in his possession were an unlicensed cal. .45 pistol, with four (4) live ammunitions, a home-made Magnum .22 cal. with magazine and 51 live ammunition, a handcuff and a Citizen’s Crime Strike Group badge and identification cards. He was brought to the NBI office in Bayombong City. Later he was referred for inquest at the Nueva Vizcaya Provincial Prosecutor’s Office for violation of PD 1866 (Illegal Possession of Firearms and Ammunition) under RA 8042 and Murder. During the inquest, suspect signed a waiver and invoked his right to a preliminary investigation. Consequently, he was turned over to the Bureau of Jail Management and Penology in Solano, Nueva Vizcaya.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A construction worker allegedly responsible for the rape slay of a 25-year-old woman was arrested by the agents of the National Bureau Investigation (NBI) in coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP) in Pasig City during the weekend. The suspect was identified by NBI Officer-In-Charge Atty. Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as ALFREDO MICARES Y ATUD, 35, construction worker and a resident of Teresa Compound, Pilar Village, Rosario, Pasig City. The victim was Anna Ysabel Santos y Cordova, 25, single, and a resident of No. 27 Pearl Compound, Dona Juana, Subdivision, Rosario, Pasig City. Investigation conducted by the ODDSIS represented by the Death Investigation Division (DID) headed by Atty. Romulo Asis, ODDIS headed by Atty. Ruel M. Lasala and NCR under Regional Director Jorge Jularbal disclosed that in the afternoon of March 21, 2012, Kristine Camille Santos, victim’s sister saw Anna’s car in front of the residence and thought that she was already in her room. At 5:30 pm that day, Kristine received a call from one Kristin Tanyag requesting the whereabouts of Anna who allegedly missed her flight to Boracay at noon of that day. Kristin rushed to Anna’s room and found in the pool of her blood lying a top her bed. Kristin called the police as well as barangay authorities. The PNP-Pasig proceeded to the crime scene to investigate. An NBI team also conducted a reprocessing of the crime scene, lifted fingerprints and blood samples. On April 18, 2012, Mark Santos, victim’s cousin and contractor of the renovation of the victim’s house together with three (3) construction workers namely: ALFREDO MICARES Y ATUD, MANNY SARMIENTO Y SERNA and DANILO BOLADO Y MONTECILLO went to the NBI office and submitted their blood samples for investigation. That same evening, a reenactment was made by a joint team of NBI and PNP probers together with Micares. During the process, security guard GENIE ALABERAN HERNAEZ approached the team and positively identified ALFREDO MICARES as the same person who requested entry at 11:00 pm of March 21, 2012. Thereafter, Micares readily admitted the crime and was brought back to the NBI main office. Found near the sink of the dirty kitchen is a kitchen knife which when submitted for forensic examination yielded positive for blood samples of victim, ANNA YSABEL SANTOS. On April 19, 2012 suspect MICARES executed an extra judicial confession assisted by his lawyers and admitted the crime. He recounted that, on the midnight of March 22, 2012, he was heavily drunk and went to Doña Juana Subdivision. He was refused entry by the guard at Gate 3 but he managed to sneak in through the gate’s small hole and proceeded to the victim’s house. Using an improvised tool, he made his way to victim ANNA’s room and found her asleep. He took her personal belongings such as (IPAD 2, BLACKBERRY CP, ITOUCH, SONY VAIO, DIGICAM with an estimated amount of Php 130,000.00). Victim was roused from sleep and gave a fight with her knife hidden underneath the bed, but was overpowered during the scuffle, Anna was stabbed several times by Micares which caused her death. She was also raped by Micares. After placing the valuables inside a paper bag, he sneaked out of the house and passed through Gate 2 and went home to his residence in Las Piñas. Charges with robbery with homicide and rape were forwarded for inquest to the City Prosecutor of Pasig City on April 23, 2012 and docketed as XV-14-INQ-12D.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF), together with the Philippine Coast Guard, rescued one hundred thirty two (132) individuals in Orion, Bataan who were promised employment in Micronesia. The NBI received a request letter for assistance from RADM Joel S. Garcia, Director of the National Coast Watch Center (NCWC) of the Office of the President. The letter states that they received an information regarding a domestic passenger vessel docked in Orion, Bataan which is allegedly involved in human smuggling and other illegal activities. Acting on the request, NBI-STF operatives conducted a verification with the Philippine Coast Guard and it was discovered that the Domestic Vessel M/V Forever Lucky owned by Fahrenheit Company Ltd was attempting to take a voyage enroute to Yap Island Micronesia without the proper licenses and permit coming from the proper authority. It was also discovered that the management of the said vessel was using a Special Permit to Navigate allegedly issued by a suspended director of the Maritime Industry Authority Regional Office (ARMM). On July 2, 2018, NBI-STF operatives, in coordination with the Philippine Coast Guard conducted an inspection in the aforementioned area. It was discovered that on board M/V Lucky Forever were the 132 individuals who were recruited by the management of Fahrenheit Company without requiring the necessary documents such as working visa, seaman’s book, and other documents which allows a Filipino to work overseas. The 132 individuals, which include tattoo artists, massage attendants, entertainers, bar tenders, food attendants, and pig roasters, were then rescued. Although there were no minors, they will be turned over to the custody of the municipal social welfare and development officer for re-evaluation. Officers and staff of Fahrenheit Company Ltd namely, ISAGANI CABRERA, MABEL MARTINEZ, RAUL MANCELITA, RACHELLE MALVAR, and JIRACEL OBDIN were then arrested and were charged for Syndicated and Large Scale Illegal Recruitment under RA 8042 otherwise known as the Migrants Workers Act.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In support of the government’s initiative towards a “Bagong Pilipinas,” the National Bureau of Investigation – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) conducted an entrapment operation in Quezon City, resulting in the arrest of Rhea S. Rivera, Mia Lyn Cunanan, and Rodel C. Deniega. They were apprehended for violation of Presidential Decree No. 1612 (Anti-Fencing Law of 1979) in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). A complaint was filed with the NBI-OTCD, reporting the loss of a container loaded with imported frozen beef shanks, valued between PHP 5,000,000.00 and PHP 6,900,000.00. The Complainant was able to trace portions of the missing shipment being sold online through a social media platform under the account name “Kaye’s Imported Cold Cuts” – Frozen Meat Supplier at BMR Frozen Meat Products Trading (BMR) located in Cubao, Quezon City. On August 22, 2025, agents of the NBI-OTCD, accompanied by the complainant, went to BMR to place an order for 30 boxes of Beef Forequarter Shin Shanks and 7 boxes of Hind Shanks, totaling PHP 133,884.40. After handing over the marked money and confirming that the purchased meat products were portions of the missing container, the NBI-OTCD agents immediately announced their authority and arrested Subjects Rivera, who received the marked money; Cunanan, who acted as the cashier; and Daniega, who released the meat products. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 37 boxes of meat products and six cellular phones used by the subjects in their operation. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City, for the aforementioned violations. Also included in the charges for the same violations are Michelle Rivera Melendrez, registered owner of BMR, and Kaye Daniega, owner of the social media account that was selling the said meat products.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 13, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES NEARLY ₱246 MILLION WORTH OF COUNTERFEIT PRODUCTS IN MULTI-CITY RAID PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD), has successfully conducted a series of enforcement operations across the National Capital Region (NCR) and Northern Mindanao, resulting in the seizure of counterfeit goods valued at approximately ₱245,898,950.00. The NBI-IPRD implemented the search warrants in two major operations, beginning on 09 February 2026, within the NCR. During the initial phase, operatives raided four locations across Manila, Valenzuela, and Quezon City, resulting in the seizure of 22,750 pieces of counterfeit “Ultra White Sunscreen” bearing the “HIKARI” trademark, valued at approximately ₱3,413,000.00. The following day, 10 February 2026, enforcement efforts shifted to Northern Mindanao, where five establishments in Cagayan de Oro City were served search warrants. The second operation led to the recovery of a massive haul of high-end counterfeit eyewear, including 9,571 pieces of fake “LUXOTTICA/RAYBAN” and 4,525 pieces of fake “OAKLEY” products, with a total estimated value of ₱242,485,950.00. The NBI underscored that the production, sale, and distribution of these goods constitute a direct violation of Republic Act No. 8293, otherwise known as the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” The involved Subjects are facing charges related to Trademark Infringement and Unfair Competition. The NBI issued a stern warning regarding the health risks associated with “knock-off” products. Manufacturers of counterfeit goods often disregard consumer safety, using the cheapest substances or chemicals available without regard for potential health hazards. The Bureau urges the public to remain vigilant and avoid purchasing these products, which not only pose risks to personal health but also undermine the country’s economic growth. The NBI remains committed to protecting intellectual property rights and ensuring that the Philippine market remains safe for both legitimate businesses and consumers. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cavite North District Office (NBI-CAVIDO North) arrested AKIRA MACHIDA, a Japanese national, together with his cohorts GLENN BELTRAN HUERTO and CHRISTOPHER LATTAO MARAMAG, in an entrapment operation in the City of Manila for Grave Threats under Article 282 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) in relation to Republic Act No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by two (2) Japanese nationals against Subject Machida. The complainants revealed through their affidavits that Subject Machida availed of the service of one of the complainants (contractor), who was engaged in the construction business, for the renovation of the subject’s coffee shop. Both parties agreed on a contract amount of Php4,728,000.00. After some time, the contractor discovered that the coffee shop was neither owned nor leased by Subject Machida but was actually owned by Subject Beltran and Frenelyn Libao Soloria. Despite this, the contractor proceeded with the renovation project and received an initial amount of Php3,309,000.00 representing 70% of the total contract price. Weeks later, while the renovation project was ongoing, Subject Machida was no longer able to bankroll the project, which eventually forced the contractor to stop the renovation. Subject Machida then urged the contractor to take out a loan, promising him the proceeds from the sale of his property in Japan. Unfortunately, the loan did not materialize. On September 20, 2025, Subject Machida, together with Subject Huerto and Maramag, set a meeting with the complainants, wherein they threatened to kill the Complainants if they did not pay a penalty, and they were also prepared to have them arrested by the Police. The next day, one of the complainants was contacted by Subject Machida, demanding Php10,000,000.00 for them to be forgiven. The Complainants were also contacted by Subject Maramag for the delivery of half of the demanded sum of money and threatened to harm them and their family if they failed to comply. On October 1, 2025, NBI-CAVIDO North agents, along with the complainants, proceeded to the agreed-upon meeting place in an establishment in the City of Manila for the handover of the demanded money. Upon receiving the marked money, the NBI-CAVIDO North agents immediately approached Subject Machida and placed him under arrest. Also arrested were his companions/cohorts, Subjects Huerto and Maramag. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Manila, for the aforementioned violation. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) lauded the agents of NBI-CAVIDO North for their successful operation leading to the arrest of the subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the order of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against Human Trafficking and Illegal Recruitment, the NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested JACOB JUMALON TUBALLA for violation of R.A. No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. No. 10022 and violation of R.A. No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003), as amended by R.A No. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012), and further amended by R.A. No. 11862 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022). On January 20, 2025, the Ninoy Aquino International Airport – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (NAIA-IACAT) Task Force turned over to the NBI-IAID four (4) passengers suspected to be victims of Trafficking in Persons and/or Illegal Recruitment. Initially, the four (4) passengers were intercepted by I-PROBES Terminal Head, NAIA Terminal 1 and were turned over to the NBI-IACAT. In response, the Agents of NBI-IAID conducted an investigation, which revealed that three (3) of the offloaded passengers were pretending to be tourists bound for Vietnam. The three (3) victims disclosed that the actual reason of their travel is to fly to Bulgaria for employment purposes. The Victims also revealed through their Sworn Statement that their companion Subject Tuballa is the one who recruited them and facilitated their travel to Vietnam. The Subject assured the Victims that they will be employed as “Ironers” in Bulgaria and promised one (1) of the Victims that she will receive a salary of BGN 1,400.00 (Php34,000.00), while the two (2) others will receive a salary of 550 to 800 Euros. Verification made by the Agents of NBI-IAID with the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) revealed through certification that Subject Tuballa is not licensed/authorized by the DMW to recruit workers for overseas employment. Thus, the Agents of NBI-IAID placed Subject Tuballa under arrest and was presented for inquest proceedings before the Duty Inquest Prosecutor of Pasay City for the above-stated violations. Director Santiago lauded the Agents of NBI-IAID for the apprehension of the Subject and stressed the NBI’s unwavering commitment in the fight against human trafficking.

body: A notorious robbery gang preying on wealthy residents was busted following the arrest of the mastermind and his cohort by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Baguio City last weekend. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: RANDY ANDRADE YACAP, native of Bugallon, Pangasinan and residing in Baguio City and; ROMULO TAN MARAYA, residing at San Luis Extension, Baguio City. Investigation conducted by the NBI-Codillera Administrative Region (CAR) headed by RD Jose A. Limmayog, Jr. disclosed that it received information about the activities of a notorious robbery gang who were responsible for a series of robberies committed on wealthy residents in Baguio City. On May 31, 2013, an informant called up the NBI-CAR and informed them that the gang was about to strike anew in QM, Quarry and they were sighted along Legarda Road, Baguio City. NBI operatives and the informant immediately rushed to Legarda Road and trailed two (2) identified suspects riding in a taxi. Upon reaching Happy Glenn loop, they alighted and walked towards Hotel 45. Seizing the opportunity. NBI agents alighted from their vehicles and approached the two (2) suspects. After introducing themselves and informing the suspects of the robberies they committed, the operatives arrested the two (2) suspects. They turned out to be suspects YACAP and MARAYA. Seized from YACAP was a homemade Magnum 357 with five (5) live ammunition, while confiscated from MARAYA was a homemade .38 cal. Revolver with five (5) live ammunition and some tools. Thereafter, they were brought to the NBI office for booking and detention. Subsequently, the duo were referred for inquest at the City Prosecutor’s Office in Baguio City for violation of PD 1866, as amended by RA 8294 (Illegal possession of firearms and ammunition); and for violation of the COMELEC gun ban. They were turned over to the BJMP.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 28, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | 23 KABABAIHAN NASAGIP NG NBI-CAMARINES NORTE SA VIDEOKE BAR; 2 SUSPEK, ARESTADO Matagumpay na naaresto ng National Bureau of Investigation – Camarines Norte District Office (NBI-CAMNODO) ang dalawang suspek sa ginawang entrapment operation sa Black Pink Videoke Bar na matatagpuan sa Bagumbayan, Paracale, Camarines Norte. Isinagawa ang entrapment operation matapos makatanggap ang NBI ng report mula sa isang Confidential Informant (CI) ukol sa umano’y pagre-recruit at pagpapatrabaho sa mga batang kababaihan para sa sexual exploitation at prostitusyon. Matapos kumpirmahin ang impormasyon sa pamamagitan ng surveillance, ikinasa ng NBI katuwang ang PSWDO Camarines Norte at Paracale Municipal Police Station ang entrapment operation kung saan huling-huli sa akto ang dalawang suspek na hawak ang marked money. Dahil sa mabilis na aksyon ng mga awtoridad, matagumpay na nasagip ang 23 batang kababaihan na karamihan ay nanggaling pa sa ibang lalawigan tulad ng Quezon, Nueva Vizcaya, Laguna, Davao, at Cebu. Pormal nang isinailalim sa inquest proceedings ang dalawang suspek sa Provincial Prosecution Office para sa paglabag sa Section 4(a) ng Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) at kasalukuyang nasa kustodiya ng Paracale Municipal Police Station, habang ang 23 nasagip na kababaihan ay ligtas at maayos na naproseso ng mga social workers. Binigyang-diin ni NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag na mananatili ang kampanya ng NBI laban sa human trafficking, kasabay ng paninindigang hindi hahayaang manaig ang mga taong nagsasamantala at kumikita sa paglabag sa dignidad at karapatan ng ating mga kababaihan. Aniya, ang matagumpay na operasyong ito ay sumasalamin sa matibay na paninindigan ng NBI na pangalagaan ang ating mga mamamayan at tiyaking mananagot sa batas ang lahat ng sangkot sa human trafficking, saanman sila nagtatago sa bansa https://www.facebook.com/reel/965858596470374

Aniya, ang matagumpay na operasyong ito ay sumasalamin sa matibay na paninindigan ng NBI na pangalagaan ang ating mga mamamayan at tiyaking mananagot sa batas ang lahat ng sangkot sa human trafficking, saanman sila nagtatago sa bansa https://www.facebook.com/reel/965858596470374

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 19, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested an individual in NAIA, Pasay City for Large Scale Illegal Recruitment under Republic Act No. 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995), as amended by R.A. No. 10022, and Qualified Trafficking in Persons committed in Large Scale under R.A. No. 9208 as amended by R.A. No. 11862. The arrest was made after Immigration Officers intercepted seven individuals, including the Subject, who were bound for Vietnam. During departure formalities, it was discovered that their true purpose for traveling was to seek employment in Cambodia as “Chat Support” or “Customer Service Representatives.” Investigation revealed that Subject recruited the six victims for these overseas positions, offering a salary of USD 500 to USD 800. Verification conducted with the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) confirmed that Subject is neither licensed nor authorized to recruit workers for overseas employment. Based on the statements of the victims and evidence gathered, Subject was placed under arrest by the Agents of NBI-IAID on November 9, 2025. He was then presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City through a virtual inquest for the aforementioned violations. OIC Director Atty. Angelito DLP Magno said that the recent successful operation conducted by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is part of their sustained efforts to combat human trafficking in the country. He highlighted the critical importance of increasing operational activities aimed at addressing both human trafficking and illegal recruitment practices. These measures are essential in protecting individuals who are at risk of exploitation by unscrupulous recruiters, particularly those seeking employment opportunities abroad. Magno underscored the necessity of vigilance and proactive interventions to ensure the safety and well-being of vulnerable populations who may be targets of these criminal activities.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI- Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) have seized a total of Php 86.5 Million worth of counterfeit Nike and Converse shoes in an operation in Pasay City. On March 21, 2017, Judge Rainelda H. Estacio-Montesa of RTC Branch 46, Manila issued Search Warrant against Subjects Ana Chua, Wang Yu Bo, and other proprietors/occupants of premises located in various units at 111 J. Fernando Street, Pasay City and at One Shopping Center, Kapitan Ambo Street, Pasay City. Charges for Violation of R.A. 8293 otherwise known as the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines are now being prepared against the Subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI ARRESTS TWO CHINESE NATIONALS IN QUEZON CITY KIDNAP-FOR-RANSOM PLOT; VICTIM RESCUED PASAY, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation – International Operation Division (NBI-IOD) has successfully rescued a Chinese national and arrested two of her compatriots during a high-stakes entrapment operation in Quezon City on 11 February 2026. The investigation began after the victim’s boyfriend reported her missing. On 09 February 2026, the complainant managed to contact the victim via Viber, only to be informed that she was being held against her will. During the call, one of the kidnappers seized the phone and demanded a ransom of Php 500,000.00 for her release. Investigations later revealed that the abductors had already coerced the victim into transferring RMB 104,000.00 (approx. Php 832,000.00) via online transfers before the ransom demand was even made. To pressure the complainant, the kidnappers permitted a video call where the victim displayed visible bruising on her body. The suspects threatened to dismember or kill the victim if the ransom was not paid by February 10. Communication was subsequently moved to Telegram to evade detection. On 11 February 2026, a strategic entrapment operation was executed by NBI-IOD Operatives at a hotel in Quezon City. As the marked ransom money was exchanged, NBI agents immediately moved in, successfully arresting two Chinese nationals and ensuring the safe recovery of the victim, who is now out of harm’s way. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention, in relation to Section 6 of Republic Act No. 10175, also known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. “The NBI will be relentless in pursuing criminals who target both Filipinos and foreign nationals, ensuring that our country remains a safe haven for all,” stated NBI Acting Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno. He commended the IOD agents for their swift action and reiterated the Bureau’s commitment to maintaining a secure environment where foreign guests and residents are protected and criminal syndicates find no room to operate. ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 2, 2022 NBI ARRESTS TWO AFTER DEROGATORY RECORDS SURFACED DURING NBI CLEARANCE APPLICATION The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of two individuals charged with Rape in Nueva Ecija. Arrested individuals were identified as JOSE JR. BIDO y LOPEZ and VINCENT EMMANUEL GAN y DE GUZMAN. Both BIDO and GAN were arrested by operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) after they applied for NBI Clearance. As per NBI Clearance Quality Control, derogatory record showed remarks that BIDO is “Wanted” for the crime of Rape. In coordination with RTC Branch 19, Bacoor, Cavite, NBI-CABDO operative found out that the case on the record was BIDO’s criminal record. On the other hand, when GAN applied for NBI Clearance, his NBI Clearance Quality Control Derogatory Record showed remarks that he was “Charged/At Large” for the crime of Rape. He was then interviewed and was found out that the criminal case on record pertains to him. Coordination with RTC Branch 23, Trece Martires, Cavite, where the case was filed, was likewise made. Notably, the arrest of the two accused proves that NBI Clearance is the most reliable clearance service in the country, the NBI being the national repository of all criminal records NBI-CABDO expresses gratitude to the full cooperation of RTC Branch 19 and 23, especially to the clerks of both courts, for the speedy verification and transmittal of Subjects court records, and to Agent-In Charge Eric Mercado and Agent-In Charge Jun Astrero, and staff of NBI-CAVIDO North and South for the inter-district courtesy and cooperation.

body: PRESS STATEMENT November 2, 2022 NBI ARRESTS ONE FOR MULTIPLE VIOLATIONS, ALL IN RELATION TO THE CYBERCRIME LAW The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of ANTHONY QUEZON y EBONA a.k.a. “LOUIE JOHN DIAZ” by the NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) in an entrapment operation in Quezon City. According to the Complainant, she met Subject Quezon thru BIGO LIVE APP who introduced himself as LOUIE JOHN DIAZ from Seattle, USA, 30 years of age and single. They continued their communication on iMessage and Facebook (FB) Messenger, and after almost a year of courtship, their relationship was made official on January 25, 2021. During their relationship, Subject Quezon’s and the Complainant’s video calls became more intimate and they would video call each other while pleasuring themselves. After sometime, the Complainant asked for Subject’s passport and ID to know more about the latter. Subject Quezon obliged and sent photos of his passport and driver’s license and IDs. Complainant then discovered that the latter’s real name is ANTHONY QUEZON y EBONA. After Complainant learned about the personal circumstances of Subject, the former tried to break-up with the latter, who, nonetheless, managed to make Complainant stay in the relationship. After sometime, a certain FB account communicated with her on FB Messenger and introduced herself as wife of Subject Quezon. She even sent a family picture together with Subject Quezon and an infant. Complainant immediately contacted Subject Quezon and broke-up with him. Unwilling to let her go, Subject Quezon threatened the complainant that he will upload their intimate videos on porn sites, FB and other social media platforms, which the subject previously recorded without the permission of the complainant. On October 8, 2022, Complainant informed the NBI-CCD that Subject arrived in the Philippines and was pestering her to meet with him. Subject Quezon told Complainant that if she agrees to meet with him, he would delete their intimate videos. Otherwise, he will upload the videos on various social media platforms. Agents of NBI-CCD immediately planned an entrapment operation, which led to the apprehension of Subject Quezon. Subject Quezon was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for violation of R.A. 9262 otherwise known as the Anti-Violence Against Women and their Children Act of 2004, Section 4 (a) of R.A. 9995 otherwise known as The Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009, and Grave Coercion punishable under Article 286 of the Revised Penal Code, all in relation to R.A. 10175 otherwise known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as BAINISIN PULNA a.k.a. ELSA CORNELLO SALADILI. Subject Pulna was about to depart on April 16, 2021 for Saudi Arabia via Gulf Air Flight when she was questioned by the duty Immigration Officers. Subject Punla gave inconsistent and contradicting statements regarding her age during the secondary inspection. Subject Pulna was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Pasay City, for violation of Section 19 (d) (1) of R.A. 8239, otherwise known as the Philippine Passport Act of 1996.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 26, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI-LAOAG ARRESTS SUSPECTS IN ILLEGAL INVESTMENT SCHEME The National Bureau of Investigation – Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO), in coordination with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Laoag Extension Office, successfully conducted an entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of two individuals involved in an alleged illegal investment scheme in Laoag City. Subjects who were apprehended on March 25, 2026, at around 3:30 PM in Brgy. 25, Laoag City, Ilocos Norte. The operation stemmed from a request by the SEC after receiving information that Aura Financing Corporation was offering investment opportunities without proper registration or authority to solicit investments from the public. Prior to the operation, NBI-LADO conducted surveillance which confirmed that the suspects were actively engaging in investment activities, including accepting money from investors and issuing investment contracts. During the entrapment operation, NBI operatives acting as poseur-investors handed over ₱100,000.00 to the suspects in exchange for an investment contract, leading to their immediate arrest. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Laoag City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of the Securities Regulation Code (RA 8799). NBI Director Atty. Melvin Matibag emphasized the Bureau’s firm stance against illegal investment activities: “We will not allow individuals or groups to take advantage of the public through fraudulent investment schemes. The NBI, in close coordination with the SEC, remains relentless in its efforts to protect the Filipino people from financial predators. We urge the public to remain vigilant and always verify the legitimacy of investment offers before parting with their hard-earned money.” The NBI reiterates its warning to the public to exercise due diligence before engaging in investment opportunities and to verify with the SEC the legitimacy of companies offering financial and investment services. #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI FILES CHARGES AGAINST CIVIL REGISTRY OFFICIALS OVER FRAUDULENT BIRTH REGISTRATIONS INVOLVING FOREIGN NATIONALS PASAY CITY, Philippines – In a significant move to protect the integrity of the country’s civil registration system, the National Bureau of Investigation – Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO) has filed formal charges against several public officials and private individuals involved in a coordinated scheme to issue fraudulent birth certificates. The investigation, in close coordination with the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), focused on systemic irregularities within the Local Civil Registry Offices of Pikit and Aleosan, North Cotabato. Investigation revealed a sophisticated conspiracy involving local civil registrars, their staff, and a retired municipal civil registrar who acted as a private facilitator. These individuals allegedly bypassed legal protocols to process the late registration of Certificates of Live Birth (COLB) using falsified and fabricated supporting documents. Evidence gathered by the NBI-CEMRO indicates that foreign nationals, primarily of Chinese origin, were the primary beneficiaries of this scheme. By using fictitious identities, these individuals obtained Filipino civil status, effectively exploiting the system to gain Filipino citizenship under false pretenses. Evidence further uncovered that many of these birth records were “ready-made,” meaning they were processed and issued without undergoing the mandatory verification procedures. In exchange for facilitating these unlawful registrations, local registry personnel reportedly received monetary compensation and other illicit benefits. The scale of the issue was highlighted by the PSA, which flagged over 50,000 potentially fraudulent birth records across more than 1,600 registry offices nationwide. The municipalities of Pikit and Aleosan were specifically identified as high-risk areas, leading to the NBI’s intensive and successful operation in the region. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 29, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On July 13, 2025, NBI-Cavite District Office (NBI-CAVIDO) and Bureau of Immigration (BI) arrested WANG XIUJUN, a Chinese national, upon her arrival at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) from Guangdong, China for misrepresenting herself as a Filipino citizen. The case stemmed from an intelligence report received by NBI-CAVIDO that WANG is using a Filipino name CASSIA PALMA POLIQUIT in some of her business transactions. Investigation conducted by agents of NBI-CAVIDO revealed that WANG was able to secure a Philippine passport under the said Filipino name as per certification issued by the Office of Consular Affairs of the Department of Foreign Affairs and a Certificate of Live Birth via late registration. Also, based on the documents secured from the Securities and Exchange Commission, she established several companies where she represented herself as a Filipino. All these, despite the fact that she is a Chinese national with a Special Investor’s Resident Visa (SIRV) as per verification with the Bureau of Investment. In addition, Chief of NBI Dactyloscopy Division, was requested to conduct comparative examinations and analysis of POLIQUIT’s fingerprint in her NBI Clearance and DFA Passport Application with that of WANG in her NBI Clearance and BOI’s SIRV Application Form. As a result, the Dactyloscopy Report dated March 26, 2025, and July 7, 2025, stated that the questioned fingerprint of POLIQUIT and the standard fingerprint of WANG were found identical. Hence, POLIQUIT, CASSIA PALMA, and WANG XIUJUN are one and the same person. Accordingly, WANG was charged by the BI with violation of the Immigration Law, specifically Misrepresentation as a Filipino, Violating the Limitations and Conditions of Stay, and Undesirability. Thereafter, on July 28, 2025, NBI-CAVIDO filed a case of violations of Article 172, in relation to Article 171, paragraph 4, and Article 178 of the Revised Penal Code, and Section 19 (b)(1) and (c)(1) of Republic Act 8239, the “Philippine Passport Act of 1996”, against WANG before the Prosecutor’s Office of Taguig City. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CAVIDO for this operation, and highlighted the significance of effective collaboration with counterpart government agencies. Director Santiago assures that the NBI will delve deeper into what may be another “Alice Guo” story.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the government against environmental crimes, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crimes Division (NBI-EnCD) recently arrested nine (9) individuals in Ternate, Cavite for illegal mining. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as NARCISO PEJI y DIONIDO, MARY JANE MAALA y ILAGAN, RYAN NAPARAM y ROCERO, ALVIN AQUINO y CORNEJO, JOSE REMY COPONES y LOVITE, EMMANUEL MANAO y SACE, ROBERT DELOS SANTOS y AQUINO, JOEBERT AGUISANDA y ANBANO, and ROGER BETONIO y SALAZAR. body: PRESS STATEMENT October 07, 2022 NBI ARRESTS SEVEN (7) FOR THEFT OF MINERALS The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of seven (7) individuals by the Agents of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (EnCD) in Tarlac City for Theft of Minerals. The NBI-EnCD conducted a series of surveillance operations on September 2 and 19, 2022, confirming the existence of a quarry operation located at Barangay Sta. Maria, Tarlac City. Verification with the Local Government Unit and DENR-MGB Region III disclosed that no quarry permits were issued within the area indicated. On October 3, 2022, environmental law enforcement was conducted with the assistance of the DENR-MGB Region III. The operation resulted in the arrest of Barangay Captain Albert Mercado who was in charge of the illegal quarry operation, and Barangay Councilor Arturo Dela Cruz who served as the checker/collector. Their helpers who were also sighted within the premises of the quarry operation are as follows, namely: Joel Santos; Jesus Santos; Jessie Santos; Jonathan Santos and Jerry Espinosa. Arrested Subjects were caught in flagrante de licto conducting a quarry operation without the necessary documents from any of the concerned government agencies. One (1) payloader and four (4) trucks with a total value of Php 1,800,000.00 were seized and turned over to the appropriate office. Delivery receipts among the documents seized from the subjects showed that the aggregates were being delivered to the provinces of Cavite, Batangas, Gapan, Pampanga, among others. After eliciting information, it was found that the proceeds of the quarry operation are being shared by Brgy. Captain Mercado and the Provincial Government of Tarlac at 60:40 ratio. Further investigation revealed that Royal Crown Monarch Inc., an entity contracted by the DPWH for the construction of government projects in Tarlac City, has been sourcing earth materials from the said illegal quarry operation to complete its contracts. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceeding on October 4, 2022, at the Tarlac City Prosecutor’s Office for violation of Section 103 (Theft of Minerals) of RA 7942 otherwise known as the “Philippine Mining Act of 1995.”

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 13, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is proud to announce the signing of a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), the agency mandated for maritime search and rescue, maritime law enforcement, maritime safety, marine environmental protection, and maritime security. The MOA signing aims to enhance cooperation and coordination between NBI and PCG to improve their capabilities in law enforcement. The agreement signifies the agencies’ commitment to strengthen enforcement efforts in maritime areas including the detection, investigation, and prosecution of maritime-related crimes and offenses, as well as enhance the efficiency of both agencies in suppressing crimes committed within the Philippines jurisdiction, both land and maritime. Among the initiatives in the MOA include extending collaborative partnerships with local sectors, organizations, and other government agencies for more resolute maritime and coastal monitoring, and ensuring effective and efficient implementation of RA 9993, Executive Order No. 94, and RA 10867. The signing ceremony took place at NBI Conference Room, V-Tech Tower on June 13, 2024, with key representatives from both organizations present. The NBI was represented by Director Medardo G. de Lemos with the Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors, while PCG was represented by CG Admiral Ronnie Gil L. Gavan together with the high-ranking officials of PCG.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 10, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI Dismantles Counterfeit Footwear Operation in Pasay City; Over PHP 15.6M in Goods Seized PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBO-IPRD), successfully executed a series of enforcement operations in Pasay City on March 5, 2026, dealing a major blow to the local trade of illicit goods. Acting on evidence that several commercial establishments were engaged in the unauthorized storage, distribution, and sale of counterfeit merchandise, NBI agents served multiple search warrants targeting the illegal activity. The operation was launched to enforce compliance with Republic Act No. 8293, also known as the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. The seizure on the target locations resulted in a significant haul of illicit footwear, totaling 13,058 pairs of various sizes and designs. All seized items bore the counterfeit trademark of the popular brand “HAVAIANAS,” representing a major blow to the distribution of trademark-infringing goods in the area. The estimated total value of the confiscated merchandise is placed at PHP 15,669,600.00. The NBI remains committed to protecting the rights of legitimate brand owners and ensuring the safety of Filipino consumers. Legal proceedings are currently being prepared against the owners of the establishments involved in the distribution of these illegal goods. #NBIServes

body: A couple who kept custody of a girl after her disappearance a month ago, and demanded payment for her alleged debts were arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives during and entrapment last week. NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas identified the suspects as: Spouses EVELYN, 42, and ORLANDO MARINDUQUE, 48, tricycle driver, and both residents of Puelay, Caranglaan, Dagupan City. Investigation by the Dagupan District Office (DADO) headed by Head Agent Pedro C. Roque Jr., disclosed that a certain Vilma R. Ballesteros sought investigative assistance regarding the disappearance of her daughter, Mevil, since May, this year. The complainant Ballesteros traced her daughter’s whereabouts to the residence of the suspects at Bgy. Caranglaan in Dagupan City. Upon confrontation, spouses Marinduque refused to return her daughter claiming that Mevil has an outstanding debt to them. Through Ballesteros’s insistence, the Marinduques gave way but demanded P30,000 for payment of board and lodging. They even threatened that she would not see her daughter anymore if she failed in their demand. This prompted Ballesteros to seek NBI assistance last week. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment was planned. The suspects and complainant, set a meeting for the payment at the De Luxe Restaurant in Dagupan City on June 26, 2013 after a negotiation. On the appointed date, time and place, Ballesteros went to restaurant and so did the Marinduque couple. Complainant was discreetly accompanied by NBI agents who posted themselves within the meeting place. Expectedly, the meeting took place during which the Marinduque couple received the marked money from Ballesteros. Moments thereafter, after receiving the marked money, NBI agents approached, introduced themselves and apprehended spouses Marinduque. They were brought to the NBI Dagupan office for booking and detention. Subsequently, charges for Robbery/Extortion and Grave Threats were filed against the suspects before the Dagupan City Prosecutor’s Office.

body: With a long and colorful history as the country’s premier investigative agency, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) celebrated its 75th diamond anniversary in fitting ceremonies at its main office in Manila today. President Benigno S. Aquino III was the guest-of-honor and speaker. He was welcomed by NBI Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula and Justice Secretary Leila M. De Lima. The program was held at 10:00 AM at the NBI gym. Director Gatdula delivered the opening remarks followed by the presentation of awards to 23 NBI personnel. Justice Secretary De Lima introduced the President. This year’s celebration is a milestone, after over 75 years of meaningful public service under 17 directors. As any organization, it confronted countless challenges which put to test the capability of its men and women as professional investigators and experts in support services. Its strength has been shown in many trying circumstances and it takes pride that after over seven decades it has surmounted them all. Today, under the leadership of Director Magtanggol B. Gatdula and with the support of the Aquino administration, it pursues a vision of a law enforcement institution that is globally recognized and capable in fighting criminal and lawless elements. This year’s theme is – “NBI: Ang Inyong Kaagapay sa Tuwid na Daan.”

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) arrested an individual in Iloilo City on February 8, 2018 for Rape and Child Abuse. Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subject as ROLLY CARDINES y MANA-AY, 48 years old, married and a resident of Sta. Barbara, Iloilo. body: A man who employed his website in the sale of a firearm was arrested by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) during a buy-bust operation the other day in Makati City. The subject was identified as VICTOR OLIVER AQUINO Y LEONIO, 41, a resident of Parañaque City. On September 24, 2012, the NBI received an intelligence report on the alleged illegal operation being conducted through on-line gun selling by a certain “monkeynfish.” It turned out to be suspect Aquino who was the seller. Accordingly, he is also posting in various websites in the internet this activity of selling firearm even those unlicensed to him. He does not have any pertinent documents authorizing him to engage in said trade. Eventually, an NBI poseur-buyer was able to contact him for a transacted sale as posted in his website. This led to a buy-bust operation. In the afternoon of October 3, 2012, a buy-bust operation was conducted at the Makati Cinema Square in Pasong Tamo, Makati City. Aquino and a poseur-buyer met. The former offered to sell a high powered HK MP5 submachine gun which he brought and showed to the latter. However, he failed to present the corresponding license and documents for the said firearm. Moments thereafter, at a pre-arranges signal, NBI agents strategically posted in the vicinity rushed to him. Introducing themselves as NBI men, Aquino was immediately arrested. He was brought to the NBI where he was booked. Subsequently, Aquino was brought before the Makati City Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceeding for violation of PD 1866 as amended by RA 8294 Section 1.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 11, 2024 To intensify its campaign to deter the proliferation of fake products, the National Bureau of Investigation-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO), under the supervision of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago, seized misbranded and tampered drug products amounting to Php 1.9M. The case stemmed from a complaint letter received by NBI-RIZDO from a law firm requesting for investigation and enforcement action against illicit traders operating in the National Capital Region (NCR) who are engaged in the Illegal Scale or Distribution of Misbranded / Tampered VICKS Products. Confirmation through surveillance and test-buy operations were conducted, resulting in the application for and issuance of a search warrant. Thus, on October 07, 2024, NBI-RIZDO operatives together with the officers from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) implemented the search warrant in Tondo, Manila. Seized and confiscated were numerous misbranded and tampered VICKS products, medicines (LOSARTAN and AMLODIPINE) marked as Property of the City Government of Pasay, as well other prohibited items incidental to a lawful search warrant implementation. Director Santiago concluded that the said items and the people responsible will be subjected for further investigation and verification.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all forms of criminality, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested four Chinese nationals and a Filipino in Pasay City for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran identified the Subjects as DONG DAHENG, LU LIHUI, ZHANG XIAOLIN, YE JINTAO, all Chinese nationals, and ANN MICHELLE DEL ROSARIO MELENDEZ (Filipino). On February 13, 2020, the complainant and live-in partner of the kidnapped victim, sought the help of the NBI in rescuing the victim who was allegedly being illegally detained by unidentified Chinese nationals. According to the complainant, her partner was kidnapped on February 11, 2020 in a hotel at Newport Manila, Pasay City. The victim was allowed by the kidnappers to make calls and ask for ransom money worth Php 400,000.00 to be deposited to a given bank account of a certain ANN MICHELLE MELENDEZ. The complainant hurried from Davao to Manila and upon arrival, she received a video call from the kidnap victim in handcuffs. With this, the complainant, together with the kidnap victim’s brother, decided to give the ransom money on February 13, 2020. They were instructed to deliver the ransom money in a casino-hotel in Pasay City. While at the counter of the hotel, complainant and the victim’s brother were approached by a Chinese national (later identified as Ye Jintao) and asked for the money and deposited the P400,000.00 in the account of another Chinese, Hu Xinhai. At around 10:00 in the evening of the same day, the kidnap victim was released near Villamor Airbase. In the evening of February 14, 2020, NBI-SAU operatives, together with the kidnap victim and his live-in partner, proceeded to the casino-hotel in Pasay City. After some time, the kidnap victim caught sight of the three (3) kidnappers, positively identified as DONG DAHENG, LU LIHUI, and ZHANG XIAOLIN. The operatives announced their authority and purpose to the 3 Chinese nationals. Out of nowhere, ANN MICHELLE MELENDEZ introduced herself to the SAU operatives as the girlfriend of Subject DONG DAHENG. The above-named Subjects were then arrested and brought to NBI for the booking procedures. The next day, Subject YE JINTAO was arrested in a hotel in Pasay City and was likewise brought to the NBI. Arrested Subjects were presented on February 16, 2020 for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention. They are currently detained at the NBI Detention Center. Subject HU XINHAI and four others, who are at large, were also charged with the same crime.

body: In line with the relentless campaign of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) against all illegal activities, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) have arrested five (5) individuals in Quezon City for illegal investment activities. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subjects as BERNIE LIMPIADA y REVADENERA a.k.a. BRIX, MARVIN OJEDA y JAUREZ, a.k.a. MARVIN JUAREZ OJEDA, GLORY ANN PILLORA y ID, ROGELIO LAVERINTO FAMBUENA JR., and SISON INOCENCIO y NICOLAS. Distor said the case stemmed from the report of a walk-in informant regarding an alleged investment scam perpetrated by AGRI-WEALTH FARM VENTURES INC. owned and operated by Subjects BERNIE LIMPIADA y REVADENERA and MARVIN OJEDA y JUAREZ. Informant and his associate, accompanied by the officials of Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA), reported to NBI-AFD the illegal investment activities of Subject LIMPIADA and his cohorts. According to the informant, AGRI-WEALTH is offering investment to the public with the promise of 160% return of investment within the period of 100 days. Subjects promised investors a daily profit ranging from 1.6% to 2.5% of the invested amount. For each direct referral or recruit that one brings to the company, he gets an additional 5% of the invested amount of his referral and additional 2% for the second level recruits and 1% for the succeeding levels of recruit until the 10th level. AGRI-WEALTH make this offers appear to be viable and believable by leading their investors to believe that the company owns a 20 hectares high yielding aqua farm of mud crabs and tiger prawns in Hagonoy, Bulacan where they tour their prospective investors. Acting on the said information, verification was made with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and it was revealed that AGRI-WEALTH is neither registered as corporation nor was it issued a secondary license as a Lending Company, Broker, or Dealer of Securities, Dealer in Government Securities, Investment Adviser of an Investment Company, Investment House and Transfer Agent. Moreover, AGRI-WEALTH has not filed nor has any pending application for a secondary license with SEC. With these, entrapment operations were hatched on July 21, 2021. Informant and Subject LIMPIADA arranged a meet up at a restaurant in a mall in Quezon City for the scheduled submission of the collected investment money. NBI-AFD strategically positioned themselves within the premises of the establishment. Thereat, informant was seen handing a brown envelope containing the marked money to a man later on identified as Subject BERNIE LIMPIADA who then passed the same to a woman companion identified as Subject GLORY ANN PILLORA, the System Administrator of AGRI-WEALTH. The latter then put the envelope inside her black backpack while the other male companion, identified as Subject SISON INOCENCIO, the Project Manager of AGRI-WEALTH, was vigilantly watching the surroundings. NBI-AFD immediately approached and introduced themselves and their authority. They informed the Subjects of their constitutional rights and placed them under arrest. Subsequently, an entrapment was also conducted at AGRI-WEALTH’s office in New Manila, Quezon City. Poseur-investors, along with the informant and his associate, proceeded to AGRI-WEALTH office. They were followed by SEC Investigator and Administrative Assistant while NBI-AFD operatives strategically positioned themselves within the premises. Poseur-investors were immediately catered in and attended to by Subject ROGELIO LAVERINTO FAMBUENA JR. who introduced himself as the General Manager of AGRI-WEALTH. The latter presented the comp-plan, marketing plan, scheme, and operations of the company. Midway of the presentation, Subject MARVIN JUAREZ OJEDA entered the office and supported FAMBUENA’s presentation. He represented himself as the Chairman/CEO of AGRI-WEALTH. After the presentation, poseur-investor handed the marked investment money to OJEDA. NBI-AFD operatives then approached the Subjects, announced their authority, informed them of their constitutional rights and placed Subjects under arrest. When asked to present their SEC registration papers, business permits, and other pertinent documents relating to the operation of their business, Subjects failed to present any. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Quezon City for violation of Sections 8 and 26 of RA 8799 otherwise known as The Securities Regulation Code.

body: An impostor who misrepresented himself as a notary public was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in an entrapment in Manila. The suspect is identified as: MANUEL GARCIA TANJUTCO, of 2543 Andrade St., Blumentritt, Sta. Cruz, Manila. Investigation by the NBI National Capital Region (NCR) headed by Regional Director Elfren L. Meneses Jr., disclosed that in July 2013, a certain Carl G. Fernandez went to the Professional Regulations Commission (PRC) for a personal purpose. On his way to the Commission, he noticed the office of one Atty. Deodegario A. Belarmino with whom he sought legal services of the same lawyer sometime earlier in his office in Blumentritt, Manila. Thereupon, he entered Atty. Belarmino’s office and informed him that he had a Contract of Lease notarized by a certain “Atty. Deodegario A. Belarmino” in 2543 Andrade St., Blumentritt, Sta. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: A seven year old boy who was abducted was rescued and his kidnappers arrested during an operation by National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) agents in a Manila mall recently. Subjects are identified as: RONEL SANTIAGO aka “BRYAN ANTOS”, a resident of Malabon City ; and RONA SABROSO GADOR, with address at San Jose Del Monte and Malolos, Bulacan. Investigation report of the NBI – National Capital Region office disclosed that on December 14, 2012, it received a complaint from the mother of the kidnapped victim informing that the day before, December 13, her son JC was kidnapped from the residence in Marilao, Bulacan. The kidnapper is allegedly a friend of the victim’s father who introduced himself as a certain Kuya Jason. He demanded P20,000.00 for the release of her son and a threat of possible harm or death. The victim’s mother relayed to the NBI of several exchange of cellphone messages between the mother and the subject. It was demanded that the ransom money be through money transfer via Cebuana Lhuillier. Subsequently, a rescue operation was planned, in which the money through wire transfer will be sent to the kidnapper with a tracking or claim number. Numerous informants were tasked to monitor several branches of Cebuana Lhuillier within Metro Manila to identify the person who would claim the wired transfer amount. The suspect also instructed that the amount be in the name of a certain Brian Santos as claimant. On the night of December 14, 2012, an informant called the NBI and said that he saw a boy resembling the kidnap-victim based on the photos given to informants. The boy was in the company of a man and a woman who entered the Cebuana Lluillier branch inside the Odeon Mall located at the corner of C.M. Recto and Rizal Avenue Sta. Cruz Manila. NBI operatives rushed to the place and they saw the duo in the company of a boy waiting for their turn to be serviced. Certain of the identity of the kidnap-victim, the operatives waited for Subjects to finish their transaction. After they received the money- transfer demanded, the pair hurriedly left the counter. At this point, NBI operatives approached, introduced themselves and arrested the subjects while the boy was rescued. Found in the possession of the subjects are: a postal ID in the name of Brian Santos, an electronically validated PERA PADALA claim receipt and Santos’s cellphone containing series of messages sent to and from the complainant. When asked of their true identities, they themselves as RONEL SANTIAGO and as RONA GADOR. The next day, the subjects were brought to the Manila Prosecutor’s Office and recommended for prosecution for Violation of Article 267 otherwise known as Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said its operatives have rescued three (3) persons who were recruited as drug mules at the NAIA Terminal in Pasay City yesterday. The NBI Anti-Illegal Drugs Unit (NBI-AIDU), in a Post Operation Report dated June 18, 2015, said the 3 rescued persons identified as CESAR APOLINAR, CLAIRE BAUTISTA, and ROSALIE FERNANDO who were recruited as drug couriers were being brought to Hong Kong before being sent to Brazil to smuggle cocaine back into Hong Kong. The AIDU said the drug mules were accompanied to the airport by a certain MICHAEL VINCO who was to ensure that they will all aboard the flight to Hong Kong where they will be delivered to a certain IRENE DULDULAO ALLAM. The NBI-AIDU said its operatives coordinated with the NAIA Inter-Agency Drug Interdiction Task Group (NAIA-IAITG) for an inter-agency operation that resulted in the rescue of the 3 drug mules. All 3 victims confirmed their recruitment as drug couriers and are executing statements against their illegal recruiters RENALYN BACTOL and JEWME DOLOR who were working together with VINCO and ALLAM. Charges for Large-Scale Illegal Recruitment and Syndicated Illegal Recruitment are being prepared against the above-mentioned Subjects. The NBI-AIDU stressed that the NAIA-IAITG of which the NBI-AIDU, Bureau of Immigration, Bureau of Customs, PNP-AIDSOTF and PDEA are members, demonstrated in this operation that an inter-agency Task Force greatly enhances coordination and effectiveness of counter-drug operations.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 10, 2024 In line with the instruction of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against child abuse, the NBI – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) arrested an individual in Quezon City for sexually assaulting his own son. Director Santiago said that on December 3, 2024, the Complainant together with her son filed a formal complaint against her husband for alleged rape committed against her five (5) year old son. According to the wife of the Subject, there is a pending case against her husband for alleged rape by sexual assault committed against their son who was then only three (3) years of age. Also, Complainant disclosed that she filed a marital rape case against the Subject and is being heard on the same court. During the course of the proceedings, the Subject continuously courted his wife and eventually regained her trust and reconciled with each other sometime in October 2024 in an effort to rebuild their family. However, when the Complainant returned from her four (4) day vacation, while bathing her son, the child complained of a sharp pain in his rectum. The Complainant brought her son to the hospital for examination, which revealed that the wound was not caused by a simple constipation and was advised to proceed with a medico legal examination. Thus, the Complainant appeared before the NBI-OTCD and filed a complaint against her husband and the victim’s own father. Medico-genital examination conducted on the Victim revealed that external injury is present on his ano-genital area. Based on the result of the medico-genital examination and personal knowledge of facts and circumstances, the operatives of NBI-OTCD conducted a hot-pursuit operation on December 4, 2024. The operatives together with the Complainant proceeded to the current whereabouts of the Subject in Brgy. Paltok, Quezon City, which resulted in the Subject’s apprehension. The arrested Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for the crime of Rape as defined and penalized under the Revised Penal Code (RPC) as amended and violation of R.A. No. 7610. Director Santiago commended the operatives of NBI-OTCD for their immediate action resulting in the arrest of the Subject. The Director encouraged the public to report to the NBI any kind of criminality and assured that the NBI is steadfast committed in their mandate in enforcing the laws of the country.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 01, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Following the issuance of a Warrant of Arrest stemming from a joint investigation Department of Justice (DOJ), National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), and Philippine National Police (PNP), two (2) of the accused in the murder of Atty. Wesley Barayuga voluntarily surrendered to the NBI-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) on September 29, 2025. On July 30, 2020, Atty. Wesley Barayuga, then PCSO Board Secretary and a retired police officer and his driver were shot by motorcycle-riding gunmen while traversing the intersection of Calbayog and Malinaw Streets in Mandaluyong City. Barayuga died at the scene, while his driver was rushed to Victor R. Potenciano (VRP) Medical Center in EDSA after sustaining gunshot injuries. To shed light on the assassination of Atty. Barayuga, a DOJ-NBI composite team was established as ordered by DOJ Secretary JESUS CRISPIN REMULLA. The team coordinated with the Philippine National Police – Crime Investigation and Detection Group (PNP-CIDG) to conduct a joint investigation aimed at appropriately filing charges against the perpetrators behind the Barayuga Murder Case. During a Quad Committee hearing in the House of Representatives on September 27, 2024, Police Lieutenant Colonel Santie F. Mendoza and his informant, former police officer Nelson E. Mariano, confessed their involvement in the incident. They implicated two (2) former high-ranking officials of the PNP: PCSO General Manager ROYINA MARZAN GARMA, and National Police Commission (NAPOLCOM) Chairman EDILBERTO DELA CRUZ LEONARDO as the masterminds behind Barayuga’s assassination. The testimonies of Mendoza and Mariano during the Quad Committee hearing corroborated the findings of the joint investigation by the NBI-OTCD and PNP-CIDG. Consequently, the team recommended that ROYINA MARZAN GARMA, EDILBERTO DELA CRUZ LEONARDO, JEREMY ZAPATA CAUSAPIN (a.k.a. TOKS), SANTIE FUENTES MENDOZA, and NELSON ENRIQUEZ MARIANO be charged for Murder and Frustrated Murder. Subsequently, the Regional Trial Court, Branch 279 of Mandaluyong City, issued a Warrant of Arrest against the above-named individuals. After learning that a Warrant of Arrest has been issued, Mariano and Mendoza expressed their intention to surrender to the NBI. On September 29, 2025, Subject Mariano voluntarily surrendered to the NBI-OTCD in Manila. On September 30, 2025, the agents of NBI-OTCD flew to Bacolod City to implement the Warrant of Arrest issued against Subject Mendoza, who also voluntarily surrendered. NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) commended the agents of NBI-OTCD and thanked the PNP-CIDG for their successful investigation leading to the surrender of Mariano and Mendoza. He emphasized the importance of collaboration among law enforcement agencies in criminal investigations.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 19, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Technical Intelligence Division (TID), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual who was introducing himself as an NBI Agent. On May 8, 2025, a complaint was lodged before the NBI-TID against TRIX M. BETONIO as he was claiming to be an NBI Agent and is authorized to recruit NBI Agents in exchange for monetary consideration. Verification with the NBI-Human Resource Management Division (HRMD) disclosed that TRIX M. BETONIO is not bona fide NBI personnel/employee and that the purported documents that he presented to complainant for signing are fake. When BETONIO contacted the complainant again on May 12, 2025 for signing of additional documents and requested for payment of another Php 2,500.00, TID operatives hatched an entrapment operation. On May 14, 2025, the agreed date of complainant and BETONIO to meet, TID operatives proceeded to a coffee shop inside a mall in the City of Manila and strategically positioned themselves. After Subject handed over the documents and received the marked money, TID operatives effected the arrest. BETONIO was brought to the NBI Headquarters in Pasay City for booking and processing. He was subjected to ultraviolet Examination for fluorescent dust particles, which yielded positive results. On May 15, 2025, TRIX M. BETONIO was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, City of Manila, for Use of Falsified Documents, Usurpation of Authority or Official Functions, Illegal Use of Uniforms or Insignia, and Swindling/Estafa.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 14, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In January 2025, the National Bureau of Investigation-Dangerous Drugs Division (NBI-DDD) received an information that at least two (2) Filipino women were being recruited by the African Drug Trafficking Syndicate (ADTS) to pick-up a package, suspected to contain illegal drugs, from Malaysia and transport it to Hong Kong. The information came after a series of controlled delivery operations and arrests conducted by the NBI in the previous months. The NBI-DDD immediately conducted an investigation, uncovering that the African Drug Trafficking Syndicate specifically targeted Filipinos in financial distress and those fluent in English. The syndicate lured them with promises of an all-expenses-paid trip to Malaysia and Hong Kong, offering an additional USD 5,000 each for agreeing to transport packages from Malaysia to Hong Kong. The recruits were reassured that the packages merely contained Malaysian products ordered by Hong Kong businessmen, convincing them there was no reason for concern. Upon verification of the information and confirming the identities of the two Filipinos recruited by the syndicate, NBI Director, Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), dispatched a team from the NBI-DDD to Malaysia. With the assistance of the Philippine Embassy in Malaysia, the NBI-DDD coordinated with the Royal Malaysian Police (RMP), Narcotics Crime Investigation Division (NCID).
