body: PRESS STATEMENT June 18, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Following an inter-agency operation, the National Bureau of Investigation – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), under the leadership of Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two (2) individuals on June 12, 2025 for alleged involvement in illegal recruitment and human trafficking activities at NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City. The suspects were identified as KAYE ALFARO and DAHLIA MENDEZ BATILLER, both of whom are facing charges for violation of Section 6 of Republic Act 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995, as amended by RA 10022) and Section 4 of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by RA 11862). The case stemmed from the endorsement by the Bureau of Immigration – IPROBES to the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking – Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT-IACAT) of two (2) departing female passengers who were intercepted at NAIA Terminal 1, Pasay City. NAIATFAT-IACAT then endorsed the case to NBI-IAID for investigation. The said 2 passengers presented themselves at the Immigration Counter as tourists bound for Thailand. Upon investigation, one of the passengers, alias “Maria”, disclosed that she had been promised a job as a Customer Service Representative (CSR) in Thailand and was also offered work as a nude model in Cambodia, with payment offers of P60,000 and USD 5,000, respectively. These offers were made by the co-passenger, Kaye Alfaro, who also supplied her with falsified travel documents and facilitated her attempted departure. Alias Maria revealed she had been asked by Kaye to pay an alleged “escort” service at the Bureau of Immigration in the amount of P70,000, which she believed would guarantee her passage through immigration screening. However, the Bureau of Immigration offloaded both departing passengers after inconsistencies in their travel narratives were uncovered. Further investigation conducted by NBI-IAID revealed a network of individuals involved in the operation, including Ian, Jemar Pajarito, and a certain Hanna, all believed to be part of the fraudulent facilitation scheme. A third party, Dahlia Mendez Batiller, visited the NBI office shortly after the arrest of Kaye, allegedly under the instruction of “Hanna” to intervene in the investigation. There is a pattern of coordination with the aforementioned individuals in facilitating illegal recruitment and trafficking activities. Moreover, a certification issued by Atty. Liza C. Alcera, OIC-Director IV of the Licensing and Regulations Bureau of the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW), confirmed that neither Kaye Alfaro nor Dahlia Batiller is licensed or authorized to recruit Filipino workers for overseas employment. As a result, both Kaye Alfaro and Dahlia Batiller were placed under arrest by the Agents of NBI-IAID, apprised of their constitutional rights, and processed according to standard procedure. Victim Alias “Maria” was also processed by the DSWD Social Worker. The Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking reiterates its commitment, in coordination with partner-agencies to combat human trafficking and illegal recruitment schemes targeting vulnerable Filipinos. Authorities remind the public to verify recruitment offers and report suspicious activities through the proper government channels.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against Trafficking in Persons of minors, the NBI- Olongapo District Office (NBI-OLDO) arrested a certain “MARGIE” in San Antonio, Zambales for violation of Republic Act 9208, as amended by Republic Act 10364 and Republic Act 11862 otherwise known as the “Expanded Trafficking in Persons Act of 2022”. The operation stemmed from an information received by NBI-OLDO that the Subject is engaged in sexual trafficking involving female victims, some of whom are minors. The Subject offers female victims including minors for sexual exploitation in exchange for a fee of Php 2,000.00. The trafficking operations were reportedly being conducted within an establishment named as “Pussycat Bar in Brgy. East Dirita, San Antonio, Zambales. Surveillance operations validated the information, hence, the preparation for the entrapment and rescue operation. NBI-OLDO coordinated with the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor Province of Zambales (OPP-Zambales) and the San Antonio Municipal Police. Thus, on May 14, 2025, NBI-OLDO Agents with social workers from DSWD Field Office 3-Central Luzon and a doctor of the NBI Odontology Division proceeded to the location. The operation resulted in the arrest of subject “MARGIE”, who was later identified as EDITH EJERCITO y DUMALTE caught in flagrante delicto of receiving the marked money in the amount of Php 4,000.00 as payment for the sexual services of the two (2) trafficked victims. The entrapment operation also resulted to the rescue of eight (8) victims, including three (3) minors. The arrested Subject was presented for Inquest Proceedings for violation of the aforementioned law before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor Zambales (OPP-Zambales) on May 16, 2025. On the same day, the Inquest Resolution was released by the OPP-Zambales, filing the said charges with the Regional Trial Court-Third Judicial Region at Iba, Zambales. Subject was placed in confinement to the Zambales Provincial Jail upon the order of the RTC-Zambales Executive Judge. The five victims were turned over by the DSWD social workers to the Municipal Social Welfare Development (MSWD) of San Antonio Zambales before being released to their families, while the three minor victims were endorsed to a DSWD partner non-government association (NGO) for temporary residential care.

body: PRESS STATEMENT December 08, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) joins the Chief Executive in his call for government agencies to scale down their Christmas celebrations, in solidarity with our fellow Filipinos who have suffered from the wrath of the six typhoons that hit the country recently. In just one (1) month, the Philippines was pummeled by six (6) successive typhoons which caused severe damage not only to the properties but also to the lives of those who were living in the affected areas. Thousands of families affected by the typhoons flee and take refuge in evacuation centers for their safety. Director Santiago said that the original plan was for the NBI to hold its Christmas party at the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC) in Pasay City. However, moved by the same noble call by Malacanang Palace, Director Santiago directed that the NBI foregoes with the said plan and instead send help to typhoon victims. Specifically, the NBI is in the process of procuring relief goods and food packs for the intended beneficiaries. In lieu of the PICC, the NBI will hold a simple Christmas party in its new office at Filinvest Cyberzone, Pasay City. Director Santiago highlighted that aside from the food packs, the NBI also offers prayers for the typhoon victims. Nothing beats the bayanihan spirit of the Filipino people, especially in this season of giving.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 21, 2024 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested three individuals on June 19, 2024, for hacking private and government websites, banks, and Facebook accounts. The case stemmed from numerous information regarding recent incidents involving multiple unauthorized access attempts and breaches of private and government websites. To gather information crucial to identifying and apprehending the Subjects, NBI-CCD tracked the movements of the identified hacker known by aliases such as ‘kangkong’, ‘Mirasol’, ‘Sibat’, ‘Ricardo Redoble’, and ‘lulu’. Operatives likewise monitored online activities and gathered data from various sources like social media, forums, and public databases to establish patterns and connections linked to the hacker’s activities. On June 14, 2024, an initial contact with the Subjects was made through the informant. Subjects agreed to meet and told the informant that he has a project and that he would include him on it, and the particulars will be discussed upon their meeting. Further, on June 17, 2024, Subject Kangkong sent a compressed file containing BELO’s database. Subsequently, on June 19, 2024, Subject sent hacked Facebook accounts which include email addresses and passwords. This implied that Subjects had successfully accessed BELO’s database. In the afternoon of the same day, a meet up with the Subjects was set in a hotel in Manila. @ After announcing their authority and the reason for the arrest, CCD operatives conducted a hot pursuit which resulted in the arrest of Subjects alias Kangkong and Illusion. Controlled viewing of the phone seized from one of the Subjects showed contained scripts and databases obtained from LGU and various government websites, as well as Facebook users’ credentials. Moreover, Subject Illusion’s phone contained data related to hacked banks including Philippine National Bank, Security Bank, Banco de Oro, and Union Bank. These highlight the extent of the digital assets and sensitive information accessed by the Subjects, pointing to potential cybersecurity breaches and illegal activities. Subjects were thereafter brought to NBI-CCD Office in Quezon City for the standard operating procedures. They were recommended to be charged with Illegal Access under Section 4(a)(1) and Misuse of Device under Section 5(iii) of RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, as well as Unauthorized Access or Intentional Breach under Section 29 of RA 10173 otherwise known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012. The third subject with an alias ‘Allan 10k’ will be charged thru direct filing. All Subjects are members of two big hacking groups, namely: Philippine Lulzec and Globalsec.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 15, 2025 .jusatified-text { text-align: justify; } National Bureau of Investigation-Bayombong District Office (NBI-BAYDO), under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), has filed criminal charges against PMaj. SANTY C. VENTURA, PMsg. ODRA NOEL R. AFALLA, PCpl JEFF LLOYD N. APANGCHAN, PCpl RANDY T. AGDEPPA, Pat. JOHN MICHAEL C. TANGUILAN, and Police Officer FREDERICK MARIANO for the alleged planting of evidence. The case stems from the acquittal of Freddie Mallari, who was the subject of fabricated evidence at a crime scene. Evidence gathered by the NBI, along with findings of the Regional Trial Court (RTC), Branch 37, revealed that the firearms seized during a search warrant operation on May 25, 2024, were fabricated. The court described one item as nothing more than a “metal scrap”. The court’s judgment, dated April 28, 2025, not only cleared Mallari of all charges but also condemned the officers’ conduct as a clear violation of his constitutional rights. Based on these findings and the NBI’s independent investigation, charges were filed on July 29, 2025, with the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor of Nueva Vizcaya. The charges are for violation of Section 38 of Republic Act No. 10591 (Planting of Evidence), alongside provisions of the Revised Penal Code and other special laws addressing abuse of authority and obstruction of justice. Director Santiago commended the NBI-BAYDO for solving the case. He added that the abuse of authority by wrongly incriminating a person through fabrication of false evidence has no place in the law enforcement.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 14, 2022 National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) DIRECTOR ERIC B. DISTOR has commended NBI Supervising Agent (SA) MINERVA A. SOBREVIGA-RETANAL for being the first Philippine Law Enforcement Expert and the only female law enforcement officer in South East Asia as a Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Assessor – Law Enforcement Expert for Money Laundering and Terrorism Financing. In simple ceremonies during the Directorial Staff meeting at NBI Headquarters in Quezon City, Director DISTOR cited Atty. Retanal, Executive Officer of the NBI-Anti Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) for her remarkable career and achievements as an Agent of the NBI. DISTOR said that only experts who have successfully completed the training organized by FATF and Asia Pacific Group (APG) on Money Laundering and at the same time a member of APG can be a FATF Assessor to ensure the consistently high quality of its mutual evaluations. This training teaches the FATF assessors how to critically analyze a country’s technical compliance with the FATF recommendations and how to assess whether the country’s Anti-Money Laundering /Combating the Financing on Terrorism (AML/CFT) measures are effective. “Your diligence and determination to acquire expertise in this field of investigation is worthy of recognition and emulation. Your achievement would indeed contribute to the continuance of the Bureau being the premier investigative in the country”, DISTOR emphasized. Supervising Agent Retanal has participated and represented the NBI during the Mutual Evaluation (ME) of the Philippines in 2008 and 2018. During the 2018 ME, the APG Secretariat has noticed her capabilities to become FATF Assessor. Upon the recommendation of the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC), the APG approved her nomination and undergone the Assessor Training in August 2018 in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia conducted jointly by APG and EAG. Thus, becoming the first Philippine Law Enforcement expert and the only female law enforcement officer in South East Asia trained as FATF Assessor.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in a buy-bust operation in Amadeo, Cavite for unlawful possession and selling of different wood species without necessary permits. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as NINO PAULO MANALO y AYOCOCHO, owner of NP Manalo Woodworks, who is engaged in selling different kinds of wood species. OIC Distor said that an intelligence report received by the NBI- Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) revealed that a certain individual in Brgy. Pangi, Amadeo, Cavite is allegedly in possession of undetermined quantity of lumber and flitches of different wood species which includes Akle, Narra, Acacia, and other fruit bearing trees. Distor added that surveillance operation conducted by NBI-EnCD revealed that NP Manalo Woodworks has in its possession lumbers and flitches of different wood species including furniture displayed in the furniture shop of the establishment. Verification from PENRO Cavite revealed that Subject Manalo of NP Manalo Woodworks does not have the necessary permits such as Lumber Dealer Permit, Cutting Permit, Transport Permit, Wood Importation Permit, Wood Processing Permit, Monitoring Compliance Certificate, and Chainsaw Registration. Cyber-surveillance in Facebook likewise shows that Subject Manalo is a seller of lumber, wood products, and furniture at Facebook Marketplace. Based on the evidence gathered that established Subject Manalo as indeed engaged in unlawful possession and selling of different kinds of wood species, NBI-EnCD applied for and was granted a Search Warrant by RTC Branch 20 of Imus Cavite. On June 18, 2020, NBI-EnCD operatives and DENR PENRO served the Search Warrant against the establishment of Subject Manalo. During the operation, numerous wood species with an estimated value of Php 3,499,183.91 and furniture with an estimated value of Php 323,000.00 were found in the area and seized. After subject Manalo failed to produce necessary permits, he was placed under arrest for unlawful possession and selling of different kinds of wood species. Subject Manalo was presented for inquest proceeding before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor in Imus, Cavite for violation of Section 77 (formerly Section 68) of P.D. 705, as amended by E.O. 277, otherwise known as the “Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines”.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI, Royal Norwegian Embassy Strengthen Cooperation Against Human Trafficking and Online Child Exploitation MANILA, Philippines, June 04, 2026 — National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag met with officials from the Royal Norwegian Embassy and the Nordic Police Liaison Office to strengthen cooperation in combating human trafficking and online sexual abuse offenses. The meeting aligned with the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. to intensify the government’s fight against human trafficking, Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC), and other crimes that harm women, children, and vulnerable communities. The meeting, attended by Ambassador Christian Halaas Lyster, Nordic Liaison Officer Nicolai Langaas, and Julian Jara, focused on closer collaboration to investigate and prevent human trafficking and OSAEC. Discussions centered on enhancing cooperation through the sharing of information on the financial transactions of perpetrators, coordinating cases, building capacity, and fostering cross-border cooperation to identify offenders and dismantle criminal networks. The parties recognized that tracking money flows and financial activities linked to traffickers and online exploiters is a critical component of any effective investigative strategy. Atty. Matibag emphasized that human trafficking and online child exploitation are transnational crimes that require strong cooperation among local and international law enforcement partners. Director Matibag said the NBI will continue to pursue offenders, support victim-survivors, and work with foreign counterparts to ensure that those who prey on the vulnerable are held accountable. For their part, the Royal Norwegian Embassy and the Nordic Police Liaison Office expressed continued support for the NBI’s efforts, particularly in strengthening investigative cooperation, intelligence exchange, and operational coordination — including the tracing of financial transactions — against trafficking and online exploitation. Their partnership with the Bureau reflects a shared commitment to protect children and vulnerable persons from abuse, exploitation, and organized crime. The engagement forms part of the NBI’s continuing efforts under Atty. Matibag’s leadership in building stronger international law enforcement partnerships and contributing to the whole-of-government campaign against human trafficking, OSAEC, and other transnational crimes. The key changes are in the fourth and seventh paragraphs, where financial transaction sharing is now explicitly named as a distinct pillar of cooperation rather than a passing reference.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said Agents of the Bureau’s Anti-Human Trafficking Division (AHTRAD) have rescued the 8-month old girl (baby Sophia) in Laguna who was sold by her mother for Forty Five Thousand Pesos (P45,000.00) to a buyer whom she met online. The operation also resulted in the arrest of two individuals who were with the baby on board a vehicle in Sta. Cruz, Laguna. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor commended the Agents of NBI-AHTRAD for their swift action in responding to the appeal of the parents who sought the assistance of the NBI in locating their baby. Based on the initial information received, the mother met the buyer through a Facebook (FB) group named “Bahay Ampunan”, after which they communicated via FB messenger. Their exchange and meet up transpired in the evening of March 3, 2022 in a restaurant in Quezon City. However, after delivering the baby, the mother changed her mind and realized that it was illegal to sell her child. She decided to recover her baby but the buyer immediately blocked her on FB. On March 22, 2022, an information was received by AHTRAD that baby Sophia was in the custody of IMELDA MABILIRAN y PANOPIO and her Nigerian national live-in partner, MAXWELL IFEANYI BRIGHT OKORO. Under strict orders of OIC-Director Distor, AHTRAD operatives immediately conducted investigation and found out that Subjects Imelda and Maxwell were in Pansol, Laguna on board a Black Ford Escape driven by Maxwell. With that information, NBI operatives proceeded to Laguna. When the SUV was sighted moving, they tailed the car until it stopped over a sidewalk market in Sta. Cruz, Laguna. As soon as Agents were able to see baby Sophia inside the car with Maxwell, Agents immediately apprehended both Subjects and were brought to NBI Quezon City for booking procedures. Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings before the Department of Justice for Violation of Sec. 7 of R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act) in relation to R.A. 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012; Violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A.10364 in relation to Sec 6 par (a) Qualified Trafficking; and Kidnapping and Serious Illegal Detention under Article 267 of the Revised Penal Code.

body: In line with the government’s drive against individuals taking advantage of the situation over the COVID-19 outbreak, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of two (2) Chinese nationals and one (1) Filipinio by operatives of NBI- International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) on March 25, 2020, in Pasay City for selling overpriced medical supplies. NBI Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested subjects as YANFEI MO and HENRY TAN, both Chinese nationals with RUTH DIANA R. CARDONA. The operation was based from the information that a group of Chinese nationals are into selling overpriced medical supplies. NBI-IOD was able to build communication with the subjects and ordered Ten Thousand (10,000) boxes of surgical masks worth Php 17 Million. Thus, on March 25, 2020, NBI-IOD operatives proceeded to the meeting area in Pasay City which resulted in the arrest of the subjects. The operation also resulted in the seizure of 4,000 boxes or 200,000 pieces of surgical masks worth Php 6.8 Million. Subjects were presented for inquest proceeding before the Pasay City Prosecutor’s Office for violations of Section 6 and 7 of R.A. 7581, otherwise known as the “Price Act” in relation to Department of Health Circular No. 2020-0142, Public Advisory No. 18, Section 5(2) of R.A. 7581 as amended by R.A. 10623 in relation to Department of Trade and Industry Memorandum Circular No. 20-07, and Section 52(b) of R.A. 7394, otherwise known as “The Consumer Act.” In addition to the arrested subjects, Alias Liza and Alias Marrieta were also recommended for prosecution.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 28, 2022 NBI ARRESTS TWO FOR SELLING FAKE TITLES In line with the government’s drive against all crimes of fraud, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of two (2) individuals by the Agents of NBI Western Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-WEMRO) in an entrapment operation in Zamboanga City for Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents. NBI Director ERIC B. DISTOR identified the arrested subjects as INDIRA PULALON y TAHSIN and AMELITO SAPPARI y WALIJI. Director DISTOR said that the operation stemmed from a call by the Officer-In-Charge of the Office of the Registry of Deeds, Zamboanga City informing the Agents of NBI-WEMRO that they are in receipt of eleven (11) fake/spurious titles presented by two (2) individuals together with their broker, which were later found to be victims of fraud. The 2 victims appeared before the office of NBI-WEMRO to file their formal complaints against the persons behind the fraudulent activity. The complainants stated in their affidavit that the properties were sold and mortgaged to them by four (4) individuals including the arrested Subject Pulalon. The complainants were able to shell out P13,460,000.00. On June 1, 2022, the complainants informed the NBI-WEMRO that Subjects are again dealing another title, suspected to be fake and spurious for Php1,500,000.00. Thus, NBI-WEMRO planned an entrapment operation against the subjects. Upon receiving the information, NBI-WEMRO proceeded to the target meeting area, which resulted in the arrest of Subject Pulalon and a certain WENCESLAO S. TANGLAO, whom they claimed to be the owner of the subject property but was later identified as AMELITO SAPPARI. The operatives later learned that Subject Sappari only used the name of Tanglao to lure their victims in purchasing their fake titles. On June 2, 2022, the arrested subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Zamboanga City for Violation of Article 315 and Article 172 of the Revised Penal Code (Estafa thru Falsification of Public Documents). DISTOR cautioned the public to be more vigilant in their transactions before they shell out their hard earned money. Moreover, Director DISTOR stated that the NBI will continue to hunt the three (3) subjects who are still at-large and warned that the NBI will not stop until all of these unscrupulous individuals were put behind bars.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: PRESS STATEMENT October 27, 2022 NBI ARRESTS A KOREAN FUGITIVE The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the arrest of KIM GIROK by the operatives of NBI- International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) on October 13, 2022 in Taguig City. Subject Kim is a Korean fugitive wanted in South Korea for Human Trafficking activities. The operation stemmed from the request of the Supreme Prosecutor’s Office of Korea, seeking assistance of the NBI-IOD for the arrest and deportation of Subject Kim. Immediately, agents of NBI-IOD conducted series of stakeout, casing operations and internet surveillance to ascertain the exact location of the Korean subject, which resulted in the discovery of the subject’s current residence in a condominium in Taguig City. Coordination was made with the Bureau of Immigration – Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU) requesting for a joint operation for the apprehension of Subject Kim. In addition, NBI-IOD also coordinated with the Southern Police District (SPD) regarding with the operation. Thus, on October 13, 2022, operatives of NBI-IOD together with the BI-FSU proceeded to the residence of Subject Kim where they waited for his arrival. A few hours later, Subject Kim was spotted arriving at the area and was immediately arrested. Subject Kim was brought to the NBI-IOD office for booking procedures and was then turned-over to the Bureau of Immigration.

Santiago (Ret.) lauded the NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing search warrants and reminded the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to protect to the intellectual property rights of brand owners.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Three Nigerians engaged in drug trafficking were arrested by NBI agents during a buy bust operation in Paranaque City last night. The suspects are identified as: 1) Christopher O. Chima a.k.a. Chirixtobar Okeafor a.k.a. Anthony Chima, nicknamed “CHIMA”, 37,Nigerian,Mitoria St., Las Pinas City; 2) Lucky Ugboaga y Chinwe, 37, Nigerian 3) Xtanley Chirkezie, 35, Nigerian, Times St., Las Pinas City. Investigation report of the NBI-Anti Organized Crime Division (AOCD) disclosed that early last month, the NBI received information of some Nigerian nationals who were trafficking metamphetamine chloride or shabu. On March 13, 2013, two (2) test buys were made in Malate, Manila and Las Pinas City. The transaction yielded several grams of shabu. Thereafter, a buy bust operation was planned last weekend. At around 10:00 pm of April 14, 2013, agents of the NBI-Anti Organized Crime Division proceeded to Las Pinas City, and conducted said buy-bust operation in Zapote, Las Pinas City. Some 100 grams of shabu worth P300,000.00 in sachets were purchased leading to the arrest of the Nigerian suspects. Another 5 grams of shabu in sachet was recovered from Chirkezie. They were brought to the NBI main office for booking and detention. Charges for violation of RA 9165 Illegal Possession and Selling of Metamphetamine Hydrochloride known as shabu are prepared before the City Prosecutor’s Office in Las Pinas City.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announces the promulgation of Sta. Cruz, Laguna Family Court Branch 6, convicting Subjects MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDELANA VIRAY y MASALONGA, who were arrested by the elements of NBI-Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Division (NBI-AVAWCD) on September 26, 2019 and charged for Human Trafficking. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor said that last September 2019, NBI-AVAWCD received an information regarding with the unlawful activities of the subjects in Laguna offering minor girls for sexual pleasure for a fee. NBI-AVAWCD operatives immediately conducted surveillance to confirm the veracity of the information which yielded positive results and confirmed that there was indeed human trafficking activities in the area. Thus, on September 26, 2019, NBI-AVACD operatives hatched the entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of Subjects MENDOZA and VIRAY, together with their companion WARREN MASACAYAN y REYES and with the rescue of two (2) female victims including three (3) minor girls. In a series of court appearances, NBI-AVAWCD operatives testified categorically and muster the test of credibility and consistency which ultimately earned the full faith and confidence of the court. The court hearings were also attended by the victims and witnesses who gave their testimonies which solidified the fact that Subjects Mendoza and Viray indeed committed the crime of Qualified Trafficking. Thus, on March 04, 2021, a judgment was promulgated finding accused MARY JANE MENDOZA y PARAISO and MAGDALENA VIRAY y MASALOGA guilty beyond reasonable doubt for five (5) counts of Qualified Trafficking in Persons as defined and penalized under R.A. 9208 as further amended by R,A, 10364. The court ordered the two (2) accused to suffer Life Imprisonment for each count and also ordered them to pay a fine of Php 2 Million without eligibility for parole and to pay each private complainants the amount Php 200,000.00 as moral damages and Php 100,000.00 as exemplary damages. The court, however, ordered the acquittal of WARREN MASACAYAN Y REYES for failure of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the latter. OIC-Director Distor emphasized that the NBI will tirelessly hunt groups and individuals who are continuously taking advantage and exploiting the weaknesses of our fellow countrymen.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of five (5) Subjects by operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) on January 21, 2021 for illegal occupation of a protected area in Antipolo City. NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor identified Subjects as MILANIO RESURECCION, ZERNAN VILLAFRANCA, JOJO MALLORCA, MARWIN LLEAVANES, and ERWIN INTELA. OIC-Distor said that January 12, 2021, a request from DENR-PENR Rizal was sent to the NBI-EnCD requesting assistance and joint operation in Sitio San Ysiro, Brgy. San Jose, Antipolo City. The aforesaid area located within the Upper Marikina River Basin Protected Landscape (UMRBPL) has illegal occupants who constructed infrastructure without Protected Area Management Board clearance. During the verification and inquiries, a report was received that a certain “ELIO”, one of the five identified illegal occupants within UMRBPL, is allegedly involved in selling the other portions of the land also falling within UMRBPL. With this, poseur-buyers transacted with “ELIO” later identified as MILANIO RESURECCION wherein a 1,000-sqm lot within Sitio San Ysiro, Brgy. San Jose, Antipolo City was agreed to be bought for Php150,000.00. The parties also agreed that the poseur buyers will pay Php20,000.00 as downpayment. Operatives saw that there are permanent structures found within the UMRBPL and they were able to verify the existence of the five structures owned by MILANIO RESURECCION (structure 1), GIGI and JUNJUN MUTYA with actual occupant ZERNAN VILLAFRANCA (structure 2), JOJO MALLORCA (structure 3), JAMES BAUTISTA with actual occupant MARWIN LLEAVANES (structure 4), and JOHN ROBIE JUAREZ with actual occupant ERWIN INTELA (structure 5). Upon communication with the DENR-PENRO Rizal, the entrapment operation was conducted on January 21, 2021 resulting in the arrest of subject MILANIO RESURECCION after receiving the boodle money as payment for downpayment. Occupants of the illegal structures, ZERNAN VILLAFRANCA y DATARIO, JOJO MALLORCA y TOCA, MARWIN LLEAVANES y CANONCE, and ERWIN INTELA y PANOY, were likewise arrested after failing to show any document claiming title or right to occupy a portion of the UMRBPL. A certification from the DENR-PENRO Rizal was likewise issued identifying that the above-named Subjects are not authorized to conduct, erect, or maintain the structure built within the same area. Charges for violation of Section 20 and (o) of RA 7586 as amended by RA 11038 and violation of Section 81 of PD 705 were filed against the Subjects before the Office of the Prosecutor General, Department of Justice.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless campaign against graft and corruption, operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) arrested an employee of DBM-Procurement Service in Manila on April 16, 2020 for unauthorized sharing of confidential files. NBI OIC Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as ENGR. MANUEL S. AVILA, an employee of the Procurement Service, an attached agency of the Department of Budget and Management. OIC Distor said that the NBI on April 15, 2020, received a complaint from PS-DBM, relative to the unauthorized access given by Engr. Manuel Avila to a certain DENNIS CHUA who was, in turn, able to access and view the shared files containing all procurement documents and information for the COVID-19 Response Procurement. Distor said the documents contained in Google Drive folder include files from the preparatory procurement stages until the issuance of the Notice to Proceed including the files that were recently added by other price monitoring team collaborators of PS-DBM, which are all considered CONFIDENTIAL. According to the complaint, the PS-DBM is in the process of procuring Personal Protective Equipment, medicines, medical supplies, and medical equipment needed to contain, if not, eliminate the Covid-19 pandemic in the Philippines. Relative to this, PS-DBM availed of the emergency bidding as allowed by the law by creating a Special Bids and Awards Committee (SBAC) for the purpose of the Covid-19 Response-Related Procurement. Because of the ECQ and the work from home arrangement imposed by the office, PS-DBM created a Google Drive Account/folder where members of the SBAC and its related teams may access, edit, or view pricing of the supplies and equipment, as well as collaborate real time for such matter while working at home. The Google Drive Account contains sensitive and confidential information relative to the bidding of the supplies and equipment which include, but not limited to, the prices canvassed for the items, the buds offered by proponents, list of suppliers and their personal information, among others. On April 6, 2020, while uploading the Market Survey in the Google Drive Account, a member of the Price Monitoring Team discovered that a certain DENNIS CHUA was seen to have accessed and viewed all the shared files in the Google Drive Account. Upon review of the Google Drive, it showed that on March 18, 2020, subject Engr. MANUEL S. AVILA was the one who granted access of the shared files in the Google Drive Account to Dennis Chua, without consent from his superiors or from the head of the Procurement Service, and surreptitiously shared or disseminated the files, data, and information therein to Dennis Chua. The complaint added that, in effect, the latter, who is not a member of the SBAC nor an employee of the PS-DBM, had gained access to the confidential files in the Google Drive. Distor stressed that on April 16, 2020, NBI-SAU operatives proceeded to PS-DBM with regard to the complaint against Engr. MANUEL S. AVILA. Subject said that he did not know that the files which he sent to Dennis Chua are confidential. Based on said admission, together with testimonies of witnesses and other supporting evidence, Engr. Avila was placed under arrest. Subject Engr. Avila was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012), and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012).

body: PRESS STATEMENT January 27, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI RESCUES TWO VIETNAMESE NATIONALS IN PASAY CITY ANTI-TRAFFICKING STING PASAY, Philippines — On 22 January 2026, the National Bureau of Investigation, through its Human Trafficking Division (NBI-HTRAD), in coordination with the Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking (IACAT), CSWD Pasay and local police, successfully rescued two (2) Vietnamese nationals during a targeted Anti-Trafficking Operation at a luxury hotel in Pasay City. The operation stemmed from intelligence reports regarding a foreign-led syndicate operating within Metro Manila. The group allegedly utilizes encrypted social messaging platforms to advertise the sexual services of Vietnamese, Chinese, and Japanese women. The NBI-HTRAD conducted technical surveillance, which included monitoring the illegal transaction and the reservation of the hotel premises. Following a tactical stakeout, agents observed two women matching the victims’ digital profiles arriving at the scene. Upon a predetermined signal, the team executed the operation, successfully securing the two victims. While the Subjects were not physically present at the drop-off location, agents recovered several mobile devices believed to be central to the syndicate’s communications and booking logistics. The victims were then escorted to the NBI Headquarters to undergo standard medical examinations and formal documentation, as mandated by protocols for rescued foreign nationals. “This operation highlights the evolving nature of human trafficking, where syndicates use technology to hide in plain sight,” Director Magno stated. “We are currently conducting follow-up law enforcement actions to identify, track, and apprehend the organizers behind this international syndicate.” ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, National Bureau of Investigation #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 16, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI ARRESTS FIXERS AND LTO EMPLOYEES FOR CORRUPTION Pasay City, Philippines – On April 14, 2026, agents of the NBI-Homicide Division arrested nine individuals in Quezon City for violations of Republic Act No. 11032 (Anti-Fixing Law) and R.A. No. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act). The operation stemmed from intelligence reports of a fixing scheme at an LTO satellite office in Quezon City involving fixers and certain LTO personnel. Acting on this, NBI agents conducted an entrapment operation where an undercover agent, posing as a license applicant, was approached by a fixer and later introduced to individuals with direct links to LTO employees facilitating the scheme. The poseur-buyer paid Php 7,000.00 for expedited processing and guaranteed approval. Investigation revealed coordination among fixers, a “bagman,” and involved personnel, enabling applicants to bypass standard procedures through marked documents and unauthorized access to restricted areas. Upon receiving the prearranged signal, NBI agents entered the premises and arrested six fixers, two LTO personnel, and one internal hire reportedly connected to the office’s leadership. The arrested individuals were presented for inquest proceedings for the said violations. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag commended the operatives and reiterated the Bureau’s firm commitment to the government’s anti-corruption drive. He warned that public officials who engage in corrupt practices will be pursued and held fully accountable under the law. You can watch the video below https://www.facebook.com/reel/3557222014435176

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 23, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the government’s efforts to strengthen the foreign relations with the international community, the National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) arrested a Korean fugitive identified as JANG SEONG WOONG in Pasay City. The arrest was based on an official communication from the Senior Consul of the Embassy of the Republic of Korea to the Bureau of Immigration. This communication identified the individual as an undesirable alien who poses a risk to public safety and security due to his status as a fugitive from justice. Additionally, an Interpol Red Notice has been issued for this individual, following a warrant of arrest from the Daegu District Court for Serious Physical Injury and Kidnapping in violation of the Criminal Act of Korea. The Subject, along with fellow gang members, detained and severely assaulted the victim with a baseball bat, resulting in multiple injuries. This attack was related to the victim’s gambling debts. Verification with the Bureau of Immigration (BI) confirmed that the Subject arrived in the Philippines on May 1, 2017, as a tourist and was initially granted a 30-day stay. The Subject later applied for extensions, with the most recent extension valid until January 28, 2020. Since then, the Subject has stopped reporting to the BI and is therefore considered to be in the Philippines in an overstaying status. Further, BI disclosed that the Subject has an active derogatory record under Blacklist Order dated November 28, 2019 for undesirability and being a fugitive from justice. On May 22, 2025, agents from the NBI-OTCD and the BI-Fugitive Search Unit (BI-FSU), in collaboration with the Korean National Police Agency (KNPA) and the Philippine Air Force Military Intelligence, conducted an enforcement operation that resulted in the arrest of the Subject. The Subject was turned over to the BI-FSU agents for proper disposition. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-OTCD and expressed his gratitude to the BI-FSU, PAF- Military Intelligence, and the KNPA for their invaluable support that led to the successful apprehension of the Subject.

body: This pertains to the news reports involving agents of the Bureau. Immediately after these incidents, the Internal Affairs Division has conducted initial and thorough investigations to ascertain their accountability for any violations of law. Misconduct has no place in this Bureau. Due process will be observed, but those who dishonor the badge will be held fully accountable. When formal charges are filed, preventive suspension will immediately follow. From here onwards, we will further intensify our internal programs on professional conduct, discipline, leadership, and crisis behavior—not as punishment, but as a commitment to growth. To the general public we serve, your trust is the foundation of our mandate. We owe you transparency, professionalism, and unwavering commitment. This incident is a reminder of the reforms we must continue to strengthen from within so we may serve you better. To the good men and women of the NBI—you are the reason we protect the integrity of this institution. A few cannot be allowed to stain the service of the many who work with decency, discipline, and respect for the law. The NBI moves forward with three clear commitments: 1. Accountability — wrongdoers will face consequences, without fear or favor. 2. Re-education and Reform — we recommit to training, values formation, and strengthening our internal culture. 3. Renewed Trust — trust in the NBI must begin with the NBI. We build it from within, and we uphold it every day in public service. We will continue to intensify programs on professionalism, conduct, and leadership. Trust in the NBI begins with us, and we will earn it every day. body: • On April 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) arrested as ENGR. MANUEL S. AVILA, an employee of Procurement Service, an attached agency of Department of Budget and Management, for unauthorized sharing of confidential files. Subject was arrested in entrapment operation which stemmed from a complaint of PS-DBM relative to the unauthorized access given Engr. Manuel Avila to a certain Dennis Chua who was, in turn able to access and view the shared files containing all procurement documents and information for Covid-19 Response Procurement. Documents contained in Google Drive include files from the preparatory procurement stages until the issuance of the Notice to Proceed including the files that were recently added by other price monitoring team collaborators of PS-DBM, which are all considered confidential. Because of the ECQ and the work from home arrangement imposed by the office, PS-DBM created the Google Drive Account folder where members of the SBAC and its related teams may access, edit, view pricing of the supplies and equipment, as well as collaborate real time for such matter while working at home. On April 6, 2020, while uploading the Market Survey in the Google Drive Account, a member of the Price Monitoring Team discovered that a certain Dennis Chua was seen to have accessed and viewed all the shared files in the Google Drive Account. Upon review, it showed that it was Engr. Avila who granted access of the shared files to Dennis Chua without consent from his superiors of from the head of Procurement Service. On April 16, 2020, the NBI operatives proceeded to PS-DBM with the regard to the complaint. Subject Engr. Manuel Avila said he did not know that the files which he sent to Dennis Chua are confidential. Based on the said admission, together with the testimonies of witnesses and other supporting evidence, Engr. Avila was placed under arrest. Subject Engr. Manuel Avila was presented for inquest proceedings before the Department of Justice for violation of RA 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act), RA 9184 (Government Procurement Reform Act), RA 10173 (Data Privacy Act of 2012), and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act), in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). • On April 20, 2020, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested RYMEL MACARIMBAG y SORONGON in entrapment operation for selling online overpriced alcohol. Seized during the operation were 5 pieces of 1-liter unlabeled plastic bottles that Subject sold at Php 270 per liter which exceeds the price ceiling set by the DOH. Cases for violation of RA 7581, RA 7394, and RA 11469 in relation to RA 10175 were filed before the Iloilo City Prosecutor’s Office. • On April 21, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) arrested MARVIN ROQUE y SANTOS and GERALD SANTOS and turned them over to their Punong Barangay. They were apprehended after being seen on board a tricycle with a passenger while operatives were dispatched to Brgy. Sto. Rosario to validate the information regarding an ambulance that was allegedly used for transportation of passengers from Manila to Bulacan and vice versa, in violation of the Enhanced Community Quarantine issued to the Local Government Units. Marvin Roque, the tricycle driver, has no professional license and any identification document. It was gathered upon checking Brgy. Sto. Rosario’s CCTV footage, that an ambulance with plate number AQA 5453, resembles the above-mentioned vehicle. In this connection NBI operatives requested to conduct investigation to identify and file charges against the perpetrators, if warranted. • On April 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested SHI JIANCHUAN, a Chinese national, for selling and distributing capsules purportedly as a cure for Covid-19. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that there are groups of Chinese nationals who are selling and distributing capsules purportedly as treatment for Covid-19. Poseur-customers then ordered six (6) boxes of said medicine for a total of Php 240,000 thru “WeChat” app. A box contains 400 packs which in turn, contains 24 capsules per pack. Coordination with the FDA was likewise made. On the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. FDA issued by the FDA states the Subject does not a license to operate and the capsule is unregistered in their office. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of City Prosecutor of Manila for violations of RA 3720 (Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act) as amended by RA 9711 (FDA Act of 2009) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act). • On April 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested MARIE ANTONNETTE F. FLORES for selling overpriced medical supplies. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation at San Fernando, La Union in coordination with the DTI-Region 1. Poseur-customer transacted with Tonnie Flores (Tonyang) who was selling alcohol and facemasks. The deal resulted to a sale of 50 bottles of 1-liter alcohol that cost Php 280 per bottle amounting to a total sum of Php 14,000. Confiscated were 50 bottles of 1-liter unbranded ethyl alcohol but with labeling Ethyl Alcohol 80%, NISCE SKIN MEDICAL GROUP, INC. Subject is identified as the manager of Farmacia Win-J. During the entrapment operation, the driver-helper identified as ALBERT ALLAN D. CUENCA, two employees of Farmacia Win-J identified as IMELDA BAUTISTA CASPILLAN and JASMIN ACOSTA FAMA, were also present. Verification was made with DTI to determine the proprietor of Farmacia Win-J. Subjects were arrested in entrapment operation after they delivered 120 gallons of isopropyl alcohol to the poseur buyer with an estimated amount of Php 62,400. Charges for violation of RA 7581 (Price Act), RA 7394 (Consumer Welfare Act) and RA 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) were filed against the Subjects. • On April 24, 2020, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested BERNARDO ALBULADORA JR y OPAMA for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act). Rosario to validate the information regarding an ambulance that was allegedly used for transportation of passengers from Manila to Bulacan and vice versa, in violation of the Enhanced Community Quarantine issued to the Local Government Units. Rosario’s CCTV footage, that an ambulance with plate number AQA 5453, resembles the above-mentioned vehicle. body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } Under the directive of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), the NBI – Cavite North District Office (CAVIDO-North) arrested NOEL P. SANTOS for a violation of Section 6 of Republic Act No. 8042, as amended by R.A. 10022, otherwise known as the “Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995,” Estafa under Article 315 paragraph 2 (a) of the Revised Penal Code, and Acts of Lasciviousness under Article 336 of the Revised Penal Code. Several complainants went to the NBI-CAVIDO-North to file a complaint against Subject Noel Santos y Pagsibigan, A.K.A. Mark Ivan Rosel, for illegal recruitment, estafa, and acts of lasciviousness. Subject allegedly received money and promised employment in Japan as a masseur without the necessary license or authorization from the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW). On August 1, 2025, NBI-CAVIDO-North agents arrested Subject Santos during an entrapment operation in Naic, Cavite. Subject Santos was presented for inquest before the Provincial Prosecutor of Cavite for the above-stated violations. He was then properly turned over and detained at the Bureau of Corrections, NBI Jail Facility, Muntinlupa City. The arrest of an illegal recruiter is not just about punishing an individual; it’s about protecting vulnerable workers, promoting ethical recruitment, and ensuring justice for victims of exploitation. Director Santiago reiterates the NBI’s commitment, in coordination with partner agencies, to combat human trafficking and illegal recruitment schemes targeting vulnerable Filipinos. Authorities remind the public to verify recruitment offers and report suspicious activities through the proper government channels.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual in Marikina City for illegal drugs and illegal possession of firearms. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subject as PHILIP JACOB NOCOM Y LIM a.k.a “ALEX BENSON VERGARA y MARAGONDON, a.k.a. JOHN ROBERT BAUTISTA y CHUA, and a.k.a. JOSEPH FRANCIS LEE y CAMACHO. The operation stemmed from a report received by NBI-International Operation Division (NBI-IOD) from the owner of a security firm on June 25, 2020, that his employees discovered in a condo unit two pieces of high powered firearms, live ammunitions, and white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu. Earlier that day, a representative of the unit owner sought the assistance of the two security guards of the condominium to check on the tenant whom they known as “ALEX VERGARA” because the tenant has defaulted payment for two months. After knocking several times and waiting for several hours, and with the permission of the unit owner, they forcibly opened the door. They found Mr. Vergara lying on his bed, almost unconscious and weak. The security guards also saw an M16 rifle beside Vergara’s bed and a 9mm caliber automatic pistol with several loaded magazine lying around. They also saw several transparent plastics with white crystalline substance. Several identification cards were also found inside the unit. Thereafter, the security guards informed their superior and reported the incident to the NBI-IOD. NBI-IOD operatives immediately proceeded to the area and inspected the unit. There they found crystalline like substance on several plastic sachets. NBI-IOD then called the assistance of NBI-Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) being the operational unit within the NBI mandated to investigate illegal drug related cases. When the NBI-TFAID arrived, the security guards in the presence of barangay officials, turned over to the NBI operatives the M16 automatic rifle, caliber 9mm automatic pistol, several live ammunitions, several loaded M16 and pistol magazines, several tactical knives, hand held radios, several electronic devices, and several government issued identifications including two (2) kilograms of shabu and .5 grams of cocaine with an estimated value of Php 13 Million. Based on the seized documents, the operatives discovered that subject Vergara is using three other aliases. Subject was placed under arrest and was brought to the NBI-Manila. Subject was presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Marikina City for violation of Section 28 of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act), Section 11 of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002), and Section 3 of Commonwealth Act No. 142, Regulating the Use of Alias.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 14, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI RESCUES TRAFFICKED VICTIMS FROM SCAM HUB; RECRUITER ARRESTED The National Bureau of Investigation-International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID) arrested an individual linked to the illegal recruitment and transport of Filipino victims to a scam hub in Myanmar, following the rescue and repatriation of those who were allegedly forced to participate in fraudulent online scam operations targeting foreign nationals. On May 11, 2026, the NAIA Task Force Against Trafficking (NAIATFAT) endorsed to the NBI-IAID for investigation twenty-five (25) repatriated passengers which arrived from Myanmar. The NBI-IAID established through interviews and sworn statements that the twenty-five (25) passengers had been held by the Myanmar military in connection with an online scam operation during the last week of December 2025, following their earlier request to be rescued from the scam hub. Investigation conducted resulted in the filing of complaints by the passengers against their co-passenger who acted as their recruiter, facilitator, maintainer, harborer, trafficker, and conduit in operating a scam hub in Myanmar. The Subject recruited the complainants through Telegram and WhatsApp by offering overseas jobs with a promised monthly salary of around Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php50,000.00) and other benefits. The complainants were later coached to pretend as tourists or legitimate OFWs to avoid immigration scrutiny before being transported through several transit countries to KK Park, Myawaddy, Myanmar. Upon arrival, the complainants discovered that they would not be employed in legitimate customer service work as promised, but were instead forced to participate in fraudulent online scam operations targeting foreign nationals. Their passports and travel documents were confiscated, their movements were restricted, and they were subjected to intimidation, monetary penalties, and other coercive measures whenever they failed to meet imposed quotas. Unable to leave and fearing for their safety, the complainants sought assistance and were eventually rescued by Myanmar authorities. After their repatriation to the Philippines on May 9 to 10, 2026, twenty-two (22) complainants executed sworn statements positively identifying the Subject as the person responsible for their recruitment, transport, and exploitation. Verification conducted with the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) confirmed that the Subject is neither licensed nor authorized to recruit and deploy workers for overseas employment. Based on the investigation and the DMW certification, authorities found probable cause for violation of Republic Act No. 9208, as amended, for recruiting, transporting, harboring, and exploiting the complainants through fraud and deception. The Subject was placed under arrest, informed of the nature of the offense and her constitutional rights, and subjected to standard booking and arrest procedures. She was thereafter brought for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay through electronic inquest proceedings with the assistance of their counsel. Subject was later turned over to the NBI Detention Center in Muntinlupa City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 17, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI EXPANDS CHILD EXPLOITATION PROBE: CHARGES FILED AGAINST BIOLOGICAL FATHER FOLLOWING MOTHER’S CONVICTION PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has officially filed criminal charges against the biological father of a rescued minor victim of Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC). The charges follow an extensive investigation by the NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), in coordination with the City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWD) of Taguig City on December 19, 2025. The investigation is a continuation of a case originating from a rescue operation in Lower Bicutan, Taguig City, on October 21, 2024. While the victim’s mother has already been convicted and is currently serving her sentence at the Correctional Institution for Women, new testimony has brought the father’s alleged complicity to light. Investigation revealed critical disclosures from the seven-year-old victim-survivor. The child alleged that her father was not only fully aware of her mother’s illicit sexual communications with a foreign national but also engaged in direct communication with the same individual. Further investigation suggests that explicit photographs were transmitted to this foreign contact in exchange for monetary compensation. Beyond the digital exploitation, CSWD-Taguig reported that the father actively attempted to interfere with the minor’s trauma-informed psychosocial interventions while simultaneously seeking to regain legal custody of the victim. On March 5, 2026, operatives from the NBI-NCR, accompanied by the victim, shelter representatives, and personnel from the CSWD, formally filed a criminal complaint before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Taguig. The father now faces charges for violations of Republic Act No. 11930, also known as the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) Act, as well as Republic Act No. 7610, the Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act. “The NBI remains firm in its commitment to protecting the most vulnerable members of our society, and the Bureau will not stop at the indictment of a single subject; our investigation will include every person who participated in the crime, no matter how long it will take,” said NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag. “Let this be a clear message: anyone who participates in, facilitates, or profits from the abuse of children—including their own kin—will be held accountable to the fullest extent of the law.” #NBIServes

body: PRESS STATEMENT September 07, 2022 NBI ARRESTS THREE FOR ESTAFA AND USE OF ALIASES The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) announced the arrest of CHARITO COMENDADOR a.k.a. “JULIETA DE ASIS y SANCHEZ”, MA. LIEZEL HERNANDEZ y IGNACIO a.k.a. “MARITES TORES y REYES”, and LOLITA GALERO y GARAY by the operatives of NBI-Bulacan District Office (NBI-BULDO) in an entrapment operation in Guiguinto, Bulacan for violations of Article 315 of the Revised Penal Code (RPC) and Commonwealth Act No. 142 (An Act to Regulate the Use of Aliases). The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of the 3 above-named subjects alleging that the latter connived with each other and used other names for their modus operandi. Subject Ignacio offered a mortgage of a land title allegedly owned by a certain JULIETA DE ASIS who was later identified as Subject Comendador. Believing in the representations of Subject Comendador, the complainant gave Php500,000.00 as mortgage amount and a “Kasulatan ng Sanglaan” was then signed by both parties. After sometime, the complainant discovered that the document presented and given to her by Subject Comendador was a falsified document and it was confirmed thru the heir of the real JULIETA DE ASIS that the subject property is not for mortgage. Also, Subjects were demanding additional mortgage money from the complainant. Thus, the complainant proceeded to the office of NBI-BULDO and filed a complaint against the 3 Subjects. The complainant was advised to agree with the demand of the Subjects and planned an entrapment operation. The Subjects and the complainant agreed to meet in a fast food chain in Guiguinto, Bulacan for the additional mortgage money. On September 2, 2022, Agents of NBI-BULDO proceeded to the agreed meeting place. Upon handing over of the entrapment money, the operatives immediately approached and arrested the subjects. NBI-BULDO was able to seize the entrapment money, Conditional Deed of Sale signed by Subject Comendador and her cohorts, Subjects Hernandez and Torres, as witnesses; acknowledgement receipt by Subject Comendador; one (1) cellphone; one (1) BIR I.D. of Subject Comendador; and a Philhealth ID under the name of Subject Comendador. The arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Malolos City.

The operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of the 3 above-named subjects alleging that the latter connived with each other and used other names for their modus operandi. Subject Ignacio offered a mortgage of a land title allegedly owned by a certain JULIETA DE ASIS who was later identified as Subject Comendador. Believing in the representations of Subject Comendador, the complainant gave Php500,000.00 as mortgage amount and a “Kasulatan ng Sanglaan” was then signed by both parties. After sometime, the complainant discovered that the document presented and given to her by Subject Comendador was a falsified document and it was confirmed thru the heir of the real JULIETA DE ASIS that the subject property is not for mortgage. Also, Subjects were demanding additional mortgage money from the complainant. Thus, the complainant proceeded to the office of NBI-BULDO and filed a complaint against the 3 Subjects. The complainant was advised to agree with the demand of the Subjects and planned an entrapment operation. The Subjects and the complainant agreed to meet in a fast food chain in Guiguinto, Bulacan for the additional mortgage money. On September 2, 2022, Agents of NBI-BULDO proceeded to the agreed meeting place. Upon handing over of the entrapment money, the operatives immediately approached and arrested the subjects. NBI-BULDO was able to seize the entrapment money, Conditional Deed of Sale signed by Subject Comendador and her cohorts, Subjects Hernandez and Torres, as witnesses; acknowledgement receipt by Subject Comendador; one (1) cellphone; one (1) BIR I.D. of Subject Comendador; and a Philhealth ID under the name of Subject Comendador. The arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office of Malolos City.

body: On May 4, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested ROSEMARIE N. MAURILLO and GAUDENCIO MONTANO AYUDA JR. for violation of PD 1612 (Anti-Fencing Law of 1979) in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation conducted Robinsons Otis, Manila. The operation stemmed from the complaint of Alicia C. Rodriguez against the Subjects for the aforementioned violations. Recovered from the Subjects during the operation were the stolen dental supplies of complainant worth Php 396,800.00. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor, Manila. On May 5, 2018 , operatives of NBI- International Airport Investigation Unit (NBI-IAIU) arrested three (3) human traffickers namely PATRICIA LAMBINO a.k.a. “Mommy”, ROSIE LOPEZ and MARILYN FILOMENO , and rescued one hundred thirty seven (137) female victims in Pasay City. Subjects were arrested in a rescue operation based on an information received by the NBI from a minor who was turned over by DSWD on May 4, 2018. The said 16-year old minor was intercepted by Immigration Officers for attempting to travel to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Investigation revealed that the minor was recruited in from Maguindanao. She was able to get a passport through the help of one Pamiya Muhammad who made it appear therein that she was twenty three (23) years old. She said that she stayed in an apartment at Tolentino St., Pasay City that was provided by Global Connect Manpower Resources, the recruitment agency facilitating her deployment abroad. Certificates on TESDA training and pre-departure seminar were given to her by the said recruitment agency even though she did not attend the training and seminar. According to her, she has a friend, also a minor, and others who are still in the apartment and are due for deployment abroad. Acting on the information, a rescue operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and the rescue of the trafficked women, twenty nine (29) of which are minors. Subjects were brought before the Department of Justice, Manila for Inquest proceedings for violations of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by RA 10364 (Expanded Anti-Human Trafficking in Persons Act of 2012) and RA 8042 (Migrant Workers and Overseas Filipinos Act of 1995). On May 7, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested twenty individuals for illegal gambling. Subjects were arrested in two (2) Peryahan ng Bayan Outlets by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 89, Quezon City. Nine (9) Subjects namely LITO GARIN ESTEMBER, GEZELLE TABA TANIQUE, DONNA DALAGUIT MELLAMA, RODELYN POLEROS MELLAMA, JOFFREY POLEROS MELLAMA, ARJOERAN JUAREZ ELISAN, MARK JOHN ESCOBA CAMARINES, JOHN RAY NAPILAY SUEDE, and OFELENIO BELNAS TOMAQUIN were arrested in Peryahan ng Bayan station located at Burgos-Lacson Streets, Bacolod City. On the other hand, eleven (11) Subjects namely MARY MAY SANTILLAN BRITAIN, ELENA VILLAJOS JOSE, EMALYN JOSE GUARDANIA, SHIELA MAE DALAGUIT CASTILLA, JOEREVIN ADLIT VILLARANTE, CARLOS TAGPUNO, DELA CRUZ, CHINGRIG VELANO PADAYOGDOG, EDMUND PUZON BOSICO, ROY BRAVO AGABON, JUVY BANDOJO BONDA, and VICENTE CABATANIA GOMEZ were arrested at Peryahan ng Bayan station located at North Avenue, Escalante City, Negros Occidental. The searches were conducted in an orderly and peaceful manner. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor for violation of RA 9287 (Illegal Gambling Law). On May 9, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office arrested JIMBOY TALIB y AMIRUL and BENJIMAR HUSSAM y GUMBAN for violation of RA 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002). Based on the information, a certain AL and MUNIB, together with the runners they employed are engaged in the sale of illegal drugs. Investigation conducted disclosed that a certain “Jul” later identified to be Subject JIMBOY TALIB y AMIRUL , who upon orders from drug patrons delivers drugs to various barangays in Zamboanga City. With this, a buy-bust operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of above-mentioned Subjects. Charges for violation of RA 9165 were filed against the Subjects. On May 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested RHOWIN M. BIAG in an entrapment operation for violation of cybercrime law (sextortion). The case stemmed from the complaint of Jovelyn F. Soriano against the subject who was in possession of her private photos and videos. Subject demanded sexual favors in exchange of the private photos and videos not to be posted online. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subject. Subject was presented for inquest proceeding before the fiscal’s office for the aforementioned violation. On May 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested PATRICIA ELLAINE LUIZ SANTOS y LASTIMOSA in an entrapment operation for Theft and violation of RA 8484 (Access Devices Regulations Act of 1998). The case stemmed from the complaint of Rosalyn H. Tabbu against the Subject. Seized from the Subject were Php 20,000.00 cash and the Metrobank ATM card of the complainant. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for the aforementioned violations. On May 15, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested HIDEFUMI OBATA and SHINSAKU FUJITA for Grave Coercion. The case stemmed from the complaint of Nerisa P. Cai against the Subjects who coerced her so that the case of Physical Injury filed by Subject OBATA against her husband Jian Quan Cai would not be filed. It all started when Subject OBATA wanted to return the backpack in complainant’store and have a refund. Complainant explained that she does not sell the kind of backpack that Subject OBATA was claiming to have been bought from her store. A heated argument occurred and Jian Quan Cai punched Subject OBATA’s abdominal part which caused the latter a broken rib as per medical examination. Jian Quan Cai was thereafter brought to the Prosecutor’s Office for inquest proceedings. Subject OBATA, with the help of his translator, started demanding money from the complainant in exchange for non-filing of the case against her husband. Complainant paid the amount that the Subject was asking for but no favorable result ensued. Complainant then sought the assistance of NBI. Acting on the complaint, an entrapment operation was set as the Complainant was continuously receiving text messages from the interpreter SHINSAKU FUJITA demanding for the payment. The entrapment operation resulted in the arrest of Subjects HIDEFUMI OBATA and SHINSAKU FUJITA. They were thereafter brought to the City Prosecutor, Department of Justice for inquest proceedings for Grave Coercion. On May 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized counterfeit Crayola crayons with an estimated amount of Php 426,420.00 in Navotas City. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. The case stemmed from the complaint of Ma. Esmeralda G. Alcaraz, Vice President of Amalgamated Specialties Corporation (AMSPEC), requesting investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of fake Crayola crayons. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against Tony Tan, et.al. On May 18, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested THOMAS LEWIS MILLER, a Canadian/South African, for violation of Article 315 (Estafa) of the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The case stemmed from the complaint of Lilia G. Apostol who averred that she met a certain WESLEY thru an internet dating site. The latter introduced himself as an Operations Manager of Galliford Try and residing in Los Angeles, California. Soon after, by sweet talks in Facebook Messenger, they had established relationship. In the course of the conversations, Wesley told the complainant that he will be visiting the Philippines so they can meet personally and buy a house and lot where they can both reside. To fulfill that, Wesley told the complainant that he will be sending $500,000 but since he was caught up with some issues in the ports, he will be asking THOMAS, identified as son of his friend, to bring the money to the Philippines. Complainant then met THOMAS who asked Php 100,000 to claim the package at the airport. Thereafter, MILLER presented a box sent by Wesley, containing the money which was dyed black to avoid detection from the airport security. MILLER demonstrated how the black paper turned into dollars by using SSD chemical. However, according to MILLER, the chemical had already expired so they need to purchase the chemical which costs $45,000 or Php 2,500,000. Complainant, however, told MILLER that she cannot produce the amount. As she was looking for the chemical online, she discovered that the SSD chemical is well-known as being used in fraudulent modus operandi known globally as Black Money Scam. With this, complainant sought the assistance of the NBI. A careful scrutiny of the black paper revealed that the same quality of paper was used in another fraud case in Vigan City sometime in 2009 by some Nigerian citizens. After investigation and verification, operatives of NBI-STF conducted an entrapment operation which resulted in the arrest of Subject MILLER. Charges for violation of RA 10175 (The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012) were filed against the Subject. On May 21, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested RICHARD D. JALANDOON in an entrapment operation for Grave Threat. The case stemmed from the complaint of Gina D. Galedo against the Subject. After the usual booking process, Subject was presented for inquest proceedings before the office of the City Prosecutor, Manila for Grave Threat under the Revised Penal Code in relation to RA 10175 (The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On May 22, 2018 , operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized counterfeit Jo Malone perfumes with an estimated amount of Php 17,290,000.00 in Binondo, Manila and Pasay City. Items were seized by virtue of Search Warrants issued by RTC Branch 46, Manila. Charges for violation of RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the owners/operators of various stalls at 168 Shopping Mall and 999 Shopping Mall located at Binondo. Manila, and Baclaran Reminal I Plaza located in Pasay City.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with the relentless effort of the government against cyber-criminals, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of a 21-year old IT student for hacking the website of a prestigious University and accessing the accounts of its students. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric Bito-on Distor identified the subject as JOHN RAVEN AQUINO. OIC Distor said the case stemmed from a complaint filed by representatives of San Beda University (SBU) regarding the alleged hacking and defacement of the SBU’S online School Management System Portal. It was also disclosed that penetration of the web servers were determined on June 02, 2020 and were reported accordingly by the IT administrators of SBU. However, on June 04, 2020, unknown hacker/s defaced the SBU website. Cyber-surveillance was then conducted by the NBI. A Twitter account @yougotpwn unveiled on the social media that SBU’s student personal information and log-in credentials were extracted from the SBU’s server. @yougotpwn was reported and later removed from Twitter. It was followed by numerous incidents on social media that respective Facebook/Twitter accounts of SBU students were illegally accessed. A deeper cyber-surveillance was conducted and revealed that Subject/s created a github.com account under username @yougotpwn and dumped the extracted SBU’s log-in database. On June 10, 2020, representatives of SBU presented to the NBI user-registration database and audit report of their anti-virus application conducted on June 03, 2020. In their standard operating procedures of registering users, the NBI noticed a questionable user registration under email [email protected] registered on May 26, 2020. Also, the database leaked on github.com also contained user email [email protected] using various I.P. addresses for the period May 26, 2020 to May 20, 2020. Moreover, Audit Report from SBU’s Anti-Virus Application showed on June 02, 20200 logs of high risk malwares penetrated their system and subject/s had installed a backdoor web shell solus.php. Handler name @solus was known through the NBI-Cyber Crime investigation of Justine Claveria who was arrested in an entrapment operation in Agoncillo, Batangas on April 21, 2020. @solus is one of the cohorts of Claveria in hacking, phishing and scamming activities. He is the founder and leader of Global Security Hacker Group (GSH) whose members were also identified by the NBI-CCD. Information also disclosed and supported that @solus was identified as JOHN RAVEN AQUINO. Casing and surveillance operation was then conducted which confirmed the address and the vehicle owned by @solus (as described by Claveria). On June 22, 2020, the NBI-CCD applied for a Warrant to Search, Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) before RTC Pasig City for Violations of Section 4 (a) (1) Illegal Access, Section 4 (a) (3) Data Interference and Section 4 (a) (4) System Interference under Republic Act 10175, otherwise known as “The Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012”. The WSSECD was granted against JOHN RAVEN AQUINO aka “solus and other occupants of Block 14 Lot 20, Condor St. Rolling Meadows 2, Novaliches, Quezon City. On June 25, 2020, CCD operatives implemented the WSSECD and were able to search the premises and found various paraphernalia such as Paymaya cards, Blank cards, Skimming device (MSRX6), Laptop computer system, cellphones, iPad, Router, among others. JOHN RAVEN AQUINO was placed under arrest, apprised of his rights and was brought to the NBI headquarters in Manila for booking procedures.
