body: PRESS STATEMENT August 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with its relentless efforts to combat human trafficking and protect those most at risk, the National Bureau of Investigation-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), intercepted and rescued three women from a suspected human trafficking operation at Francisco Bangoy International Airport in Davao City. The victims were allegedly recruited by a certain “Lalang” and a certain “Yolly”, who are both currently at-large. They were promised employment as entertainers in SSingapore and were booked on a flight from Davao. However, they were offloaded due to improper travel documents. During the NBI’s on-site investigation, the victims disclosed that they were instructed to seek clearance from specific immigration officers. They did not approach those individuals, which prompted further scrutiny by another immigration officer who flagged their papers. Preliminary findings indicate that the victims had allegedly paid “Lalang” a sum of money for the processing of their employment documents. body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by operatives of NBI-Technical Intelligence Division (NBI-TID) for alleged Robbery Extortion. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as SANDY FRIAS y CABALIDA, an employee of the Local Building Office (LBO) of Taguig City, who was arrested in an entrapment operation in Taguig City on May 12, 2021 OIC-Director Distor said a complaint was filed against the subject alleging that when complainant’s company applied for a Building Permit or Certificate of Occupancy on January 19, 2021 at the LBO of Taguig City, they paid the total fees of P108,743.60 and was issued the official receipt as payment for Certificate of Occupancy and Certificate of Electrical Inspection. When complainant asked for the release of the certificates, Subject Sandy Frias told them that the certificates can only be released in exchange for Php 800,000.00. Since the amount is too big, they pleaded to the Subject that the amount be reduced. Subject Frias then told them that the Committee approved the amount to be reduced to P400,000.00, which should be directly paid to him. After more than 3 months of waiting and the same were still withheld by Subject Frias, Complainant finally decided to file a formal complaint before the NBI against the subject for extortion. Under strict orders of Director Distor, NBI-TID operatives conducted an entrapment operation at the meeting place in Taguig City that led to the arrest of Subject Frias after he received the marked money from conplainant. Subject peacefully submitted himself and was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject was presented for Inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor, Taguig City for Robbery Extortion in violation of Article 294 (5) of the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of the NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) have arrested ten (10) persons for illegally possessing and selling giant pearls attached into giant clams. The NBI has identified the Subjects as JONATHAN ACERES, VICTOR ACERES, GERARDO CEREZO, MANUEL TEMPRA, NORBERTO ENVERZO, JESUSALORA OLIVA a.k.a. NORA, VINCENT TANGGARA alias ROY, DIXIE MARIE MADRIDANO, NATRANILLO LARIOSA, and NONITO GRANDIA who were arrested yesterday in an operation along T.M. Kalaw St., Ermita, Manila. The operation was based on the information received on December 19, 2016 that a group of individuals from Tarlac is engaged in selling Giant Pearl produced by a Taklobo or a giant clam which is considered as endangered species. In February 2017, contact with the group was established through a confidential informant. Subsequently, the group offered for sale the giant pearls allegedly weighing at least thirty (30) kilograms at Php 150,000.00 per kilogram. Photographs secured from the Subjects reveal that the alleged pearls are still attached to the valve of a giant taklobo. Operatives, through the confidential informant, haggled with the Subjects for the price of the giants pearls who agreed to deliver the three (3) giant pearls for Ninety Seven Million Pesos (Php 97,000,000.00). In the afternoon of March 13, 2017, the entrapment operation took place. Three (3) vehicles arrived wherein Subject JESUSALORA OLIVA a.k.a. NORA led the poseur buyer to one of the vehicles and thereat pointed at one (1) alleged giant pearl. After which, poseur buyer was led to another vehicle where three (3) pieces of alleged giant pearls attached to the giant taklobo valves were found. Upon verifying the presence of the giant taklobo valves, operatives effected the arrest resulting in the arrest of the Subjects and seizure of the giant pearls. Subjects were brought to the NBI for the booking procedures and recovered specimens were listed in an inventory and were shown to the Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) technical personnel. Mr. November A. Romena, Senior Aqua Examiner and Mr. Crejay Lacena, for appropriate test. Initial examination conducted by the BFAR states that the recovered items are in fact giant clams with common name, True Giant Clam and with scientific name Tridacna Gigas. Charges for Violation of Section 102 of R.A. 8550 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998) as amended by R.A. 10654, were filed against the Subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 08, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } The National Bureau of Investigation-Central Luzon Regional Office (NBI-CELRO), under the supervision of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested two (2) individuals in Cabanatuan City on August 5, 2025 for selling unregistered vape products with an estimated value of Php 10 Million. The operation stemmed from an information regarding the illegal importation and online distribution of unregistered vapor products. These products were reported to be distributed without the necessary Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) Stamps and were not registered with the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI). Acting on the information, NBI-CELRO agents conducted surveillance and test-buy operations targeting identified persons operating in Nueva Ecija and nearby areas. The test-buy confirmed the sale and distribution of illicit vapor products with brand name “SPARK” which includes battery cartridges and various flavored pods. Also, verification with the DTI disclosed that the vape brand “Spark” is not registered with the DTI Office for Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products. On August 5, 2025, NBI-CELRO agents conducted a buy-bust operation in Cabanatuan City that led to the arrest of Subjects JAN MARC DE GUZMAN TRINIDAD and MARC ANGELO DE GUZMAN TRINIDAD. The two were apprehended at a warehouse located at Cantarilla Street near corner Perigola Street, Valdefuente, Cabanatuan City after they attempted to sell illicit vape products to the NBI-CELRO agents who act as poseurbuyer. 100 boxes of vapes consisting of 200 pods and 200 cartridges/batteries each and two cellphones were seized and confiscated from the Subjects. Aside from the fact that the vapes in the warehouse were not duly registered with the DTI and BIR, it was further discovered that the items do not conform with the packaging requirements set by R.A. No. 11900 wherein it lacks the health warnings set by the said law and the Department of Health (DOH) required to be printed in the packaging. Subjects were brought to NBI-CELRO for the standard booking procedure and were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of San Fernando, Pampanga for violation of Section 4 of R.A. No. 11900, otherwise known as the “Vaporized Nicotine and Non-Nicotine Products Regulation Act”. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CELRO for the successful operation, saying that it demonstrates the Bureau’s continued efforts to pursue and apprehend individuals who are engaged in the sale and distribution of illicit vapor products.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the filing of Robbery Extortion charges against a subject who was arrested by operatives of the NBI-Central Luzon Regional Office (CELRO) in an entrapment operation in San Fernando City recently. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ALFONSO JUAQUIN LAZATIN y OCAMPO. OIC Director Distor said that the case stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Lazatin. According to complainant, sometime in October 2020, she saw a Facebook post of the subject offering a straight swap of Xiaomi Red Note 9 (cellphone). Subject Lazatin and the complainant agreed to swap their cellphones. When they met, complainant also handed over the battery charger of her cellphone but the subject refused and insisted that he has a charger and does not need one. After sometime, Subject Lazatin contacted the complainant informing her that the battery of the cellphone expanded. Subject demanded Php 2,000.00 for the repair of the battery to w/c complainant initially refused. Subject threatened that he will tag her online that she is a “scammer” and will post her identification and sex videos which the subject was able to retrieve from her phone. Subject was able to post the gov’t IDs of complainant online. With this, she was compelled to seek assistance from the NBI-CELRO. Subject Lazatin and the complainant agreed to meet in a mall in Telebastegan, San Fernando City, Pampanga to hand over the Php 2,000.00 which the subject demanded. Thus, on April 15, 2021, NBI-CELRO proceeded to the meeting area for an entrapment operation to arrest the subject. Operatives of the NBI immediately arrested the subject after receiving the marked money from complainant. Subject Lazatin was presented for inquest proceedings on April 16, 2021 before the Office of Prosecutor of San Fernando City for the crime of Robbery (Extortion) punishable under the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On the same day, the Prosecutor issued an Inquest Resolution finding probable cause to indict the subject as charged and recommended his prosecution for the said violations of the law.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals by the NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) inside the new NBI Building in Quezon City. NBI Officer-in-Charge (OIC)-Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as LEONARDO G. MONTEVERDE and CHRISTOPHER BACOLOD ENGLE. OIC Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of the subjects before the NBI-STF office alleging that the two (2) subjects entered their establishment Spa along Kamuning, Quezon City and identified themselves as NBI Agents by showing their badges. The complainant also stated that one of the subjects told the attendant of the Spa to inform their manager to call them, otherwise their establishment will be subjected to law enforcement operations. The manager called the subjects and was told that the establishment committed several violations of law. The subjects then demanded a protection money of Php 20,000.00 for them to be spared from law enforcement operations and P18,760.00 for reimbursement of surveillance expenses. The complainant and the subjects agreed to a monthly payment of P8,000.00 and the first payment is to be collected in the establishment by the subject. On May 21, 2021, the NBI-STF hatched at entrapment operation, proceeded to the establishment and strategically positioned themselves in the area. When the subjects called the complainant to meet them in a convenience store just across the Spa to hand over the money, the NBI operatives saw the subjects onboard a NMAX motorcycle wearing a black and red t-shirts, respectively. When the money was about to be handed over to the subjects Monteverde and Engle, both sensed that they were being monitored and immediately left. One of the agents discreetly followed the subjects up to Shell Gas station near the new NBI Building. The agent was surprised because the two subjects entered the NBI Building. The agent followed the subjects and verified that they are not connected with theì NBI. The NBI-STF team followed and arrested the subjects in the basement lobby of the NBI new office at Vtech Tower. Seized from the subjects are fake NBI IDs, badges and a firearm with no permit to carry. Further investigation revealed that Subject Monteverde was a former member of Destiny Rescue, a civic organization organized to stop human trafficking and was dismissed because he used his connection with the organization to extort money from establishments considered as worthy of investigation for possible human trafficking violations. Subjects were presented for Inquest proceedings for Usurpation of Official Functions (Article 177 of the RPC), Attempted Robbery Extortion (Art. 294 of the RPC), and violation of R.A. 10591, otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Regulations Act.

body: A group of workers were arrested for transporting three truck-loads of illegally-cut logs estimated at P4 million which were seized by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Cagayan de Oro City last week. CONGO, and his brother JUNREY, and REY B. SALAZAR, all from Talakag, Bukidnon; VICTOR A. LANUZA, of Patag, Cagayan De Oro City; MARLON D. LINIAN, of Kauswagan, Cagayan De Oro City; and ROLANDO B. NOOL, of Milaya, Wao, Ilocos Sur. An investigation report by the Northeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NEMRO) headed by Acting Regional Director Jose D. Doloiras was submitted to NBI Officer-In-Charge Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas. It was disclosed that in the first week of March, they received information that three truckloads of illegally cut logs were to be transported from Talakag, Bukidnon going to Cagayan de Oro City. The illegal logs were expected in Cagayan De Oro on March 11 or March 12, 2012 with armed escorts on board motorcycles who will serve as their look-out or “sweeper” in case of the presence of checkpoints. Acting on the information, an NBI-NEMRO team was immediately formed to probe and verify the report. In the evening of March 11, said team proceeded to Bgy. Lumbia and positioned themselves in case the truck loads of illegal logs passed by. After several hours of monitoring and search, the team later proceeded to Talakag, Bukidnon. At around 3:00 am of the following day while at Mambuaya, the team saw a convoy of three trucks enroute to Cagayan De Oro heavily loaded with cargoes covered with tarpaulin escorted by two men in motorcycles. The NEMRO team tailed the trucks to the direction of Cagayan De Oro City. Minutes after, the group flagged down the convoy, and ordered the drivers to stop at the Cagayan De Oro Gardens in Lumbia, Cagayan De Oro City. However, when a look-out later identified as suspect Linian, was ordered to disembark from his motorcycle, he tried to flee, but the NBI men subdued him. During verification, it was found out that the lumber cargoes were cut without any permit from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR). The three trucks loaded with thousands of board feet of illegally cut lumber were confiscated. Charges for violation of illegally cut in violation of Section 68 (Section 77 re numbered) of PD 705 as amended by Executive Order No. 277 of the Revised Forestry Code of the Philippines were filed against the suspects before the Cagayan De Oro City Provincial Prosecutor’s Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said today it has filed Murder and Theft charges against two (2) police officers and two unidentified Subjects before the Department of Justice on May 29, 2020 for the killing of DELFIN C. BRITANICO (Del), the son of former Congressman Salvador B. Britanico. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor said the NBI-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID), filed the charges against Subjects PCpl. JERRY VILLANUEVA y CARMELOTES, PCpl. JOSEPH ANDREW JOVEN y PONELES, and two John Does for the death of Del, who sustained eight (8) gunshot wounds on his head and on different parts of his body. Results of investigation disclosed that on January 19, 2020, at about 12:10 in the afternoon, Del left their house at Prime Estate Subdivision and drove his BMW motorcycle to visit their Avida condominium unit in San Rafael, Mandurriao, Iloilo City. At about 12:17 in the afternoon, his wife received a phone call from him regarding some suspicious looking guys. His call abruptly ended and his wife returned-call Del, the latter’s mobile number was already out of reach. Soon after, the security guard at Prime Subdivision heard four (4) successive loud explosions. The security guard and Del’s wife proceeded to the foot of the bridge along Trenas Road and saw the bloodied and unconscious Del lying on the road. Del was brought to Medicus Hospital but was declared dead on arrival. Investigation revealed that the Subjects were also the ones behind the demise of Allen Muller y Secreto who was shot dead minutes earlier than Del. Witnesses of Muller’s shooting incident said that they saw a gray Adventure that stopped by near him followed by sound of series of gunshots. Verification from the Land Transportation Office (LTO) revealed the registered owner of the gray Adventure with plate number ABQ7754, who later averred that they have not been in possession of the car since January 2020 as they entered into rent-a-car business agreement with PAPO Car Rental. In the CCTV footage on the crime scene of Muller, it appeared that there were four (4) individuals inside the Mitsubishi Adventure. In Del’s crime scene, witnesses saw two (2) armed men standing near the Adventure, shooting at Del. The owner of the PAPO Car Rental stated in his sworn statement that subject JOVEN, a police officer, rented the Adventure for two (2) days or until January 20, 2020. The next day, the owner of the car rental was surprised when JOVEN asked to meet with him and during their meeting, subject JOVEN confessed that the Adventure he rented was used by his group as their get-away vehicle in killing Muller and Del. Subject JOVEN admitted that he was the driver of the group. Further, subject JOVEN said that after killing Muller, they stopped at a vacant lot in Nabitasan, La Paz to strip off the white stickers from the Adventure. Del saw and confronted them so they shot Del to death. Subject JOVEN also asked the owner of the car rental to pin one Osting Del Pilar, a drug-related target of their group, in case an investigation about the death of Muller and Del would ensue. Subject PCpl. JERRY VILLANUEVA y CARMELOTES was positively identified by one witness, a part-time taxi driver and security guard. Theft was also committed as Del’s mobile phone was not recovered from him. According to Del’s wife, he had temper for traffic violators and does not hesitate to take photographs or videos of such and post them on social media. With this, Subjects may have assumed that Del reported their activities to authorities when he made a call or that he took photos or videos of them. Hence, after inflicting several fatal wounds at Del, they took his mobile phone without his consent. As one witness also stated, he noticed that one of the shooters was trying to get something from the road after firing several shots. With the filing of the charges, the Britanico and Lao families said that this is a welcome milestone in the case of Del. In a joint statement, they said “Today, one hundred thirty days after the shooting and murder in broad daylight of our dearest husband, father, son, brother, and family member Delfin Celestial Britanico on 19 January 2020 in Iloilo City, the criminal charges of murder and theft have been filed against four (4) suspects: PCpl. Jerry Carmelotes Villanueva PCpl. Joseph Andrew Poneles Joven and Two (2) John Does We ask that the Philippine National Police immediately place the identified suspects on restrictive custody and make them face the charges filed against them”. Administrative charges shall also be filed against these suspects with the National Police Commission (Napolcom). The families said that they continue to trust that the law enforcement agencies will be able to identify and catch all involved in the gruesome crime and swiftly bring them all to justice. The families are thankful to the personnel of the National Bureau of Investigation and others who have been working on the case and continue to do so.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of four (4) individuals by the NBI- Special Action Unit (NBI-SAU) in Angeles City for illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as JOEYLYN CASTRO, VIRGILIO YALUNG, ZENIA ANDRES, and MARILYN LUCERO. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from the information that a group of individuals were about to proceed to a money changer in Angeles City to exchange the counterfeit US Dollars into Philippine Pesos. Thus, the NBI-SAU coordinated with the Payments and Currency Investigation Group, Office of the Assistant Governor, Payments and Currency Development Sub-Sector, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (PCIG-PCDSS, BSP), and the local authorities. The operatives were able to arrange a meeting through an informant, where two (2) of the subjects would bring and use the counterfeit bills. The NBI-SAU proceeded to Angeles City and closely monitored the movements of the two (2) subjects later identified as Castro and Yalung. Subjects Castro and Yalung then proceeded to a money changer where they tried to exchange the US Dollars but the money changer refused because the US Dollars were counterfeit. At this juncture, NBI-SAU approached the subjects and effected their arrest. Seized from the subjects were seventy-eight (78) pieces of counterfeit One Hundred US Dollar bills with various serial numbers. Subjects Castro and Yalung revealed to the operatives their source of the counterfeit bills, which resulted in a follow-up operation. The arrested subjects led the operatives to the house of their source in Anopol, Bamban, Tarlac where the two (2) undercover agents were met by two (2) elderly women later identified as ZENIA ANDRES and MARILYN LUCERO. Upon asking the undercover agents about the counterfeit bills, the operatives immediately apprehended them. The operatives were able to seize seventy-eight counterfeit US Dollar bills and two (2) bundles of counterfeit One Thousand Peso bills from Subjects Andres and Lucero. The seized items were presented to the Bank Officer of PCIG-PCDSS, BSP, who confirmed that the seized bills were counterfeit. The four arrested subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the Prosecutor – Department of Justice, Manila for violation of Article 168 (Illegal possession and use of false treasury or bank notes and other instruments of credit) in relation to Article 166 (Forging treasury or bank notes on other documents payable to bearer) both under the Revised Penal Code, as amended.

body: PRESS STATEMENT April 12, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE: | NBI ASSURES PUBLIC: TEMPORARY DISRUPTION OF ONLINE SERVICES DUE TO SYSTEM TRANSITION Pasay City , Philippines– The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) informs the public that its official website and several online services are currently experiencing temporary downtime due to an ongoing transition between internet service providers. Earlier today, access to the NBI website (nbi.gov.ph), including the Online Clearance Application Portal and official email services, was disrupted. According to the NBI Technology and Infrastructure Division (TIND), the interruption occurred during the agency’s migration to a new internet provider. In simple terms, the issue involves the system that directs users to the correct NBI servers online. During the transition, the connection from the previous provider was unexpectedly cut before the new system was fully activated, causing the services to go offline. The affected services include: • NBI Official Website • Online Clearance Application Portal • Internal and External Email Systems At present, NBI technical teams are working continuously to restore full service. The agency is also closely coordinating with the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) to ensure proper system configuration and prevent further disruptions. NBI Director Atty. Melvin D. Matibag assured the public that the disruption is purely technical in nature and not the result of any security breach, emphasizing that the agency’s systems remain secure. He added that teams are working around the clock to restore all services as soon as possible and appealed for the public’s patience and understanding as the NBI completes the transition toward a more stable and improved digital infrastructure. The NBI will provide updates as soon as services are fully restored. For urgent concerns, the public is advised to coordinate with the nearest NBI office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of an individual by the NBI- Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) in Del Gallego, Camarines Sur for Human Trafficking. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the subject as ANALYN PEREZ y VILLAR. Director Distor said that the operation stemmed from an information that certain bar identified as MAMALETS BAR, located at National Highway, Tumangkok, Gallego, Camarines Sur, is involved in Human Trafficking activity. Thus, on February 9, 2022, NBI-NADO operatives proceeded to the target bar to conduct an entrapment and rescue operation. The operatives were able to arrest Subject Perez “in flagrante delicto” after receiving the payment as bar fine from the undercover agent. During the operation, NBI-NADO were able to rescue six (6) trafficked victims who were offered for sexual services in exchange for a fee. Subject Perez will be charged for violation of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. 10364 (Expanded Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2021).

body: The Information Division is pleased to submit herewith the significant cases of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) for the following afore-mentioned period as follows: • On April 1, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested EDRIS BOLUG MACALABO and ARVIN BELLEZA ZAPANTA, members of a drug syndicate operating in the country, and seized Php 120 Million worth of illegal drugs in Tondo, Manila. Barely a month since the Department of Justice (DOJ) reinstated the authority of the NBI to conduct anti-illegal drugs operation, the NBI-NCR busted the two (2) members of a drug syndicate and intercepted the transport of almost 19.831 kilograms of suspected methamphetamine hydrochloride otherwise known as shabu contained in twenty four (24) plastic bags along with short and long firearms for distribution. An intelligence information was received by the NBI-NCR on March 29, 2017 that a drug syndicate headed by a certain alias “KIM” a.k.a. Boy Muslim will be transporting from Manila to Mindanao several kilograms of shabu together with several firearms. Intelligence gathering and undercover operations conducted by the NCR resulted in zeroing the specific motor vehicle to be used by the syndicate. The said vehicle, a Toyota Corolla, was traced parked along R-10 near Manila North Harbor in Tondo, Manila. During the two (2) days of stake out, two (2) male individuals, who were later identified as Subjects MACALABO and ZAPANTA riding–in-tandem on board a Yamaha motorcycle approached the said vehicle and were observed to be checking the vehicle and the surroundings until they took the car keys hidden in the exhaust muffler, opened the door and boarded the same. They were about to leave when the NBI operatives approached them. They were requested to get out of the car for inspection. Found thereat is a travel bag loaded with twenty-four (24) plastic bags, each containing crystalline substances, which yielded positive results for methamphetamine hydrochloride or shabu, with a total net weight of 19.831 kilograms with an estimated value of Php 120 Million. Also found inside the vehicle are ten (10) .45 caliber pistols, ten (10) .38 caliber revolvers, five (5) 9mm submachine guns, ten (10) 9mm magazine clips, nineteen (19) .45 caliber magazines, four (4) suppressors for 9mm, and thirty (30) 9mm live ammunitions. Subjects failed to provide documents and permits on the said items when being asked for. The operation was conducted in collaboration with the PDEA. The drug syndicate primarily operates in the City of Manila and nearby provinces like Cavite, and transports the drugs and firearms to Mindanao. The registered owner of the vehicle is being verified with the LTO for workable leads against other members of the syndicate. Charges for violation of R.A. 9165 (Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2012) and violation of R.A. 10591 (Comprehensive Firearmss and Ammunition Regulation Act) were filed against Subjects MACALABO and ZAPANTA. Follow up operations are still being conducted to determine the identity of the mastermind and source as well as the distributor and seller in the province. • On April 4, 2017, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) arrested three (3) British nationals, namely: ANDREW ROBSON, GRAHAM ALLAN BENNET, and DOMINIC WHELLAMS for selling non-existent bonds, securities, debentures, and similar products to non- suspecting investors outside the Philippines. Informant, who provided information which led to the application of search warrant, testified before the issuing court the high pressure tactics employed by the company named PLUSTEL SOLUTIONS INC. in selling non-existent bonds, securities, debentures and similar products. Prospective investors were usually chosen from engineering, oil and gas and manufacturing industries. Initial contact through the telephone was made by tele qualifiers to assess prospective victim’s financial capacity and willingness to invest. Favorable result will be forwarded to the verifiers who gauge the probability of an investment to sign up. Encoding follows wherein financial information will be forwarded to the loaders who will ensure that the investor parts with their money in exchange for non-existent securities to their damage and prejudice. Previous verification with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) revealed that the PLUSTEL lacks authority to offer securities there being no prior application for secondary license from the Commission. On the above-mentioned date, the search warrant for violation of the Securities Regulation Code in relation to the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012 (R.A. 8799 in rel. to R.A. 10175) was issued by Executive Judge Cynthia R. Mariño-Ricablanca, Fourth Judicial Region, Sta. Cruz, Laguna pursuant to the application initiated by the NBI-IOD in close coordination with the Enforcement and Investor Protection Department of the SEC, against the premises of PLUSTEL SOLUTIONS INC. located in Brgy. Maduya, Carmona, Cavite. Incident to the implementation, the three (3) British nationals were arrested. Thirty five (35) other Filipino personnel who were caught in the act of selling securities, were apprehended. One hundred seventy two (172) other individuals working as data miners, qualifiers, and verifiers were brought to the NBI for investigation and verification. • On April 4, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested AIRA ENRIQUEZ y SORIAGA and ROBERT TESORERO y ALAUREN for fraud. The case stemmed from a complainant who alleged that sometime in February 2017, after attending a seminar conducted by Major General Galma Jeremiah Arcilla of the Transnational Anti-Organized Crime Intelligence Group (TAOC-IG) in Zamboanga City, participants were asked by Gen. Arcilla if they want to work in the government because he might be of help. On February 24, 2017, complainant went to Marco Polo Hotel in Davao City with other applicants coming from Luzon, Zambales and Manila. Subject ENRIQUEZ interviewed him and claimed that her boss, Alma Carreon is the little President of Malacañang, will soon interview him with the assurance that he will be appointed soon. While waiting for Alma Carreon, he was informed that Subject ENRIQUEZ was asking Php 20,000.00 from each applicant to defray her expenses and that of ALMA CARREON. The next day, Alma Carreon arrived at the lobby of Marco Polo Hotel where complainant was interviewed and was assured of his appointment. Complainant then gave the Php 20,000.00 to Subject ENRIQUEZ who received the same but did not issue any receipt. Complainant even promised that President Duterte would interview him but never materialized. Alma Carreon instead conducted the final interview and assure him to just wait for his appointment and oath taking. Recently, Subject ENRIQUEZ sent complainant via email that his application has already been received by the Office of the President and thereafter demanded Php 10,000.00 as budget to facilitate his application. This led to the entrapment operation and arrest of Subjects AIRA ENRIQUEZ and ROBERT TESORERO. Per certification issued by the Human Resource Management Office of the Office of the President, Subjects AIRA ENRIQUEZ, ALMA S. CARREON, and ROBERT TESORERO are not employed in any capacity with the Office of the President. Record check conducted also revealed derogatory records against Subject AIRA ENRIQUEZ who was previously charged for Carnapping, Estafa and other deceits. The Subjects, including ALMA CARREON (at large) have been charged before the Department of Justice for Usurpation of Authority or Official functions and Estafa under Article 177 and Article 315 par.2(a) of the Revised Penal code, respectively. • On April 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested LARRY SANTIAGO y ADLAWAN, MARK JUNE DELA CRUZ y SANTIAGO, JOEMAR DELVO y WANSON, and LEVY MANLAPAS y FRANCISCO for oil pilferage in Navotas City. Based on an intelligence report, alleged illegal activities were being perpetrated by a group of persons headed by a certain alias “RUBY ANNE” or “ROVY ANNE”. The group operates in the area of Tangos, Navotas City. Acting on the report, AOTCD operatives, together with CIIS-Bureau of Customs operatives, proceeded to monitor said illegal activities. The Subjects were caught in the act of unloading/selling petroleum products on board their motorized banca. As the operatives approached the banca, the buyer-banca immediately left. Found left in banca were ten (10) empty containers and four (4) containers filled with diesel. The subject-banca was later identified as owned by LEVY MANLAPAS. When operatives proceeded to the residence of Subject LEVY MANLAPAS, several more containers of petroleum products were found. When asked for their license to operate, he failed to produce any, resulting in their arrest and seizure of the products. Verification with the Department of Energy (DOE) showed that Subject has no approved license to operate. Charges for violation of Batas Pambansa Blg. 33 also known as Oil Pilferage Law, as amended by Presidential Decree No. 1865, were charged against the Subjects before the Office of the Special Prosecutor of Navotas City. • On April 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested HENRY FLORES JR. y CORDETA for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Game). The case stemmed from an intelligence report disclosing a rampant proliferation of “Last Two”, an illegal numbers in Davao City and nearby areas. On the aforementioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject FLORES who owns and manages a store in Panacan, Davao City where illegal number game operates. Number games used and unused tally sheets, stub receipts and number games paraphernalia were recovered from the Subject. Subject was brought to NBI-SEMRO office where he underwent proper booking procedures. He was thereafter presented to the Office of the City Prosecutor of Davao City for inquest proceedings. • On April 4 and 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized several counterfeit Tory Burch products as well as counterfeit Apple, Beats and Skullcandy products with an approximate value of Php 34,317,000.00, Php 77,724,000.00, and Php 708, 000.00 respectively. The case stemmed from a complaint of Lee Bumgarner Inc., (LBI) requesting on behalf of their clients Tory Burch, Apple, Beats, and Skullcandy, for an investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of their fake products in Metro Manila. Fake items were seized in Binondo, Sta. Cruz, and Quiapo, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines were filed against John/Jane Doe and owners/lessees/occupants/operators/managers of various stores and stalls located in 168 Shopping Mall in Binondo, Manila and Carriedo St., Quiapo, Manila. • On April 6, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested twenty four (24) individuals namely BERNARDITO MISOLA y MENOR, MARVIN MANA y RAMOS, PRUDENCIO BALELIN y MORANA, EFREN BALELIN y MESA, ALVIN DELA VEGA y BANAAG, JEOFFREY ELAOG y MORADOS, BENJAMIN MANIS y MITRAN, JULIO NATUPLAG y ALINDAYO, ELPIDIO BALELIN y MESA, REYNALDO BERNAL y DE JUAN, ROMELITO MORTEL y MENDOZA MARK RENE GLENOGO, WILFREDO MITRAN, SHERSIN MILLADO y MERCED, BRIAN VALENTINO y MUEGA, FREDDY TUMAMAO y MONTERO, PAULO ASPURIA y CARINO, GLEN ELAOG y MESIA, ROGELIO DULAY y DOTIMAS, JOSHUA AURE y BARTIDO, ARCHIE BALELING y BARRERA, DAN BERNAL y ESPINOSA, LEO JAMES ZULUETA, and ROSBERT ECLEVIA y HERMOSO for illegally hauling mineral ore. On April 4, 2017, DENR Undersecretary Arturo Valdez, Head of National Anti-Environmental Crime Task Force (NAECTF) sent a letter-notice to the NBI requesting for investigative assistance and manpower to stop illegal hauling of minerals and/or nickel ore stockpiles in Zambales. Acting on the request, NBI-ENCD operatives proceeded to the province of Zambales to conduct surveillance operations. It was found out that trucks loaded with minerals i.e. nickel ore were being transported from mining areas to either Brgy. Guisguis, Lucapon South and Guinabon, all of Sta. Cruz town or to Binabalian Port, Candelaria, Zambales. Despite the fact that there was already a cancellation of the Mining Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) of these mining firms, and the subsequent stoppage order by Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB-Region III) dated March 28, 2017, these aforestated mining firms continue to extract nickel ores from their respective mining sites and transporting them to their stockpile sites. A joint operation of NBI-ENCD operatives, members of the DENR-NAECTF, MGB-Region III, representatives from Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Philippine National Police (PNP) and the Philippine Army (PA) was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in flagrante in the act of hauling minerals and/or nickel ores. Seized items including dump trucks used in the illegal hauling, barge/vessels, excavators/backhoes, and nickel ores stockpiles were duly turned over to MGB. Charges for violation of Section 103 of R.A 7942 (the Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed against the Subjects. • On April 10, 2017, operatives of Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested MARY GRACE LAURENCIO for Estafa. The case stemmed from a complaint of Jacqueline Lourdes M. De Guzman against the Subject. Complainant alleged that Subject collected amount of money from the complainant for the latter’s payment of quarterly income tax and monthly percentage tax from 2008 to present. However, upon verification, it was found out that Subject never paid any of complainant’s tax dues to BIR since 2008. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the subject who was caught in flagrante delicto counting the marked money given by the complainant. Subject was detained in NBI detention cell and was presented for inquest proceedings on April 11, 2017. • On April 10, 2017, operatives of NBI-Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO), rescued three (3) infants, namely: ANGEL MAE SALAZAR (11 mos.), ZACHARY MASON SALAZAR (8 mos.), and CANDELARIO SALAZAR (11 mos.) from the custody of their foster parents RUTH BORJA-SALAZAR and JOHN ROBERT SALAZAR (Mexican-American). According to Jenilyn Bautista, one of the helpers of the spouses Salazar, last March 2017, during a heated argument, Ruth suddenly choked one of the infants, while last April 2, 2017, the three infants were forced to eat fresh camote leaves instead of milk. On April 6, 2017, Melchie S. Franco, RSW-area social worker, conducted a physical inspection and asked for the birth certificate of the infants. Ruth admitted that she adopted the three infants and that two of the infants have birth certificates while the other does not have one. However, upon verification made by the Area Social Worker, two infants (Zachary and Candelario) do not have birth certificates while the documents of the other one (Angel) are questionable for alleged Simulation of Births. Furthermore, there was no record for the application being lodged by Ruth for the aforesaid adoption. Thereafter, a rescue operation was conducted. The infants were brought to the nearest hospital for physical and medical check up. The infants were in the custody of City Social Welfare Office of General Santos City. Investigation against the spouses Salazar for alleged violation of Sec.21 (i)(ii) of Adoption Act of 1998, R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse Law) and simulation of births defined and penalized in Article 347 of the Revised Penal Code as amended, is ongoing. • On April 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 17, 520 pieces of assorted Nivea and Victoria’s Secret products with an estimated amount of Eight Million Four Thousand Pesos (Php 8,004,000.00) in Tondo, Manila. The case stemmed from a complaint of Mr. Jaime S. Dela Cruz of I-Data Consolidators, Inc. on behalf of Nivea and Victoria’s Secret against Justine Lim and any of the owners/officers/employees of a business establishment located at V Tower Building, 1257 Dagupan St., Tondo, Manila. On the aforementioned date, Judge Maria Victoria A. Soriano-Villadolid, Branch 24, Manila issued Search Warrant against the Subjects. NBI-IPRD operatives, with proper coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), proceeded to the target area and implemented the Search Warrant. The search conducted yielded positive results and seized items were reflected in the Receipt/Inventory of Property Seized. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against the Subjects. • On April 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO in an entrapment operation in Bonifacio Global City in Taguig City for alleged Swindling. The case stemmed from a complaint of Japanese businessman Musashi Nagashima against ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO and MARIA ELVISA DACLAN TABAR. According to Nagashima, Subjects made representations to him that they own a company named GOSHEN CAPITAL HOLDINGS LIMITED that wants to fund the construction of Davao Metro Link Train and that they want to invite Japanese general contractors to implement the project. Subjects even presented that GOSHEN has 5 Billion US Dollars deposit in HSBC account in hongkong and showed a certification on the said deposit purportedly issued by certain Bernadette S. Lim, HSBC Assistant Vice President Trade Operations. Subjects told Nagashima that he needs to pay first US$150,000 (later reduced to US$120,000) bank charges to facilitate the transfer of said deposit to complainant’s employer in Japan. It was agreed that Subjects will cause the initial transfer of US$ 10 Million to Nagashima’s employer to cover the mobilization and feasibility study of the project. Subjects even offered to shoulder half (US$60,000). Convinced by Subjects’ representations, Nagashima shelled out from from his own money US$ 40,000 while US$20,000 was shouldered by his friend. After which, Subjects showed another set of documents issued by HSBC detailing the transaction on the bank transfer of US$10 Million from GOSHEN to complainant’s employer in Japan. Subjects even charged Nagashima Php 150,000 just for a copy of the transaction details. After verification with his employer in Japan, Nagashima found out that there is no such bank transfer and that bank communications and documents purportedly issued by HSBC are all spurious. This prompted Nagashima to seek assistance of the NBI. An entrapment operation was then set resulting in the arrest of Subject ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO. Subject MARIA ELVISA DACLAN TABAR remains at large since she was not present during the operation. Charges for Estafa through Falsification of Commercial Documents were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor in Taguig. • On April 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JESSIE SUANSING y REYES, NOLLY CARAJASAN y PAGAS and STEPHANIE TAGYAMON y CA for violation of R.A. 10175 and Estafa. An entrapment operation to apprehend the Subjects was conducted pursuant to the complaint of Juanita Tan and Kate Neave against the Subjects who are responsible in hacking the Facebook account of complainant Tan, which was used to dupe her FB friends, particularly complainant Neave. Subjects were apprehended after claiming the money from Palawan Express Pera Padala. Charges are now readied against the Subjects for inquest proceedings. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) arrested KIMBERLY TROFEO-DOLORICO in a buy-bust operation in Malate, Manila. On April 4, 2017, Complainant MAXIMO S. OCAMPO, General Manager of Didymus Business Propriety Support Services requested for the assistance in the apprehension and prosecution of those suspected in dealing with drug bearing counterfeit of the SINEMET mark, for and in behalf of their client MERCK SHARP & DOHME CORP., owner of the SINEMET mark. Subject was arrested in a buy bust operation after she made arrangements with the Complainant to sell SINEMET and other medicine brands. In the affidavit submitted by the Complainant, it was reported that Subject was selling counterfeit SINEMET without the authority from MERCK SHARP & DOHME CORP. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Subject. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested RENY REVIL y ORIDA and BONIFACIO RONQUILLO y SULICAR for illegal gambling. On April 10, 2017, NBI-DIPDO received information from confidential informant that illegal gambling/numbers game “suertres” is rampant in the City of Oroquietta, Misamis Occidental. Acting on the said information, surveillance and bet-bust operation were conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were brought to NBI-DIPDO for the booking procedures. Subsequently, Subjects were brought before the Office of the Honorable City Prosecutor, Oroquietta City, Misamis Occidental for inquest proceedings. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested thirteen (13) individuals namely MELECIO BOYLES BARAJAN. CRISANTO GUCOR ONCADA, INGKING BOLACOY LUCENA, DAISY ESCOLANO DEVINO, KARL JOHN GUILLERMO CASTILLO, JONATHAN GALURA KARAAN, PEPITO NIASCA LAGING JR., DANTE LUMAYAG CELLAN, RUSSELL BOISER CARCALLAS, MICHOLE KEATH UCANG TAAGAMO, MARILY BARRO CUTIN ALFREDO ANNA ESTOSE, and HERO REY MILLANA CENABRE for illegal gambling. On the aforementioned date, Judge Jennifer Chavez-Marcos, Branch 2, RTC Bohol issued a Search Warrant against PF3 GAMES AND ENTERTAINMENT CORPORATION and its incorporators and employees for violations under P.D. 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties on Illegal Gambling) in relation to R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing Penalties for Illegal Numbers and Games). NBI-BOHDo operatives served the Search Warrant inside a Small Town Lottery Outlet of PF3 Games & Entertainment Corp in a peaceful and orderly manner. The test bet and surveillance also posted positive result that said STL outlet is accepting bets for local Bohol Tres and National Suertres). Searches made was found positive on alleged illegal number games paraphernalia or implements. After positive searches and seizures of pieces of evidence, above-mentioned Subjects were arrested. Subjects were brought to NBI-BOHDO for custody and booking procedures. They were subsequently brought to Tagbilaran City Prosecution Office for inquest proceedings, and the Search Warrant was returned to the Honorable issuing court. • On April 19, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested KRISTOPER LABORES y LABEYNI, ROLLY TULALAY y REYES, CHARISE CABINGAS y YBAÑES, LIEZEL INMENZO y AGUILAR, and FRITZ ANN INMENZO y TAMAYOSA for illegally selling corals and other endangered species. Subjects were arrested after being caught in the act of illegally possessing and selling corals and other endangered species in Cartimar Shopping Center, Pasay City. A total of seven (7) erring establishments were confirmed to be engaged in illegal possession and selling corals and other aquatic wildlife species. A total of two thousand four hundred twenty five (2,425) corals and twenty (20) pieces endangered species like giant clams and seahorses were seized during the operation. The recovered specimens were properly turned over to Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR). A joint operation of NBI-IOD and NBI-IPRD was then formed resulting in the arrest of the Subject in Bacolod City. Subject was brought to NBI-Bacolod District Office where he underwent booking procedures. Later on, he was brought to NBI Manila for another booking procedure. A return of Warrant of Arrest was made with the court in compliance with the Court’s order. Subject GAMUYAO is temporarily detained in NBI Detention Center awaiting for the Court’s commitment order. • On April 24, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG a.k.a. SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ who has an outstanding warrant of arrest for three (3) counts of rape. NBI-AFD received a call from the office of SHAUN GAVIN, Attache, US Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service, US Embassy, Manila requesting for assistance to conduct an investigation on the person named SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ, a US Visa applicant. The US Embassy-Manila database reveals that JEMENEZ has fingerprint and photograph that match to a previous visa applicant named JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG. Further verification also revealed that DAGDAG has an outstanding warrant of arrest for three (3) counts of rape issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 9, La Trinidad, Benguet. Immediately thereafter, NBI-AFD operatives proceeded to the US Embassy, Manila and met the officials from the Overseas Criminal Investigation (OCI). After which, they turned over SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ. He was then brought to the NBI for further investigation. JEMENEZ claimed he was not JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG and he presented numerous documents to prove his identity as SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ. He also stated that he was an orphan that is why his birth certificate was registered late and that the claim against him is ridiculous because for many years, he had work as an OFW in Saudi Arabia. However, after thorough tactical interrogation, SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ later on admitted that he is JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG. He started assuming the identity of SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ sometime in 2009 when a case for rape was filed against him, and when he was still processing his documents as OFW in Saudi Arabia. NBI-ICTD furnished a copy of an NBI clearance under the name of JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG bearing the photograph of the Subject. Record check conducted on the name of JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG reveals that Subject is wanted for the (3) counts of rape filed in RTC 9, La Trinidad, Benguet and wanted for rape filed in RTC IV, Baguio City. Charges for multiple counts of Falsification of Public Documents and Illegal Use of Alias were filed against the Subject. • On April 25, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested MICAELA AYUBO TEMPOROSA for illegal practice of medicine. The case stemmed from a complaint of Renalyn Ordaniel Y Gavasan against the Subject. An entrapment operation to apprehend the Subject was conducted in Circumferential Road, Bacolod City when Subject was caught in flagrante engaging in the illegal practice of medicine by issuing a prescription to a poseur patient. Subject was brought to NBI-BACDO for the usual booking procedures. She was thereafter brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor for inquest proceedings for violation of Sec.10 of R.A. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959).

This led to the entrapment operation and arrest of Subjects AIRA ENRIQUEZ and ROBERT TESORERO. CARREON, and ROBERT TESORERO are not employed in any capacity with the Office of the President. Record check conducted also revealed derogatory records against Subject AIRA ENRIQUEZ who was previously charged for Carnapping, Estafa and other deceits. The Subjects, including ALMA CARREON (at large) have been charged before the Department of Justice for Usurpation of Authority or Official functions and Estafa under Article 177 and Article 315 par.2(a) of the Revised Penal code, respectively. • On April 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) arrested LARRY SANTIAGO y ADLAWAN, MARK JUNE DELA CRUZ y SANTIAGO, JOEMAR DELVO y WANSON, and LEVY MANLAPAS y FRANCISCO for oil pilferage in Navotas City. Based on an intelligence report, alleged illegal activities were being perpetrated by a group of persons headed by a certain alias “RUBY ANNE” or “ROVY ANNE”. The group operates in the area of Tangos, Navotas City. Acting on the report, AOTCD operatives, together with CIIS-Bureau of Customs operatives, proceeded to monitor said illegal activities. The Subjects were caught in the act of unloading/selling petroleum products on board their motorized banca. As the operatives approached the banca, the buyer-banca immediately left. Found left in banca were ten (10) empty containers and four (4) containers filled with diesel. The subject-banca was later identified as owned by LEVY MANLAPAS. When operatives proceeded to the residence of Subject LEVY MANLAPAS, several more containers of petroleum products were found. When asked for their license to operate, he failed to produce any, resulting in their arrest and seizure of the products. Verification with the Department of Energy (DOE) showed that Subject has no approved license to operate. Charges for violation of Batas Pambansa Blg. 33 also known as Oil Pilferage Law, as amended by Presidential Decree No. 1865, were charged against the Subjects before the Office of the Special Prosecutor of Navotas City. • On April 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested HENRY FLORES JR. y CORDETA for violation of R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing the Penalties for Illegal Numbers Game). The case stemmed from an intelligence report disclosing a rampant proliferation of “Last Two”, an illegal numbers in Davao City and nearby areas. On the aforementioned date, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of Subject FLORES who owns and manages a store in Panacan, Davao City where illegal number game operates. Number games used and unused tally sheets, stub receipts and number games paraphernalia were recovered from the Subject. Subject was brought to NBI-SEMRO office where he underwent proper booking procedures. He was thereafter presented to the Office of the City Prosecutor of Davao City for inquest proceedings. • On April 4 and 5, 2017, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) seized several counterfeit Tory Burch products as well as counterfeit Apple, Beats and Skullcandy products with an approximate value of Php 34,317,000.00, Php 77,724,000.00, and Php 708, 000.00 respectively. The case stemmed from a complaint of Lee Bumgarner Inc., (LBI) requesting on behalf of their clients Tory Burch, Apple, Beats, and Skullcandy, for an investigation and enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of their fake products in Metro Manila. Fake items were seized in Binondo, Sta. Cruz, and Quiapo, Manila. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines were filed against John/Jane Doe and owners/lessees/occupants/operators/managers of various stores and stalls located in 168 Shopping Mall in Binondo, Manila and Carriedo St., Quiapo, Manila. • On April 6, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested twenty four (24) individuals namely BERNARDITO MISOLA y MENOR, MARVIN MANA y RAMOS, PRUDENCIO BALELIN y MORANA, EFREN BALELIN y MESA, ALVIN DELA VEGA y BANAAG, JEOFFREY ELAOG y MORADOS, BENJAMIN MANIS y MITRAN, JULIO NATUPLAG y ALINDAYO, ELPIDIO BALELIN y MESA, REYNALDO BERNAL y DE JUAN, ROMELITO MORTEL y MENDOZA MARK RENE GLENOGO, WILFREDO MITRAN, SHERSIN MILLADO y MERCED, BRIAN VALENTINO y MUEGA, FREDDY TUMAMAO y MONTERO, PAULO ASPURIA y CARINO, GLEN ELAOG y MESIA, ROGELIO DULAY y DOTIMAS, JOSHUA AURE y BARTIDO, ARCHIE BALELING y BARRERA, DAN BERNAL y ESPINOSA, LEO JAMES ZULUETA, and ROSBERT ECLEVIA y HERMOSO for illegally hauling mineral ore. On April 4, 2017, DENR Undersecretary Arturo Valdez, Head of National Anti-Environmental Crime Task Force (NAECTF) sent a letter-notice to the NBI requesting for investigative assistance and manpower to stop illegal hauling of minerals and/or nickel ore stockpiles in Zambales. Acting on the request, NBI-ENCD operatives proceeded to the province of Zambales to conduct surveillance operations. It was found out that trucks loaded with minerals i.e. nickel ore were being transported from mining areas to either Brgy. Guisguis, Lucapon South and Guinabon, all of Sta. Cruz town or to Binabalian Port, Candelaria, Zambales. Despite the fact that there was already a cancellation of the Mining Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) of these mining firms, and the subsequent stoppage order by Mines and Geosciences Bureau (MGB-Region III) dated March 28, 2017, these aforestated mining firms continue to extract nickel ores from their respective mining sites and transporting them to their stockpile sites. A joint operation of NBI-ENCD operatives, members of the DENR-NAECTF, MGB-Region III, representatives from Philippine Coast Guard (PCG), Philippine National Police (PNP) and the Philippine Army (PA) was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the above-mentioned Subjects who were caught in flagrante in the act of hauling minerals and/or nickel ores. Seized items including dump trucks used in the illegal hauling, barge/vessels, excavators/backhoes, and nickel ores stockpiles were duly turned over to MGB. Charges for violation of Section 103 of R.A 7942 (the Philippine Mining Act of 1995) were filed against the Subjects. • On April 10, 2017, operatives of Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested MARY GRACE LAURENCIO for Estafa. The case stemmed from a complaint of Jacqueline Lourdes M. De Guzman against the Subject. Complainant alleged that Subject collected amount of money from the complainant for the latter’s payment of quarterly income tax and monthly percentage tax from 2008 to present. However, upon verification, it was found out that Subject never paid any of complainant’s tax dues to BIR since 2008. An entrapment operation was then conducted resulting in the arrest of the subject who was caught in flagrante delicto counting the marked money given by the complainant. Subject was detained in NBI detention cell and was presented for inquest proceedings on April 11, 2017. • On April 10, 2017, operatives of NBI-Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO), rescued three (3) infants, namely: ANGEL MAE SALAZAR (11 mos.), ZACHARY MASON SALAZAR (8 mos.), and CANDELARIO SALAZAR (11 mos.) from the custody of their foster parents RUTH BORJA-SALAZAR and JOHN ROBERT SALAZAR (Mexican-American). According to Jenilyn Bautista, one of the helpers of the spouses Salazar, last March 2017, during a heated argument, Ruth suddenly choked one of the infants, while last April 2, 2017, the three infants were forced to eat fresh camote leaves instead of milk. On April 6, 2017, Melchie S. Franco, RSW-area social worker, conducted a physical inspection and asked for the birth certificate of the infants. Ruth admitted that she adopted the three infants and that two of the infants have birth certificates while the other does not have one. However, upon verification made by the Area Social Worker, two infants (Zachary and Candelario) do not have birth certificates while the documents of the other one (Angel) are questionable for alleged Simulation of Births. Furthermore, there was no record for the application being lodged by Ruth for the aforesaid adoption. Thereafter, a rescue operation was conducted. The infants were brought to the nearest hospital for physical and medical check up. The infants were in the custody of City Social Welfare Office of General Santos City. Investigation against the spouses Salazar for alleged violation of Sec.21 (i)(ii) of Adoption Act of 1998, R.A. 7610 (Child Abuse Law) and simulation of births defined and penalized in Article 347 of the Revised Penal Code as amended, is ongoing. • On April 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) seized 17, 520 pieces of assorted Nivea and Victoria’s Secret products with an estimated amount of Eight Million Four Thousand Pesos (Php 8,004,000.00) in Tondo, Manila. The case stemmed from a complaint of Mr. Jaime S. Dela Cruz of I-Data Consolidators, Inc. on behalf of Nivea and Victoria’s Secret against Justine Lim and any of the owners/officers/employees of a business establishment located at V Tower Building, 1257 Dagupan St., Tondo, Manila. On the aforementioned date, Judge Maria Victoria A. Soriano-Villadolid, Branch 24, Manila issued Search Warrant against the Subjects. NBI-IPRD operatives, with proper coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), proceeded to the target area and implemented the Search Warrant. The search conducted yielded positive results and seized items were reflected in the Receipt/Inventory of Property Seized. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 were filed against the Subjects. • On April 11, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Graft Division (NBI-AGD) arrested ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO in an entrapment operation in Bonifacio Global City in Taguig City for alleged Swindling. The case stemmed from a complaint of Japanese businessman Musashi Nagashima against ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO and MARIA ELVISA DACLAN TABAR. According to Nagashima, Subjects made representations to him that they own a company named GOSHEN CAPITAL HOLDINGS LIMITED that wants to fund the construction of Davao Metro Link Train and that they want to invite Japanese general contractors to implement the project. Subjects even presented that GOSHEN has 5 Billion US Dollars deposit in HSBC account in hongkong and showed a certification on the said deposit purportedly issued by certain Bernadette S. Lim, HSBC Assistant Vice President Trade Operations. Subjects told Nagashima that he needs to pay first US$150,000 (later reduced to US$120,000) bank charges to facilitate the transfer of said deposit to complainant’s employer in Japan. It was agreed that Subjects will cause the initial transfer of US$ 10 Million to Nagashima’s employer to cover the mobilization and feasibility study of the project. Subjects even offered to shoulder half (US$60,000). Convinced by Subjects’ representations, Nagashima shelled out from from his own money US$ 40,000 while US$20,000 was shouldered by his friend. After which, Subjects showed another set of documents issued by HSBC detailing the transaction on the bank transfer of US$10 Million from GOSHEN to complainant’s employer in Japan. Subjects even charged Nagashima Php 150,000 just for a copy of the transaction details. After verification with his employer in Japan, Nagashima found out that there is no such bank transfer and that bank communications and documents purportedly issued by HSBC are all spurious. This prompted Nagashima to seek assistance of the NBI. An entrapment operation was then set resulting in the arrest of Subject ANSELMO MONREAL NOLASCO. Subject MARIA ELVISA DACLAN TABAR remains at large since she was not present during the operation. Charges for Estafa through Falsification of Commercial Documents were filed against the Subject before the Office of the Prosecutor in Taguig. • On April 17, 2017, operatives of NBI-Southeastern Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-SEMRO) arrested JESSIE SUANSING y REYES, NOLLY CARAJASAN y PAGAS and STEPHANIE TAGYAMON y CA for violation of R.A. 10175 and Estafa. An entrapment operation to apprehend the Subjects was conducted pursuant to the complaint of Juanita Tan and Kate Neave against the Subjects who are responsible in hacking the Facebook account of complainant Tan, which was used to dupe her FB friends, particularly complainant Neave. Subjects were apprehended after claiming the money from Palawan Express Pera Padala. Charges are now readied against the Subjects for inquest proceedings. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) arrested KIMBERLY TROFEO-DOLORICO in a buy-bust operation in Malate, Manila. On April 4, 2017, Complainant MAXIMO S. OCAMPO, General Manager of Didymus Business Propriety Support Services requested for the assistance in the apprehension and prosecution of those suspected in dealing with drug bearing counterfeit of the SINEMET mark, for and in behalf of their client MERCK SHARP & DOHME CORP., owner of the SINEMET mark. Subject was arrested in a buy bust operation after she made arrangements with the Complainant to sell SINEMET and other medicine brands. In the affidavit submitted by the Complainant, it was reported that Subject was selling counterfeit SINEMET without the authority from MERCK SHARP & DOHME CORP. Charges for violation of R.A. 8293 (Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines) were filed against the Subject. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Dipolog District Office (NBI-DIPDO) arrested RENY REVIL y ORIDA and BONIFACIO RONQUILLO y SULICAR for illegal gambling. On April 10, 2017, NBI-DIPDO received information from confidential informant that illegal gambling/numbers game “suertres” is rampant in the City of Oroquietta, Misamis Occidental. Acting on the said information, surveillance and bet-bust operation were conducted resulting in the arrest of the Subjects. Subjects were brought to NBI-DIPDO for the booking procedures. Subsequently, Subjects were brought before the Office of the Honorable City Prosecutor, Oroquietta City, Misamis Occidental for inquest proceedings. • On April 18, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bohol District Office (NBI-BOHDO) arrested thirteen (13) individuals namely MELECIO BOYLES BARAJAN. CRISANTO GUCOR ONCADA, INGKING BOLACOY LUCENA, DAISY ESCOLANO DEVINO, KARL JOHN GUILLERMO CASTILLO, JONATHAN GALURA KARAAN, PEPITO NIASCA LAGING JR., DANTE LUMAYAG CELLAN, RUSSELL BOISER CARCALLAS, MICHOLE KEATH UCANG TAAGAMO, MARILY BARRO CUTIN ALFREDO ANNA ESTOSE, and HERO REY MILLANA CENABRE for illegal gambling. On the aforementioned date, Judge Jennifer Chavez-Marcos, Branch 2, RTC Bohol issued a Search Warrant against PF3 GAMES AND ENTERTAINMENT CORPORATION and its incorporators and employees for violations under P.D. 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties on Illegal Gambling) in relation to R.A. 9287 (An Act Increasing Penalties for Illegal Numbers and Games). NBI-BOHDo operatives served the Search Warrant inside a Small Town Lottery Outlet of PF3 Games & Entertainment Corp in a peaceful and orderly manner. The test bet and surveillance also posted positive result that said STL outlet is accepting bets for local Bohol Tres and National Suertres). Searches made was found positive on alleged illegal number games paraphernalia or implements. After positive searches and seizures of pieces of evidence, above-mentioned Subjects were arrested. Subjects were brought to NBI-BOHDO for custody and booking procedures. They were subsequently brought to Tagbilaran City Prosecution Office for inquest proceedings, and the Search Warrant was returned to the Honorable issuing court. • On April 19, 2017, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-ENCD) arrested KRISTOPER LABORES y LABEYNI, ROLLY TULALAY y REYES, CHARISE CABINGAS y YBAÑES, LIEZEL INMENZO y AGUILAR, and FRITZ ANN INMENZO y TAMAYOSA for illegally selling corals and other endangered species. Subjects were arrested after being caught in the act of illegally possessing and selling corals and other endangered species in Cartimar Shopping Center, Pasay City. A total of seven (7) erring establishments were confirmed to be engaged in illegal possession and selling corals and other aquatic wildlife species. A total of two thousand four hundred twenty five (2,425) corals and twenty (20) pieces endangered species like giant clams and seahorses were seized during the operation. The recovered specimens were properly turned over to Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR). Charges for violation of Section 96 and 102 of R.A. 8550 as amended by R.A. 10654 (An Act to Prevent, Deter, and Eliminate Illegal, Unreported and Unregulated Fishing, Amending R.A. 8550 (The Philippine Fisheries Code of 1998) were filed against the Subjects. • On April 19, 2017, operatives of NBI-International Operations Division (NBI-IOD) and NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD) arrested RODOLFO “BOY” GAMUYAO for the crime of Murder. Subject, a former Philippine Constabulary Officer and a retired Police Officer 3 (PO3) had gone into hiding and had remained at large in order to evade arrest and prosecution right after the Regional Trial Court, Branch 54, Bacolod City issued on July 1, 1992 a (No Bail) Warrant of Arrest against him for the crime of Murder. Intelligence information disclosed that Subject and his group are engaged in illegal activities such as gun running of high-powered firearms and drug distribution in Region VI. After a series of discreet investigation, NBI operatives were able to confirm from informants that Subject used to hang out with former PC officers in some areas in Ilo-Ilo, Bacolod and Guimaras. A joint operation of NBI-IOD and NBI-IPRD was then formed resulting in the arrest of the Subject in Bacolod City. Subject was brought to NBI-Bacolod District Office where he underwent booking procedures. Later on, he was brought to NBI Manila for another booking procedure. A return of Warrant of Arrest was made with the court in compliance with the Court’s order. Subject GAMUYAO is temporarily detained in NBI Detention Center awaiting for the Court’s commitment order. • On April 24, 2017, operatives of NBI-Anti-Fraud Division (NBI-AFD) arrested JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG a.k.a. SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ who has an outstanding warrant of arrest for three (3) counts of rape. NBI-AFD received a call from the office of SHAUN GAVIN, Attache, US Department of State, Diplomatic Security Service, US Embassy, Manila requesting for assistance to conduct an investigation on the person named SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ, a US Visa applicant. The US Embassy-Manila database reveals that JEMENEZ has fingerprint and photograph that match to a previous visa applicant named JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG. Further verification also revealed that DAGDAG has an outstanding warrant of arrest for three (3) counts of rape issued by the Regional Trial Court, Branch 9, La Trinidad, Benguet. Immediately thereafter, NBI-AFD operatives proceeded to the US Embassy, Manila and met the officials from the Overseas Criminal Investigation (OCI). After which, they turned over SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ. He was then brought to the NBI for further investigation. JEMENEZ claimed he was not JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG and he presented numerous documents to prove his identity as SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ. He also stated that he was an orphan that is why his birth certificate was registered late and that the claim against him is ridiculous because for many years, he had work as an OFW in Saudi Arabia. However, after thorough tactical interrogation, SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ later on admitted that he is JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG. He started assuming the identity of SHAWNE ORANI JEMENEZ sometime in 2009 when a case for rape was filed against him, and when he was still processing his documents as OFW in Saudi Arabia. NBI-ICTD furnished a copy of an NBI clearance under the name of JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG bearing the photograph of the Subject. Record check conducted on the name of JULIUS AMISTOSO DAGDAG reveals that Subject is wanted for the (3) counts of rape filed in RTC 9, La Trinidad, Benguet and wanted for rape filed in RTC IV, Baguio City. Charges for multiple counts of Falsification of Public Documents and Illegal Use of Alias were filed against the Subject. • On April 25, 2017, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested MICAELA AYUBO TEMPOROSA for illegal practice of medicine. The case stemmed from a complaint of Renalyn Ordaniel Y Gavasan against the Subject. An entrapment operation to apprehend the Subject was conducted in Circumferential Road, Bacolod City when Subject was caught in flagrante engaging in the illegal practice of medicine by issuing a prescription to a poseur patient. Subject was brought to NBI-BACDO for the usual booking procedures. She was thereafter brought to the Office of the City Prosecutor for inquest proceedings for violation of Sec.10 of R.A. 2382 (The Medical Act of 1959).

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 13, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On February 4, 2025, the Office of the Ombudsman has indicted the following individuals: Floro Qimque Cases Jr., John Jigo Gaston Dacua, Grace M. Luardo-Silva, Allem Omlero Ceballos, Romelito Asinjo Datan, Mark Abarquez Ugbinar, Jerome Visarra Ornopea, Mare Vae Fernandez Reyes, Jayra Angelic Maninog Ruiz-Javier, John David Sevilles Javier, and Erika May S. Quino with one (1) count each of violation of Section 3(e) of Republic Act No. 3019 (Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act) and Malversation of Public Funds or Property, following an investigation by the National Bureau of Investigation – Central Visayas Regional Office (NBI-CEVRO) into an alleged anomaly in the collection and disposal of Cebu City’s garbage. The charges relate to a loss of public funds amounting to Php 239,728,280.62. In a separate resolution issued on March 14, 2025, the Ombudsman found the same individuals administratively liable for Gross Neglect of Duty and Conduct Prejudicial to the Best Interests of the Service. As a result, they face dismissal from their positions, cancellation of eligibility, forfeiture of retirement benefits, perpetual disqualification from holding public office, and a ban on taking civil service examinations. The NBI-CEVRO investigation, prompted by a complaint from the then-Cebu City Vice-Mayor, uncovered a fraudulent scheme involving a garbage collection contract. The city Government of Cebu had contracted with a joint venture, DOCAST Construction and JJ&J Construction and General Supply (DOCAST/JJ&J), for garbage collection, transportation, and disposal at a rate of Php 1,800.00 per ton from January 29, 2021, to July 19, 2021. The investigation revealed that DOCAST/JJ&J subcontracted with ARN Central Waste Management, Inc. (ARN), which provided a dumpsite for a fee of Php600.00 per ton. While city and barangay-owned trucks were permitted to deliver garbage directly to the ARN facility. DOCAST/JJ&J failed to accurately specify the tonnage delivered by these government-owned trucks in their billing statements to the Cebu City government. This implied that all garbage was collected and delivered exclusively by DOCAST/JJ&J. Further findings showed that DOCAST/JJ&J failed to pay ARN for their services, leading ARN to ban the company from its dumpsite on July 8, 2021. Despite this ban, DOCAST/JJ&J continued to bill the city government for services that were no longer being rendered, using falsified documents. The officials’ alleged negligence in exercising due diligence in processing these payments led to the substantial loss of public funds. Director Santiago commended the NBI-CEVRO agents for their relentless efforts in solving this complex case. Their investigation has been crucial in the Office of the Ombudsman’s resolution, which led to the indictment of the Subjects.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 17, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } On June 13, 2025, Lead Acid Automotive Batteries seized from an operation conducted by the National Bureau of Investigation-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) were subjected to disposal and destruction at DTI’s accredited facility in Brgy. Punturin, Valenzuela City. As a backgounder, on September 9, 2024, the NBI-NCR in coordination with the Department of Trade and Industry-Fair Trade Enforcement Bureau (DTI-FTEB), conducted an operation against CSS Autoparts, Inc. in its store in Binondo, Manila, and its warehouse located at Sgt. Rivera, Quezon City, for selling automotive batteries without a Philippine Standard (PS) Quality Certification Mark License and Import Commodity Clearance (ICC). The operation resulted in the seizure of 20,195 units of unregistered batteries, with estimated value of Php110,000,000.00. To date, this is DTI-FTEB’s largest seizure of Automotive Batteries without PS/ICC Mark License. The NBI charged the owners and managers of the said company for violating Article 18(a) of Republic Act No. 7394 (Consumer Act of the Philippines) and for violating Sections 6 and 7 of R.A. No. 4109 (Philippine Standards Law).

body: PRESS STATEMENT August 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In a decisive demonstration of justice in action, guided by a firm directive from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), a joint team of NBI – Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD), NBI – Southeastern Mindanao Region (NBI-SEMRO), NBI – Technical Intelligence Division (TID), NBI – International Airport Investigation Division (NBI-IAID), and the Bureau of Immigration (BI) successfully apprehended Draco Builders owners NICOLE MARTINEZ SYJUCO and her husband, MIGUEL SYJUCO on August 6, 2025 at NAIA Terminal 3 upon their arrival from Hong Kong. On July 22, 2024, the Regional Trial Court (RTC) Branch 20 in Davao Occidental issued a warrant for the Syjucos. The case alleges misappropriation and contractual deceit linked to three major projects in Mindanao, totaling PHP 200,000,000.00. Despite receiving substantial payments from the complainant—over 95% of the agreed costs— the Syjucos allegedly failed to complete the projects, leaving behind a dissatisfied client and unfulfilled contractual obligations. Furthermore, their refusal to refund the advance payment for an uninitiated project led to charges of misappropriation—a serious felony under Article 315 (1)(b) of the Revised Penal Code.
