body: A legal officer of the Bureau of Immigration (BI) who demanded additional amount for the visa extension of a foreigner was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Cebu City last Monday. The suspect was identified by NBI Director Nonnatus Caesar R. Rojas as: ATTY. SERAFIN S. ABELLON, Legal Officer II of the Bureau of Immigration (BI) Regional Office based in Mandaue City, Cebu, 63, and a resident of Cebu City. Investigation by the NBI – Central Visayas Regional Office (CEVRO) headed by RD Antonio M. Pagatpat disclosed that complainant, an American national came to the BI Cebu office on May 23, 2013 for the extension of his visa. Suspect demanded P25,000 as payment from the complainant, though the latter found out later that it costs only P2,800. He made an initial payment of P5,000 on May 6, 2013, and another P10,000 on May 16, 2013. However, ABELLON demanded an additional P15,000. This prompted the complainant to seek NBI assistance. He was brought to CEVRO where he was tested positive for the presence of fluorescent powder. Suspect was brought to the Office of the Ombudsman-Visayas for inquest proceedings for Extortion, violation of RA 3019 and Grave Misconduct. Subsequently, the following day, May 25, 2013, an information was filed against the suspect by the Office of the Ombudsman Visayas for violation of Art. 210 of the Revised Penal Code (Direct Bribery) before the RTC, Mandaue City.

body: A Chinese national was arrested by operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation – Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-AOTCD) agents during an operation in Binondo, Manila recently. The suspect is identified by NBI Director Virgilio L. Mendez as: ALBERT SO, legal age and a resident of 15B Lee Tower Condominium, Sabino Padilla Street, Binondo Manila. Investigation report revealed that NBI operatives received information from a confidential informant. After confirming said information, an authority to operate was asked and granted by Deputy Director Ricardo Pangan. On May 02, 2014, agents from the Anti Organized and Transnational Crime Division – Anti-Illegal Drugs Unit (AOTCD-AIDU) implemented a warrant of arrest against certain JAIME CHUA who resides at 15B Sabino Padilla Street, Binondo, Manila. Lim for violation of Section 6 Article II of R.A. 9165 otherwise known as The Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 Upon arrival at the area, Subject Chua was not around. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: Swift action on a report received by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) led to the rescue of an eight (8) year old school boy kidnapped on his way to school in Binan, Laguna last Friday. The abducted boy resides in Biñan, Laguna and a pupil of the Montessori Children’s Workshop also located in the same town. On June 22, 2012, the NBI office in Laguna was dispatched to act on an information about the abduction of an 8-year-old boy while on his way to school on board his school bus. A team was immediately formed and conducted surveillance. Two days later, the NBI received that a foreign-looking child was forcibly led into a wooden structure inside the Pines Ville Subdivision in Taytay, Rizal. Upon verification, it was found out that the child is a kidnapping victim from Laguna. The next day, June 26, 2012, after sustained surveillance, NBI agents proceeded to the area and rescued a boy in an abandoned shanty in Pines Ville Subdivision, Taytay, Rizal. NBI operatives brought the boy to the Bureau main office in Manila where he was reunited with his parents.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: On April 6, 2021, operatives of NBI-Western Visayas Regional Office (NBI-WEVRO) arrested LIANA VICTORIA SENINA alias “ELVI” for Robbery Extortion and violation of RA 7610. Subject LIANA VICTORIA SENINA and an alleged ADRIAN SALVADOR were threatening the minor victim of physical violence if she failed to pay the amount of Php 30,000. The victim had once created a Facebook “poser account” and used this as her own. Subjects alleged that they were angered of the misrepresentation of the minor at social media network. Subject “ELVI” successfully extorted and obtained money several times from the minor victim. Subjects took advantage of the tender age and immaturity of the minor lass to extract from her. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office, Iloilo City and was charged with Robbery Extortion and violation of RA 7610 all in relation to Cybercrime Law. On April 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Ilocos Regional Office (NBI-IRO) arrested ROSITA PETATE BALTAZAR for illegal quarrying and illegal distribution of aggregates in violation of RA 7942 otherwise known as Philippine Mining Act of 1995. Several surveillances, conduct of test buy and verification with Provincial Environment and Natural Resources Officer (PENRO) of Pangasinan resulted in the identification of Jack Knife Aggregates Trading as the entity conducting illegal quarrying and trading of aggregates in the vicinity of Brgy. Pindangan, Sison, Pangasinan. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of ROSITA PETATE BALTAZAR, cashier of Jack Knife Aggregates Trading. She was informed that she was being apprehended for violation of RA 7942 and immediately apprised of her constitutional rights. Subject was brought to NBI-IRO Office for the standard booking procedures and temporary detention. She was thereafter brought to Prosecutor’s Office in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan for inquest proceedings. On April 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested RODRIGO A. ROMBO for illegal gambling. Subject was caught en flagarante in violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287. Upon his arrest, Subject was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the standard booking procedures and was thereafter presented before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor for violation of RA 9287. On April 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Laoag District Office (NBI-LADO) arrested PREMIA SACLAYAN-VERDADERO for Human Trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the information that a house in Brgy. Lydia, Marcos, Ilocos Norte, was being maintained and operated as sex den by certain PREMIA SACLAYAN a.k.a CELLING. The veracity of the said information was established thru a series of surveillance. The modus of the Subject is to wait for the call or text of customers who want to avail of the services of women under her ward. After paying the Subject for the women’s sex services, the customer and the victim will proceed inside a room in the house of Subject to have sex. Afterwards, the other customers and their partners will follow to occupy the room for sexual encounter. Thus, on the aforementioned date, the entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the rescue of four (4) victims and the arrest of the Subject who tried to escape but eventually got arrested. Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of RA 9208 as amended by RA 10364. On April 12, 2021, operatives of NBI-Central Mindanao Regional Office (NBI-CEMRO) arrested ROGELIO PACQUIO LUMBAB, SALVADOR RAPISTORA DALISAY, ALANO DOCTOLERO ABELLANOSA, GILBERT S. SABANBAN, ELISEO PAYON, and BRYAN YANGYANG MANAYTAY for illegal treasure hunting. The NBI received a letter from Regional Executive Officer of DENR Region 12, requesting assistance in their follow up operation against a certain Joel Pamaran and spouses Leonardo and Gina Cabca who were conducting illegal treasure hunting at Purok Guadalupe, Brgy. Conel, General Santos City. Per information provided by the DENR Region 12, JOEL PAMARAN and spouses LEONARDO and GINA CABCA were already charged for violation of PD 705 or the Revised Forestry Code and RA 9147 or the Wildlife Resources Conservation and Protection Act before the Office of the City Prosecutor of General Santos City as the result of conducting illegal activity on February 2021 at the aforesaid place. Surveillance and casing operations confirmed the said illegal activity. Thus, on the above-mentioned date, NBI-CEMRO operatives, together with DENR personnel, proceeded to the target area and found thereat Subjects ROGELIO PACQUIO LUMBAB, SALVADOR RAPISTORA DALISAY, ALANO DOCTOLERO ABELLANOSA, GILBERT S. SABANBAN, ELISEO PAYON, and BRYAN YANGYANG MANAYTAY. They were placed under arrest for violation of PD 705 and RA 9147. All arrested Subjects were brought to NBI-CEMRO office in Koronadal City, South Cotabato for standard booking procedures. On April 15, 2021, operatives of NBI-CELRO arrested ALFONSO JUAQUIN LAZATIN y OCAMPO for robbery extortion. The case stemmed from a complaint filed by the victim of Subject Lazatin. According to complainant, sometime in October 2020, she saw a Facebook post of the subject offering a straight swap of Xiaomi Red Note 9 (cellphone). Subject Lazatin and the complainant agreed to swap their cellphones. When they met, complainant also handed over the battery charger of her cellphone but the subject refused and insisted that he has a charger and does not need one. After sometime, Subject Lazatin contacted the complainant informing her that the battery of the cellphone expanded. Subject demanded Php 2,000.00 for the repair of the battery to w/c complainant initially refused. Subject threatened that he will tag her online that she is a “scammer” and will post her identification and sex videos which the subject was able to retrieve from her phone. Subject was able to post the gov’t IDs of complainant online. With this, she was compelled to seek assistance from the NBI-CELRO. Subject Lazatin and the complainant agreed to meet in a mall in Telebastegan, San Fernando City, Pampanga to hand over the Php 2,000.00 which the subject demanded. Subject Lazatin was presented for inquest proceedings on April 16, 2021 before the Office of Prosecutor of the City of San Fernando Pampanga for the crime of Robbery (Extortion) punishable under the Revised Penal Code in relation to R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). On the same day, the Prosecutor issued an Inquest Resolution finding probable cause to indict the subject as charged and recommended his prosecution for the said violations of the law On April 16, 2021, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested MANOLITO VALERIO y MADULID for unauthorized possession and use of firearm. Subject was arrested in an operation which stemmed from an information that Subject always brandishes, openly carries a Cal.45 pistol, and uses the said firearm in threatening and coercing every individual who were cultivating public lands in the area of Brgy. Nauzon, Laur, Nueva Ecija. Acting on the information, operatives proceeded at the mountainous area of Brgy. Nauzon and thereat spotted Subject MANOLITO VALERIO openly carrying a gun on his right hand. Operatives tactically approached the Subject and after being subdued, he was placed under arrest and apprised him of his constitutional rights. Subject was asked for document of the firearm but failed to present any document authorizing him to possess and carry the said firearm. Subject was then brought to NBI-CABDO for standard booking procedures. Subject was thereafter presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Duty Inquest Prosecutor for violation of RA 10591 (Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act). On April 16, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao arrested alias “DATU” in MB Poblacion, Cotabato City for violation of Section 3601 of RA 4712. On April 19, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dagupan District Office (NBI-DADO) arrested JOSEPH CARRERA y PULIDO and GELYN C. ALMENARIO for Human Trafficking. Subjects were arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from an information that Citirock Spa, located at Arellano St., Dagupan City, Pangasinan, is engaged in exploitation of women for sexual activities in exchange of cash consideration. According to the information, Subjects are using the spa as a front for the illegal activities and collecting fee worth Php1,000-Php1,500 per customer for sexual pleasure. After the conduct of surveillance and validation of information, an entrapment operation was hatched to apprehend the persons involved in human trafficking and to rescue the trafficked victims. The operation resulted in the arrest of JOSEPH CARRERA y PULIDO (Manager) and GELYN C. ALMENARIO (Cashier) and the rescue of four (4) women. They were apprehended and were apprised of their constitutional rights as well as the nature of the charges. they were brought to NBI Dagupan City for the proper booking procedures and temporary detention. Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office for Human Trafficking. Rescued women were turned over to DSWD. On April 19, 2021 operatives of NBI- Special Action Unit arrested BERNADETTE UBANTE LAGAT and PAULO AREVALO ONATE for conducting Unauthorized Swab Testing, Estafa and Falsification. The case stemmed from a complaint that a Facebook page “Swab Test Pilipinas” is offering a home service swab test for Php 3,500.00 per test. Upon verification with the Health Facilities and Services Regulatory Bureau of DOH, the operatives of NBI-SAU found out that there is no existing licensed facility as COVID-19 Testing Laboratory by the name of “SWAB TEST PILIPINAS”. On the said date operatives of NBI-SAU conducted an entrapment operation at Don Pepe, Sto. Domingo, QC. Inside the residence where swab testing collection was performed, it was observed that the specimen was just placed in an ordinary container stuffed with other used materials where contamination is higher contrary to the issued guidelines of DOH for conducting remote specimen collection where the specimen shall be stored in a refrigerator or in a transport box with temperature maintained at 2°C to 8°C at all times while awaiting to be transported to the COVID-19 testing laboratory. Moreover, when the subjects were asked to provide any documents to prove their authority to conduct swab test, they failed to produce DOH License and when asked if they are trained by the RITM to perform swabbing, both subjects answered in the negative. subjects were placed under arrest and presented for electronic inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor of Quezon City for four (4) counts of Estafa under Article 315 (2)(a) of the RPC as amended and two (2) counts of Falsification under Article 172 of the RPC in relation to the Cybercrime Law. On April 20, 2021, operatives of NBI-Pagadian District Office (NBI-PAGDO) arrested LAVBREN ESPINOSA y LEGARA a.k.a LOVE and one alias BALDING for selling illegal drugs. On the said date, operatives of NBI-PAGDO conducted a buy-bust operation in Purok Sampaguita A, Brgy. Don Andres, Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay. After the informant confirmed that illegal drugs were purchased from Subjects BALDING and LOVE, another operation was conducted to apprehend the Subjects. On the same day, the poseur-buyer, together with the informant, proceeded to the place of operation and they were able to purchase from the Subjects suspected prohibited drugs packed in a heat-sealed plastic amounting to Php 5,000. After the pre-arranged signal, operatives effected the arrest in a peaceful and orderly manner. Search within the premises was likewise conducted resulting in the seizure of drug paraphernalia. Witnesses contemplated under the law had been secured and Subjects underwent the standard booking procedures. Documentation for the appropriate charges is now being readied. On April 22, 2021, operatives of NBI-Environmental Crime Division (NBI-EnCD) arrested ANGELICA SANCHEZ y ISLAO, ROSE MARIE SOLOMON y SESE, DANIEL SOLANA y BALAGOSA, ROMEO ENRIQUEZ y PAZAR, MARIA CLARISA CAMANGIAN y VILLARTE, and EMMANUEL DELA CRUZ y ZULIETA for illegal occupation and in protected landscape in Rodriguez, Rizal. Subjects were arrested in an operation which stemmed from the request of PENRO-RIZAL to conduct investigation of records and make ocular inspection on the alleged illegal occupation and construction of permanent structures in Pamitinan Protected Landscape, Brgy. San Rafael, Rodriguez, Rizal. Upon verification and surveillance conducted by EnCD operatives, there are permanent structures found within the Pamitinan Protected Landscape located in Sitio Wawa, Brgy. San Rafael, Rodriguez, Rizal in violation of RA 7586, as amended by RA 11038 otherwise known as Expanded National Integrated Protected Area System. On the above-mentioned date, joint operatives of the NBI-EnCD and PENRO-RIZAL conducted an operation and arrested in-flagrante delicto the aforementioned Subjects. On April 23, 2021, operatives of NBI-Sarangani District Office (NBI-SARDO) arrested ROSMAN HADJI IBRAHIM for blackmailing victim to have sexual intercourse. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint against him for alleged blackmailing, which was later on determined to constitute violation of RA 9262 otherwise known as Anti-Violence Against Women and Children Act of 2004 in relation to RA 10175 or the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012. According to the complainant, she and the Subject had an illicit affair since 2017 up to 2020. Complainant broke up with the Subject last December 2020 but the latter kept on texting the former. Subject threatened the complainant that he will keep sending her nude photos if she will not go out with him for the last time and have sexual intercourse. To end her agony and fear from Subject’s threats, complainant decided to meet with the Subject. Complainant sought the assistance of the NBI as she feared of being compelled to engage in sexual activity with the Subject since her purpose of meeting the Subject is just to talk to him. Acting on the complaint and with the viable information, operatives of NBI-SARDO conducted the entrapment operation in a lodge where Subject and complainant will meet. The operation resulted in the arrest of the Subject. He was brought to NBI-SARDO office where he was booked, fingerprinted, and photographed. On April 26, 2021, operatives of NBI-Rizal District Office (NBI-RIZDO) arrested WILSON VAFLOR DADULA, ROMMEL AMANDORON DADULA, and MARIO ORDONA RUANTO for Syndicated Estafa. The case stemmed from the complaint for alleged land scam/syndicated estafa committed by WILSON VAFLOR DADULA and his cohorts. Subjects disposed, sold, and offered for sale the subject land/property located in Sitio Putat, Barangay Calumbay, Tanay Rizal without authorization of the complainant who is a registered owner of the subject land/property. Subject WILSON DADULA was hired as caretaker to oversee the property by Nelson Aquino, father of complainant. However, in the year 2015, Nelson Aquino brought a complaint with the Barangay seeking the ouster of Subject DADULA as caretaker but did not materialize even though the Barangay issued Certificate to File Action in court. When Nelson died, complainant pursued the ouster of DADULA but the same proved futile. Complainant found several informal settlers in their property and by 2020, there were already more or less 90 families who had built their houses or claiming ownership of different portions of their land. On February 2021, complainant and his siblings were granted the authority for the said land and to file necessary legal action for the administration of the of the said property. This led to the filing of complaint before the NBI. Acting on the complaint, NBI-RIZDO conducted verification by acting as poseur buyers in the illegal selling activities perpetuated by Subject WILSON. They were able to confirm that indeed, WILSON DADULA and his cohorts are continuously offering and selling parcels of land owned by the complainant. It was found out that to own, occupy, or possess a portion of the subject land, buyer must first become a member of their organization called “ALPHA OMEGA WORLD DEVELOPMENT MARSHALL PROGRAMME” and pay the appropriate membership fee of Php2,500. Thereafter, a member may be able to acquire a lot ranging from 100-300 square meters for the amount of Php 350 of Php500 per square meter. After which, a member will be issued “Certificate of Occupancy”. With these information, operatives conducted the entrapment operation resulting in the arrest of Subject WILSON DADULA and MARIO RUANTO after being caught in the act of receiving the entrapment money. WILSON’s son, ROMMEL AMANDORON DADULA and MARIO RUANTO were acting as sales agent of WILSON. Arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Provincial Prosecutors Office, Taytay, Rizal for violation of Article 315 par.1 (b) (misappropriating and converting) and par.2 (a) (falsely pretending to possess property) of the Revised Penal Code as amended. On April 28, 2021, operatives of the National Bureau of Investigation – Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested ANJIENETH C. ARBUIS a.k.a. ANJ/WAWA after recovering illegal drugs in her premises. On the aforementioned date, operatives of NBI-NADO implemented Search Warrant for violation of RA 9165 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002 in the premises of ANJIENETH C. ARBUIS and LUIS C. ARBUIS a.k.a. LUISE/TUNGKAG at Zone 1, Barangay San Felipe, Naga City and Zone 7, Sagrada Familia, Barangay Penafrancia, Naga City respectively. Recovered in the premises of Subjects were several transparent plastic sachets containing white crystalline substance believed to be shabu. Subject ANJIENETH C. ARBUIS was placed under arrest and will be subjected for inquest proceedings while Subject LUISE C. ARBUIS was not around during the implementation of Search Warrant. Appropriate charges will be filed against Subject LUISE through regular filing. On April 28, 2021, operatives of NBI-Dumaguete District Office (NBI-DUMDO) arrested JOHN P. CALLAO, RANDY L. MAPA, and JOSEPH L. CALLAO for illegally transporting minerals in Barangay Candauai, Dumaguete City. In the morning of the aforementioned date, operatives of NBI-DUMDO were patrolling at Barangay Candauai and happened to chance upon two (2) Chariot cargo vehicles travelling and loading sand and gravel. The drivers were flagged down and were asked to present their transport receipts. Examination of their delivery receipts bared to be expired as they were dated March 15 and 22, 2021. They however contented that at the back of the delivery receipts was written the estimated quarry/sale for the day at .5 cu.meters of April 28, 2021. This was written by the permittee known to be JJUN SUASIN. The implementing rules under the LGU policy that every transport or delivery must be supported with one new on dated delivery receipt opposes the Subjects’ contention. The delivery receipts were recycled which is an illegal maneuver to defraud payment of taxes due to the government. Hence, they violated RA 9175 otherwise known as the Philippine Mining Act. Subjects were recommended for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutor’s Office. On April 28, 2021, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region (NBI-NCR) arrested JINKY JOY A. SENA and MARICAR A. SENA for Robbery Extortion in relation to RA 10175 and RA 9995. The case stemmed from the complaint of a minor victim. Subject JINKY JOY A. SENA hacked the Facebook account of victim. She was able to open and change the password of victim and sent several sex videos to other Facebook friends of the victim. Subject then demanded money to the mother of the victim with a promise that she will not send the other sex videos of the victim to other persons. Thru intimidation, Subjects JINKY JOY A. SENA and MARICAR A. SENA were able to receive money via money transfer from the victim’s mother. Thru the advice of NBI-Sarangani District Office, victim and her mother travelled to Manila and filed their complaint before the NBI-NCR. An entrapment operation was prepared and thru proper coordination with the money transfer branch in Pureza, Sta. Mesa, Manila, Subjects JINKY JOY A. SENA and MARICAR A. SENA were arrested. JINKY JOY A. SENA was confronted with the recordings of their conversations with the mother of the victim. Upon hearing the said recordings, she admitted that she was the one who hacked the victim’s Facebook account. Necessary documents for the filing of appropriate cases are being prepared against the Subjects for Robbery Extortion in relation to RA 10175 and RA 9995. The victim had once created a Facebook “poser account” and used this as her own. Subjects alleged that they were angered of the misrepresentation of the minor at social media network. Subject “ELVI” successfully extorted and obtained money several times from the minor victim. Subjects took advantage of the tender age and immaturity of the minor lass to extract from her. Subject was brought for inquest proceedings before the City Prosecutors Office, Iloilo City and was charged with Robbery Extortion and violation of RA 7610 all in relation to Cybercrime Law. Pindangan, Sison, Pangasinan. Thus, an entrapment operation was conducted resulting in the arrest of ROSITA PETATE BALTAZAR, cashier of Jack Knife Aggregates Trading. She was informed that she was being apprehended for violation of RA 7942 and immediately apprised of her constitutional rights. Subject was brought to NBI-IRO Office for the standard booking procedures and temporary detention. She was thereafter brought to Prosecutor’s Office in Urdaneta City, Pangasinan for inquest proceedings. On April 7, 2021, operatives of NBI-Bacolod District Office (NBI-BACDO) arrested RODRIGO A. ROMBO for illegal gambling. Subject was caught en flagarante in violation of PD 1602 as amended by RA 9287. Upon his arrest, Subject was apprised of his constitutional rights. Subject was immediately brought to NBI-BACDO for the standard booking procedures and was thereafter presented before the Office of the Provincial Prosecutor for violation of RA 9287. Lydia, Marcos, Ilocos Norte, was being maintained and operated as sex den by certain PREMIA SACLAYAN a.k.a CELLING. The veracity of the said information was established thru a series of surveillance. The modus of the Subject is to wait for the call or text of customers who want to avail of the services of women under her ward. After paying the Subject for the women’s sex services, the customer and the victim will proceed inside a room in the house of Subject to have sex. Afterwards, the other customers and their partners will follow to occupy the room for sexual encounter. title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: In line with government’s intensified campaign against illegal gambling, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) operatives of Cybercrime Division (NBI-CCD) arrested five (5) Korean nationals for online illegal gambling in Pasig City. NBI Director Dante A. Gierran said the Korean nationals were arrested as a consequence of the implementation of a Search Warrant for violation of PD 1602 (Prescribing Stiffer Penalties on Illegal Gambling) in relation to Section 6 of R.A. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012). The arrested Subjects were identified as CHEONJI KIM, ILHWAN YANG, WONSUP YANG, JEONG HYEOK KIM and MOON KYU KANG. The NBI said the Subjects operate or manage an administrator web page for online sports betting, sports toto, and online casino. They also used this kind of modus to facilitate money laundering activities. Moreover, Subjects usually choose exclusive subdivisions as their operation venue to hide from the law enforcement arm of the government. After due coordination with the Philippine National Police (PNP), CCD operatives conducted the operation in the target area wherein Subjects were caught in the act of operating the said illegal activity. Director Gierran stressed that unlicensed operations as that of the Subjects deprive the government millions of pesos in revenue adding that they are in effect robbing from Philippine government. Charges for violation of P.D. 1602 in relation to R.A. 10165 were filed in an inquest against the arrested Korean nationals before the Prosecutor’s Office in Pasig City, with an expected penalty of Prision Mayor or six (6) years and one (1) day to twelve (12) years if found guilty by the Philippine Court.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of two (2) individuals by operatives of NBI-Special Action Unit for Syndicated Estafa and Using Fictious Names. Four (4) other Subjects, who are cohorts involved in the case are currently at-large. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Director Eric B. Distor identified the arrested Subjects as MA. FE VELASQUEZ CRUZ a.k.a. GUIVEVERE REGINE KING VILLAVICENCIO and JOSE PERALTA PABUSTAN a.k.a. JAMES DE GUZMAN. The at-large individuals were identified as ERL MASANGCAY, ROSEMARIE SOLEMA, PRESCILLA SANGA, and NOEL BANZUELO. OIC Distor said the case stemmed from the complaint of the President-CEO of Wilcon Corporation against the Subjects and their cohorts. According to the complainant, sometime in November 2020, DOROTHY JOY FANIO and CATHERINE FIDEL informed them that a property in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig City was being offered for sale. Complainant expressed interest in purchasing it and directed Atty. Fortunato Lira, with the assistance of FANIO, regarding the matter and to represent the Corporation in the transaction. Atty. Lira and Fanio then met with Subjects NOEL BANZUELO, ROSEMARIE SOLEMA, and PRESCILLA SANGA who represented themselves as BGC property brokers. Subjects presented an Authority to Sell signed by GEROVY VINCENT KING, the supposed President of SHEFA BASILEA INC. along with a photocopy of Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) issued by the Registry of Deeds for Taguig City. Subject ERL MASANGCAY asked his cousin, ATTY. MARILYN MACUBA-BALLEGA if she could draft a letter of acceptance in connection with the Letter of Intent of Wilcon of its willingness to buy a parcel of land allegedly located at BGC,Taguig City. On January 8, 2021, Atty. Ballega met Subjects BANZUELO, SOLEMA, SANGA, JAMES DE GUZMAN, and GUIVEVERE REGINE KING VILLAVICENCIO. Said individuals had a meeting with the Chairman of WILCON wherein Subject MA. FE CRUZ introduced herself as GUINEVERE REGINE KING VILLAVICENCIO and supposedly Chairman of Board of Directors of SHEFA BASILEA, INC. body: A married man long wanted for rape and who abducted and severely beat a minor was arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Laguna recently. The suspect was identified as SANDY BABAO PELOBELLO, 37, married and a resident of Block 2, Lot 6, Ville de Palm Subdivision, Bgy. Santiago, Gen. Trias, Cavite. Investigation report of the Laguna District Office (LAGDO) revealed that on January 8, 2013, victim’s mother sought NBI assistance. Her minor daughter “Isa” (not her real name), a 13-year-old girl, has been missing since November 10, 2012 and suspected that her daughter must have been abducted by Pelobello. It was learned during investigation that Pelobello claimed “Isa” is his girlfriend and they allegedly eloped on the day she was reported missing. He later brought her to a cousin’s house in Manggahan, Dasmariñas, Cavite. When the suspect learned about the charges, Pelobello threatened to kill her and her family if they refused to withdraw the case they filed against him. On February 2, 2013, victim suddenly went home. However, she went back to Pelobello on February 10 for fear that the suspect might make good his threat to her family. She returned home again the next day with several bruises on her face and body as a result of his mauling her when she told him she wanted to return to her family to continue her studies. Record check conducted on the suspect revealed that he has a string of outstanding warrants of arrest to his name for rape in Iloilo City. In view of the foregoing development, in the evening of February 11, 2013, NBI- LAGDO operatives, in coordination with the local police and barangay officials, proceeded to the suspect’s residence in Calamba, Laguna. He was informed of a complaint filed against him, and by virtue of several warrants of arrest, he was apprehended. Pelobello resisted and his minor daughter tried to prevent the operatives from arresting him but was subdued and brought to the NBI district office in Laguna. Subsequently, a case for violation of RA 7610, “Special Protection of Children Against Child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act “ and Abduction were filed against the suspect before the Provincial Prosecutor of Imus, Cavite. He is presently detained at the NBI District Office.

body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today announced the arrest of four (4) individuals in a buy-bust operation in the City of Manila for selling and using illegal drugs. NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as ERIC EULOGIO, ODESSA DE GUZMAN PATERNA, RENATO ABAYA, and APRIL KYLE GONZALEZ. Information received by the NBI- Task Force Against Illegal Drugs (NBI-TFAID) from its Confidential Informants that a certain organized group known as “Akyat Condo Gang” headed by a certain Eric Eulogio, has offered to sell them high-grade shabu. Surveillance, undercover work and series of interviews conducted by the NBI-TFAID revealed that Eric’s group is notoriously engaged in robbery, theft, drug peddling, and maintenance of drug dens usually picking condominium owners within Manila and Quezon City area. Further investigation revealed that the group was already arrested by the PNP-NCRPO in 2016 for robbing millions worth of jewelries and money from a condominium owner in Quezon City. The informants reported to NBI-TFAID that they have received information from Eric that he has with him a certain amount of shabu and offered his rented condominium unit located in Oyo-V-Cat Hotel in Blumentritt, Manila, as a den for any drug-sniffing activity. Thus, on June 13, 2020, acting promptly on the information, NBI-TFAID operatives together with the said informants proceeded to the target area and positioned themselves in strategic locations for the buy-bust operation. The informants then proceeded inside the target condominium unit and were able to buy shabu worth Php 2,000.00. One of the informants texted the operatives that she was being force by Eric to sniff shabu inside the unit. Acting on the text message, NBI-TFAID rushed to the unit and arrested Subjects Eric Eulogio Paterna, Abaya, and Gonzalez who were caught by the operatives in the act of sniffing shabu. Laboratory examinations conducted on the urine of the four (4) subjects resulted positive for the presence of Methamphetamine. Subjects were presented before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Manila for inquest proceedings for violation of Section 5 (Sale of Illegal Drugs), Section 6 (Maintenance of a Den), Section 7 (Visitors of Den), and Section 15 (Use of Dangerous Drugs) of the R.A. 9165, otherwise known as the Comprehensive Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002.

body: A jobless man and his drinking companion who raped and killed a 6-year-old grade school pupil were arrested by agents of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in Candelaria, Quezon last week. The NBI identified the suspects as: EDGAR “EGAY CULTURA RAMOS, 42; and ROLANDO “JUZZAR” GUTLAY DE CHAVEZ, 46, carpenter and both residents of Barangay Pahinga Norte, Candelaria, Quezon. Investigation conducted by the Lucena District Office (LUCDO) headed by Head Agent Olivo Ramos disclosed that on July 23, 2013, the father of the victim, Renato Lopez, sought NBI investigative assistance regarding her 6-year-old daughter who was found dead floating in a canal. He said that his daughter arrived home from school in the afternoon of July 22, 2013 and went out to play. But after several hours, she failed to arrive home. This prompted him to seek help from his neighbors and other barangay officials for the whereabouts of his daughter. After eight (8) hours, the body was found floating in a canal partly covered with debris with only her cycling shorts on. Upon receipt of the complaint, NBI agents immediately conducted an investigation which led to the neighboring house being occupied by suspect Ramos where droplets of blood were discovered. Upon interrogation, suspects Ramos and De Chavez confessed to the crime in the presence of a counsel. Suspects said that his group were having a drinking spree since July 21, and the next day, being the birthday of Ramos. Around 2:00 PM, of July 22, their companions went home. When the victim passed by the house of suspect Ramos, De Chavez, who returned, snatched the victim and brought her inside. When the victim started to cry and shout, suspects began hitting her on the head using a lead pipe. While the victim lay motionless, they also took turns in sexually abusing her. Afterwards, and under the cover of darkness, they dumped her lifeless body into the canal hoping that the strong current brought about by the heavy rain will carry her to the distant river. They also tried to rid the house of bloodstains. Medico-genital examination conducted by the municipal health officer in Candelaria revealed large and deep lacerated wounds, swelling and hematoma probably from blows with a hard object and lacerations in her genitals, suggesting that victim was also sexually abused. The suspects were brought to the NBI where they were detained. Charges of Rape with Homicide were filed against the suspects before the Quezon Provincial Prosecutor’s Office.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 31, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the continuing battle against child sexual exploitation, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) under the leadership of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested a lawyer for possession of Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials (CSAEM). On October 18, 2024, the NBI-Human Trafficking Division (HTRAD) received a case referral from the Department of Justice – Office of Cybercrime (DOJ-OOC), regarding Subject “KENCHI-11”, who was allegedly uploading and storing numerous CSAEM in his Google Account, showing several nude pubescent male children engaged in sexual activity with other pubescent male minors and adult males, one of which is the Subject himself. The case was referred to Combatting Trafficking in Person (CTIP) for Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT) analysis, which revealed that the Subject is MICHAEL PEPANIA MOLINA, a member of the Philippine bar, who resides and works in Zamboanga City. On March 21, 2025, NBI-HTRAD together with NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM agents proceeded to Zamboanga City. Together with NBI-Western Mindanao Regional Office (WEMRO) and the Department of Social Welfare and Development Region IX, they were able to locate and take statements of two (2) victims of the Subject. Victims narrated that Subject would ask them to do shows, performing various sexual and lascivious activities such as kissing, licking, and oral sex with the Subject. The Subject would record the lewd shows in his cellphone and would force them to watch the replays in his room. On March 25, 2025, the Warrant to Search, Seize and Examine Computer Data (WSSECD) for violation of RA 11930, otherwise known as the Anti-Online Sexual Abuse and Exploitation of Children and Anti-Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Materials Act of 2022 applied by NBI-HTRAD was granted by RTC, Branch 7 of Zamboanga City. Thus, on the same date, a composite team from NBI-HTRAD, NBI-WEMRO, DOJ-OOC, and NCC-OSAEC-CSAEM together with DSWD IX and Zamboanga City CSWDO, PAOCC, DOJ-IACAT, and Exodus Philippines proceeded to the area for service of the WSSECD. The subject was caught in his bedroom with two (2) boys, ages 15 and 12. The team found a smartphone in his possession, which rang when the agents called the number associated with his Google account. Several external hard drives, various CSAEMs, and folders with the names of boys were found in the Subject’s room. The team brought the seized devices for off-site forensic examination. The two (2) minors in the premises disclosed that they were abused by the Subject. The social workers subsequently brought them for interview and processing. On March 27, 2025, Subject was presented for inquest proceedings for violation of Section 4(r) in relation to Sec. 6 of R.A. 11930 (Large Scale Possession of CSAEM), Sec. 4 (a) of R.A. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) as amended by R.A. 10364, and Child Abuse under R.A. 7610 (Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act).

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 02, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In accordance with the directive from National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), to intensify operations against all forms of criminal activity, the NBI Homicide Division (NBI-HD) has arrested PIO JONATHAN EULALIO y ANIERO. This arrest, made in Santa Rosa, Nueva Ecija, was executed under an arrest warrant issued by RTC Branch 215 of Quezon City for Kidnapping for Ransom with Homicide and Homicide. The case was originally investigated by the NBI-HD joint with NBI-Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD), and NBI-Public Corruption Division (NBI-PCD) pertaining to the death of Christian Ortega and the kidnapping for ransom of Gloria Ortega, which occurred on June 10, 2024, in Baesa, Quezon City. On July 12, 2024, the decomposed body of Gloria Ortega was found and recovered by the investigating team. The investigation culminated in the arrest of two individuals. In July 2024, the arrested individuals were presented to the Department of Justice (DOJ) for inquest proceedings. On February 21, 2025, the court issued a warrant for the arrest of Subject Eulalio, who was also involved in the crime. In response, NBI-HD agents immediately conducted surveillance operations that identified the current location of Subject Eulalio, who was hiding in Barangay Liwayway, Sta. Rosa, Nueva Ecija. On May 31, 2025, agents of NBI-HD implemented the warrant and proceeded to the subject’s hideout, resulting in his arrest. Subject Eulalio was brought to the NBI Main Office in Filinvest Cyberzone, Bay City, Macapagal Boulevard, Pasay City for standard booking procedures and medical examination. The Subject was turned over to the NBI Jail Facility in Muntinlupa City for temporary custody, while awaiting transfer to the Quezon City Jail. Director Santiago commended the agents of NBI-HD for the successful operation leading to the arrest of Subject Eulalio.

body: PRESS STATEMENT July 5, 2022 NBI FILES MURDER CHARGES AGAINST NCRPO PERSONNEL FOR SUSPICIOUS DEATHS OF HIGH-PROFILE INMATES The National Bureau of Investigation-Death Investigation Division (NBI-DID) recommended for the filing of eight (8) counts of Murder against NCRPO personnel before the Department of Justice on the suspicious death of high-profile Persons Deprived of Liberty (PsDL), namely, Francis Go, Shuli Lim Zhang, Jimmy Ang, Eugene Chua, Benajamin Marcelo, Sherwin Sanchez, Amin Boratong, and Willy Yang. NBI-DID conducted investigation through Department Order No. 179 series of 2020, issued by the Secretary of Justice, directing the NBI to conduct investigation on the alleged death of Jaybee Sebastian, and eight (8) other high-profile PsDL, who allegedly died of Covid-19 or its complications while isolated inside the facility of the New Bilibid Prison (NBP) in Muntinlupa City, the control of which was under the members of the NCRPO security and medical teams. Careful examination of sworn statements of witnesses and the records of the NBP revealed, among others, the following: 1. The room assignment of the high-profile PsDL at Building 4, Site Harry, where they were confined during their alleged infection with Covid 19, was according to the nature of criminal conviction. All those who were convicted of cases involving illegal drugs are all victims of this case; 2. Immediately after the segregation and transfer to the “comfortable” isolation room, victims died; 3. Witnesses had not observed any unusual situation of the Ps while inside the isolation area, even when their rooms were only separated either by curtains or plywood; 4. The only irregular observation they made was their co-PsDL gradually disappeared from Building 4 after they had revealed that they were to be transferred to the “comfortable” isolation room; 5. This is inconsistent with the allegations of the NCRPO personnel who all purported that they administered nursing intervention and were all on-alert when the PsDL were on “emergency” situation; 6. Significant amount of time elapsed before the victims were brought to the nearest hospital; 7. All the deceased PsDL were declared dead on arrival, the cause of death either by cardiac or pulmonary arrest. However, a close examination of the medical profile of the deceased high-profile PsDL generally revealed that days before they died, they exhibited neither chronic symptom of Covid-19, including difficulty in breathing or shortness of breath, nor were they observed to be weak or particularly ill. Witnesses had seen them to be well, normal, or lively; 8. Subjects took advantage of the fact that victims were confined at Building 4, Site Harry, an NCRPO-managed isolation area, due to Covid-19 infection. They availed the situation that in case of Covid-19 cases, cadavers should immediately be cremated. Cremation, for this case, was the final act to consummate and effectively cover-up the scheme to kill the victims; and 9. The circumstances surrounding the death of Jaybee Sebastian showed that he died of natural causes. On July 1, 2022, charges for eight (8) counts of Murder, as defined and penalized under Article 248 of the Revised Penal Code, were filed against PMaj. LYMEL JOHN HAYAHAY PASQUIN, PSSg. RANNEL TANAJURA GADIANO, PSSg. CHRISTIAN ARAGON MERCARSOS, PCpl. LAURENCE RALLOS ANTIPORTA, PCpl JHUNBEN OCA ALEGADO, PCpl. JAYSON LEQUIN AÑONUEVO, PCpl. ROSANIE MUJERES BERNALES, PCpl. MICHAEL HELLACONE BOCO, PCpl. ROLEX MARGAJA BORGONIA, PCpl. JOPHY TAGMAYON BUOT, PCpl. GILWEN BASALLO GARCIA, PCpl. EDMAR ILUSTISIMO GERRA, PCpl. ARCHIE AUMAN GRAPA, PCpl. VERNARDO VISPO INTO, PCpl. ENER PEREZ RESTAURO, PCpl. BANEDY TALIPOROS SOLANTE, PCpl. JERNIE MATA TIONGZON, JAN ANTHON RODULF TABOTABO UY, Pat. ROLAND BUTCH PELOSTRATUS DURAN, Pat. JAMES GEMETIZA ANINAPON, Pat. REY REPONTE FERNANDEZ, and Dr. BEVERLY DE GUZMAN before the Department of Justice, Manila.

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) today said operatives of NBI-Special Task Force (NBI-STF) arrested a Jordanian national in Makati City for illegal possession of firearm and violent acts inside a hotel premises. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Jordanian national as TAREK SIAM. OIC Director Distor said the NBI received a letter complaint from Congressman Anthony Rolando T. Golez, Attorney-in-Fact of Makati Hotel and Residences Condominium Corporation, requesting law enforcement assistance regarding MR. TAREK SIAM who had been violently harassing the employees of a hotel in Makati City and even threatened several security guards of the said establishment with a gun violating election gun ban and the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act of 2012. On January 25, 2022, NBI operatives received a phone call from the management of the hotel requesting immediate law enforcement assistance to avert the violent acts being committed by TAREK SIAM inside the hotel premises. As relayed, TAREK SIAM was in possession of a hand gun as he was destroying and breaking the hallway lights of the 22nd floor of the hotel. NBI operatives immediately responded but upon arrival, TAREK SIAM went back inside his room. Meantime, operatives were shown CCTV footages showing that TAREK SIAM was indeed in possession of a firearm and while outside his residence, he loaded his gun. According to the management of the hotel, TAREK SIAM had been brandishing and drawing his gun against any hotel personnel. NBI-STF checked the database of criminal records and found out that there is a Warrant of Arrest issued by the Manila Regional Trial Court Branch 005 against TAREK SIAM for violation of RA 7610 otherwise known as Special Protection of Children Against Abuse, Exploitation, and Discrimination Act. With the Warrant of Arrest at hand, operatives patiently waited for someone from TAREK SIAM’s room to come out, taking into consideration the safety of the hotel residents as TAREK SIAM may react violently using his gun. When a female individual came out of the room, operatives took the opportunity to sneak inside. NBI-STF operatives declared their presence and informed TAREK SIAM of his Warrant of Arrest and placed the Subject under arrest after being apprised of his statutory and constitutional rights. Recovered from Subject TAREK SIAM were one (1) Glock 27 Gen 4 mounted with a laser and inserted with a loaded magazine with 13 Caliber .40 ammunitions and two (2) magazines of Glock .40 Caliber with caliber.40 ammunitions. Charges for violation of RA 10591 otherwise known as the Comprehensive Firearms and Ammunition Regulation Act and violation of The Omnibus Election Code were filed against TAREK SIAM before the City Prosecutor, Makati City.

body: PRESS STATEMENT May 30, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI EXTRADITES RAPE SUSPECT FROM BAHRAIN The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its International Operations Division (IOD), successfully facilitated the extradition and arrest of a fugitive wanted for two (2) counts of rape following coordinated efforts with international law enforcement authorities and the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL). The subject who has a Warrant of Arrest issued by Branch 5, Family Court, Fourth Judicial Region, Trece Martires City, Cavite, was charged with two (2) counts of Rape under Article 266-A of the Revised Penal Code, as amended by Republic Act No. 8353, otherwise known as the Anti-Rape Law of 1997. Upon the request of the complainant, the NBI-International Operations Division initiated the process for the inclusion of the subject in the INTERPOL Red Notice List. Consequently, INTERPOL published the Red Notice against the subject on January 27, 2026. The Philippine Center for Transnational Crime (PCTC) subsequently informed the NBI that the subject had been arrested in the Kingdom of Bahrain. On April 16, 2026, the PCTC relayed an official communication from INTERPOL National Central Bureau (NCB) Bahrain confirming that the extradition of the subject had been approved by the judicial authorities of Bahrain. Following the approval, an NBI escort team was dispatched to Bahrain from May 18 to 21, 2026 to facilitate the transfer and return of the fugitive to Philippine jurisdiction. Upon arrival at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport (NAIA) Terminal 3 at approximately 11:54 a.m. on May 21, 2026, the subject was formally arrested by NBI-IOD operatives and informed of his constitutional rights. He was thereafter brought to the NBI for standard booking procedures, including fingerprinting, photography, and medical examination. On the same date, the subject was turned over to the Bureau’s detention facility at Building 14, New Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City, pending further proceedings before the court. The successful extradition underscores the NBI’s continuing commitment to pursuing fugitives beyond Philippine borders and ensuring that individuals facing criminal charges are brought before the courts to answer for the offenses imputed against them. The Bureau likewise recognizes the invaluable assistance of INTERPOL, the Philippine Center for Transnational Crime, and the authorities of the Kingdom of Bahrain in the successful return of the subject to the Philippines.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 24, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the directive of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.) to intensify the campaign against the proliferation of smuggled frozen fishery products in the country, the NBI Batangas District Office (NBI- BatDO) arrested Alexious Aguilar y Yumul, Romel Estrada y Malapitan, and Jeremie Villa y Gutierrez for violation of Republic Act No. 10654 amending Republic Act 8550, otherwise known as “The Philippine Fisheries Code. of 1998 and violation of Republic Act 12022, otherwise known as the “Anti-Agricultural Sabotage Act of 2024”. The entrapment operation also resulted in the seizure of one hundred (100) boxes of assorted smuggled frozen fishery products. The operation stemmed from an information that individuals are engaged in the transportation and selling of frozen fishery products in the province of Batangas. Acting on the said information, an entrapment operation was planned and conducted. Subjects agreed to deliver frozen fishery products in Batangas City, Batangas. On February 06, 2025, Subjects arrived at the agreed place where the items will be unloaded and paid. After inspecting the declared smuggled frozen fishery products and after they received the pre-marked entrapment money, NBI-BatDO Operatives declared their authority under the law and arrested the said individuals. The arrested Subjects were presented for Inquest Proceedings on February 07, 2025 before the Office of the City Prosecutor Batangas City, Batangas. Director Santiago commended NBI-BatDO for the law enforcement action taken by its operatives to deter the negative effects on the supply, production, and price stability of fishery products in the country.

body: On July 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cabanatuan District Office (NBI-CABDO) arrested PINEDA, LESTER y DIAO for Human Trafficking. Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation conducted in front of Midway Maritime School locaed in Brgy. Bitas, Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija. Documents are being prepared for inquest proceedings against the Subject for violation of RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act). He is now detained at NBI Detention Cell, Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija. On July 16, 2020, operatives of NBI-National Capital Region arrested JAMES ALEJANDRIA CATCHILLAR, CARLO ALEJANDRIA CATCHILLAR, and JAIME N. PAULITE JR. for Carnapping and Kidnapping with Ransom. A complaint for Kidnapping and Carnapping was filed before the NBI against alias JOHN TALKTO and seven (7) other conspirators who posed as buyers of 2020 model Toyota Fortuner G Variant. Subjects abducted the victims and seized the said Fortuner along with one (1) 2019 Red Wine Mitsubishi Mirage, Php 100,000.00 cash, and Vivo mobile phones on about 1:00pm of June 6, 2020 in Pantok, Binangonan, Rizal. Victims were released 5:00am of June 7, 2020 in Commonwealth, Quezon City. Through continuous tracking and investigation, operatives were able to track the Subjects who conspired in Kidnapping the complainants and taking away their vehicles. Investigation further unveiled the identity of other conspirators as JAME’s brothers namely, RICHIE CATCHILLAR, RICHARD CATCHILLAR, and BUNSO CATCHILLAR. Charges for Kidnapping with Ransom and violation of RA 10883 (Anti-Carnapping Law of the Philippines) were filed against JAMES ALEJANDRIA CATCHILLAR a.k.a. JOHN TALKTO a.k.a. JAN BAJETA CAUSAPIN, CARLO ALEJANDRIA CATCHILLAR, JAIME N. PAULITE JR., RICHIE CATCHILLAR (at large), RICHARD CATCHILLAR (at large), BUNSO CATCHILLAR (at large), and two (2) other John Does. On July 21, 2020, operatives of NBI-Iligan District Office (NBI-ILDO) arrested CRYSSAN CABTALAN y ACAYLAN and GIOVANNI REYES y CARTIN for selling shabu. Subjects were arrested in a buy-bust operation conducted at Zone 1, Del Carmen, Iligan City by NBI-ILDO, PDEA-10, PDEA-Lanao del Norte, and Iligan City Police Station 1. Bought from the Subjects was one (1) large size heat-sealed rectangular white plastic sachet containing white crystalline substance suspected to be shabu weighing more or less 5 grams with estimated value of Php 20,000. Subjects were brought to NBI Iligan District Office for the booking procedures and temporary detention. On July 22, 2020, operatives of NBI-Cordillera Administrative Region (NBI-CAR) arrested JESSICA ANNA MARIE D. YAGO for profiteering in violation of RA 7581 (Philippine Price Act). Subject was arrested in her work location at SM Mall, Luneta Hill, Baguio City by virtue of Warrant of Arrest. Subject admiited that she was engaged in online selling of alcohol with Brenda Guillermo Madrid. Her co-accused. Subject was brought before the court on July 23, 2020 and was released after posting bail. body: PRESS STATEMENT July 09, 2025 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } In line with the campaign to stop the proliferation of counterfeit products, the National Bureau of Investigation – National Capital Region (NBI-NCR), under the leadership of Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.), enforced multiple Search Warrants at locations in the City of Manila, NCR, and in a separate operation in Iligan City, Lanao del Norte for violation of Section 155 (Trademark Infringement), in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No. 8293 or the “Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines.” The first case stemmed from the complaint filed by Orion Support, Inc. (OSI) representing GUCCI, BOTTEGA VENETA, BALENCIAGA, and YSL. On 25 June 2025, NBI-NCR agents, together with the NBI-Intellectual Property Rights Division (NBI-IPRD), validly implemented twenty (20) search warrants against eight (8) establishments for violation of the aforementioned offense and successfully seized and confiscated Eight Hundred and Eighty-Two (882) pieces of counterfeit various products, all bearing trademarks of GUCCI, BOTTEGA VENETA, BALENCIAGA, and YSL, and various business documents, receipts, including other pieces of evidence, which were estimated to be worth more or less Thirty Million Pesos (Php 30,000,000.00). On the following day, 26 June 2025, NBI-NCR and NBI-IPRD, acting on the complaint of OSI on behalf of their client OSRAM, lawfully served two (2) search warrants against two (2) locations in lligan City for violation of the aforementioned offenses. The operation resulted in the seizure of Two Hundred and Twenty-Six (226) pieces of various counterfeit products bearing the OSRAM trademark, with various business documents and receipts used in their illegal operations, with a total estimated monetary value of more or less One Hundred Thousand Pesos (Php 100,000.00). Director Santiago lauded the NBI-NCR for successfully implementing said search warrants and their law enforcement actions to stop the proliferation and distribution of counterfeit/fake products. NBI reminds the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: PRESS STATEMENT October 22, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation Organized and Transnational Crime Division (NBI-OTCD) under the leadership of NBI Director JUDGE JAIME B. SANTIAGO (Ret.) arrested LI, MING, Cashier of Baima Hui Life Supermarket (Baima) and SUN, ZHEN FU, warehouseman of Baima in Parañaque City for violations of Section 11(j) [Illegal Sale of Medicine) of R.A. No. 3720, as amended by R.A. No. 9711 (Food and Drug Administration Act of 2009) and Section 45(a) and (d) (Illegal Dispensing/Sale of Pharmaceutical Products) of R.A. No. 10918 (Philippine Pharmacy Act). Director Santiago said that the operation stemmed from intelligence information regarding unauthorized or illegal operation of a pharmacy identified as BAIMA HUI LIFE SUPERMARKET (Baima) in Parañaque City. In response, NBI-OTCD conducted a surveillance operation against Baima, which confirmed that Baima is indeed engaged in selling and offering for sale medicines and other pharmaceutical products without the necessary permits/licenses from the Food and Drug Administration (FDA). On October 14, 2024, NBI-OTCD proceeded to Baima located in Pacific Avenue, Brgy. Don Galo, Parañaque City and hatched the buy-bust operation, which resulted in the arrest of Subjects Li, Ming and Su, Zhen Fu in the act of committing the above-stated violations. The arrested Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Parañaque City. Director Santiago congratulated the operatives of NBI-OTCD for the successful apprehension of the two (2) Subjects and warned the public to refrain from buying unregistered medicines from unauthorized sellers.

body: PRESS STATEMENT June 11, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } PRESS RELEASE | NBI INAUGURATES KAUSWAGAN SATELLITE OFFICE TO BRING GOVERNMENT SERVICES CLOSER TO THE PEOPLE KAUSWAGAN, Lanao del Norte – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) formally inaugurated the NBI Kauswagan Satellite Office on June 10, 2026, at the Kauswagan International Organic Convention Center (KIOCC), marking a significant milestone in the Bureau’s continuing efforts to expand access to government services and strengthen its presence in communities across Northern Mindanao. The inauguration ceremony was led by NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag together with Deputy Director for Administration Atty. Jose Justo S. Yap and Deputy Director for Operations Atty. Antonio M. Pagatpat. Also present were officials from NBI Regional Office X, Agent-in-Charge (AICs) of nearby district offices and other officials and personnel who gathered in support of the Bureau’s continuing expansion of its services in the region. Joining the event were Hon. Rommel C. Arnado, Vice Mayor of the Municipality of Kauswagan. The ceremony was further highlighted by the attendance of Commander Mujstaba A. Macapaar, Commander Aleem Ansari T. Murad, and fellow commanders and representatives of Kauswagan’s renowned Arms-to-Farms Program, whose presence reflected the municipality’s enduring commitment to peacebuilding and sustainable development. In his message, Director Matibag emphasized that the establishment of the satellite office is a testament to the Bureau’s dedication to making NBI services more accessible, efficient, and responsive to the needs of the public. He noted that residents of Kauswagan and neighboring municipalities will now have easier access to essential NBI services, particularly the processing of NBI Clearances and the accommodation of complaints, inquiries, and other matters requiring the Bureau’s assistance. Director Matibag likewise underscored the importance of strengthening the Bureau’s presence at the local level in support of its mandate to uphold justice, promote public trust, and ensure the effective delivery of investigative services. He further assured district and regional offices that the NBI National Office remains fully committed and always open to providing the necessary support and assistance needed to enhance operations, improve service delivery, and advance the Bureau’s mission throughout the country. Vice Mayor Arnado welcomed the establishment of the satellite office and expressed the local government’s appreciation for the Bureau’s decision to expand its services in the municipality. He recognized the initiative as an important development that will benefit not only the people of Kauswagan but also residents from nearby communities who seek convenient access to NBI services. The participation of Commander Mujstaba A. Macapaar, Commander Aleem Ansari T. Murad, and other representatives of the Arms-to-Farms Program added meaningful significance to the occasion. Their presence highlighted Kauswagan’s remarkable transformation from a conflict-affected area into a model community for peace and development. Through the Arms-to-Farms initiative, former combatants have become active partners in nation-building, contributing to peace, security, and agricultural productivity within the municipality. The establishment of the NBI Kauswagan Satellite Office is expected to significantly improve the delivery of frontline services by reducing travel time and making government services more readily available to the public. The facility will serve as an important extension of the Bureau’s efforts to provide responsive, efficient, and citizen-centered service while enhancing coordination with local stakeholders in addressing concerns related to public safety and justice. The inauguration likewise demonstrated the strong partnership between the National Bureau of Investigation and the Municipality of Kauswagan in promoting good governance, public service excellence, and community development. As the Bureau continues to expand its reach nationwide, the opening of the NBI Kauswagan Satellite Office stands as a symbol of its unwavering commitment to bringing quality government services closer to the Filipino people and ensuring that justice remains accessible to every community.

NBI Officer-In-Charge Eric B. Distor identified the subjects as MARICOLE RAMOS y MENDOZA and ALEXANDER PERALTA y ABAD who were apprehended by Agents of the NBI-Anti Human Trafficking Division (NBI-AHTRAD) in an entrapment and rescue operation in an apartelle in Fairview, Novaliches Quezon City. Distor said that in the course of said operation, a 17-year old and an 18-year old trafficked victims were rescued and had been placed under the custody of the Social workers. Distor said the case stemmed from an intelligence report received by the NBI-AHTRAD on April 30, 2020 that a certain individual has been recruiting and offering minor girls for sexual exploitation to clients for a fee. The report further disclosed that herein subject has a Facebook account with name MARICOLE RAMOS II (Marrieon Kyle) who allegedly offers young girls ages 14-21 years old for sexual services to customers for a fee of P3,000.00 and has been using Trivago, Airbnb and similar platforms to book accommodations (hotels, condominium, penthouse, apartelle) where supposed child trafficking may take place, Distor emphasized. Under his strict orders, Distor said that on May 5, 2020, operatives of NBI-AHTRAD and Intelligence Agents from the DOJ Inter-Agency Council Against Trafficking in Persons (DOJ-IACAT) hatched an entrapment and rescue operation. The NBI likewise sought the assistance of social workers from Social Services Development Department in Quezon City (SSDD-QC) and coordination from the Philippine National Police. An Agent acted as poseur-customer and together with informants met at a certain place in QC with subject MARICOLE RAMOS and together with the victims, transferred to poseur-customer’s vehicle. They were then advised by subject MARICOLE RAMOS to proceed to a certain apartelle in Fairview Novaliches QC and also told the poseur-customer that she knows the owner of the apartelle. As soon as they arrived at the place, and the marked money representing payment was received by subject MARICOLE RAMOS, the poseur-customer declared his authority and placed subject MARICOLE RAMOS under arrest. The driver of another vehicle who tailed them up to the apartelle, subject ALEXANDER PERALTA y ABAD, who was hired by subject MARICOLE RAMOS and who fetched the victims was likewise arrested. Subjects MARICOLE RAMOS y MENDOZA and ALEXANDER PERALTA y ABAD have been presented for inquest proceedings before the Office of the City Prosecutor of Quezon City via online for violation of R.A. 9208, otherwise known as the Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003, as amended by R.A. 10364 sec 4 par (a) in relation to Sec 6 par (a) (Qualified Trafficking in Persons by Minority and violation of R.A. 11469 (Bayanihan to Heal as One Act) since both subjects do not have Quarantine Pass.

body: In line with the government’s campaign against erring government personnel, operatives of NBI-Naga District Office (NBI-NADO) arrested an employee of Optical Media Board (OMB) for alleged extortion. NBI Officer-In-Charge (OIC) Eric B. Distor identified the Subject as ATTY. FERDINO M. CONDEZ. OIC Director Distor said Subject was arrested in an entrapment operation which stemmed from the complaint filed before the NBI-NADO against a certain lawyer, who according to the complainant, introduced himself as Optical Media Board (OMB) employee. According to the complainant, manager of HYH Cellphone and Accessories, members of OMB went to HYH Cellphone and confiscated all memory cards and several cellphones displayed in the said store. Complainant asked the Subject not to close the store but Subject told him to pay Php 500,000.00 in exchange for non-closure of said store. Complainant then went to NBI-NADO to report the incident. On even date, Subject called the complainant and demanded the Php 500,000.00. Complainant told the Subject that he can only pay Php 100,000.00 but Subject disagreed and demanded Php 400,000.00 instead. On June 9, 2021, complainant and Subject agreed to settle for P350,000.00 in exchange for the non-closure of the store. With this, NBI-NADO, in coordination with NBI-Bicol Regional Office (NBI-BRO), an entrapment operation was hatched. Operatives strategically positioned themselves inside a restaurant of a hotel in Naga City where complainant and Subject agreed to meet. body: PRESS STATEMENT November 12, 2024 The National Bureau of Investigation-Organized and Transnational Division (NBI-OTCD), under the guidance of NBI Director Judge Jaime B. Santiago (Ret.), arrested an individual in San Fernando, Pampanga, for Estafa through Falsification of Commercial Document, Computer-related Identity Theft, and violations of RA No. 3720 (Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act) as amended by RA No. 9711 (FDA Act of 2009) and RA No. 10918 (Philippine Pharmacy Act). The case stemmed from the complaint of Endure Medical Inc. (EMI) against certain individuals for Estafa through Falsification of Commercial Document in relation to RA No. 10175 (Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012), Computer-related Identity Theft, and violation of the Philippine Pharmacy Act. According to their complaint, several individuals placed an order of their pharmaceutical products but no payment has been reflected on EMI’s account. Representatives from the companies who allegedly ordered pharmaceutical products also said that they did not place any order and that the signatures on the purchase orders were forged. Further, one of EMI’s clients raised that an individual represented herself to be a representative from EMI and was selling pharmaceutical products. It was then discovered that the said individual had scammed many other pharmaceutical companies. On November 6, 2024, another order was placed by someone who used the name and photo of an EMI personnel. When asked for the proof of payment, the said individual sent a screenshot of an online payment, but the amount was not debited to the account of EMI. There being a probable cause that a crime of Estafa and other fraudulent activities might have been committed, NBI-OTCD hatched an entrapment operation. With the foregoing circumstances, a controlled delivery was made on the products being ordered. Poseur-delivery rider was instructed to deliver the package to Genesis Bus Transport and ship the same to San Fernando, Pampanga. In the morning of November 9, 2024, the package was picked up by an individual, and when the boxes were already placed in his car, OTCD operatives approached him, identified themselves and their authority, and explained the purpose of the entrapment operation. Found in Subject’s possession were various kinds of pharmaceutical products, which were properly inventoried. Subject was identified through his driver’s license as CARLOS SIMBUL DELA CRUZ. He was apprised of his constitutional rights and was placed under arrest for Estafa through Falsification of Commercial Documents in relation to RA No. 10175, Computer-related Identity Theft, violations of Section 11(k) of RA No. 3720 as amended by RA No. 9711, and Article VII Section 45 (p) of RA No. 10918.

body: PRESS STATEMENT February 05, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI CRACKS DOWN ON SEXUAL EXPLOITATION RING IN BULACAN; 29 RESCUED PASAY, Philippines — As part of its relentless campaign against human trafficking, the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), through its Cybercrime Division (CCD), successfully arrested two individuals and rescued 29 victims, including five minors, during an entrapment operation on 28 January 2026. The operation was initiated following a complaint from a non-governmental organization regarding violations of Republic Act No. 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003). NBI-CCD operatives conducted extensive cyber surveillance beginning 20 January 2026. The investigation revealed that the Subjects operated as pimps (bugaw) and facilitators, utilizing social media and messaging platforms—including Facebook Messenger, Viber, and Telegram—to advertise victims. To entice prospective clients, the Subjects distributed sexually explicit photographs of the victims and negotiated fees ranging from ₱3,500 to ₱5,000, from which the facilitators took a commission. On 28 January 2026, NBI-CCD operatives executed an entrapment operation in San Jose Del Monte, resulting in the immediate arrest of both Subjects. Of the 29 individuals rescued during the entrapment, five were confirmed to be minors. The Subjects were presented for inquest proceedings before the San Juan Del Monte Prosecutor’s Office. They face charges for Qualified Trafficking in Persons under Section 4(e) of RA 9208, as amended by RA 10364 and RA 11862. “The NBI remains steadfast in its commitment to protecting children and vulnerable individuals from those who seek to exploit them,” stated NBI Director Atty. Angelito DLP. Magno. “We urge the public to remain vigilant and report any suspected cases of human trafficking to the proper authorities.” ATTY. ANGELITO DLP. MAGNO Acting Director, NBI #NBIServes Media Contact: HA Palmer U. Mallari NBI Spokesperson [email protected]

SANTIAGO (Ret.), implemented search warrants at locations in Manila and Parañaque for violation of Republic Act 8293 or the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. Director Santiago lauded the NBI-IPRD for successfully implementing said warrants and reminded the public to refrain from patronizing pirated products to give protection to the intellectual property rights owners and enhance our economic growth.

body: PRESS STATEMENT March 19, 2026 .justified-text { text-align: justify; } NBI SEIZES OVER ₱31 MILLION IN COUNTERFEIT DATA STORAGE DEVICES IN MANILA OPERATIONS PASAY CITY, Philippines – The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) – National Capital Region (NCR) announced the successful seizure of counterfeit data storage devices valued at more than ₱31.4 million following a series of coordinated enforcement operations in Manila. The operations, conducted on March 16, 2026, targeted the proliferation of high-capacity storage electronics that falsely bear the trademarks of global industry leaders. The NBI-NCR executed search warrants across two key locations, uncovering a massive inventory of unauthorized hardware totaling an estimated ₱31,459,990.00. In Quiapo, Manila, agents recovered 5,474 units of assorted SD, microSD, SDHC, and SDXC memory cards, as well as USB flash drives and hard drives, all featuring counterfeit “SANDISK,” “SANDISK ULTRA,” and “EXTREME PRO” branding with a value of ₱23,367,750.00. Simultaneously, a raid in San Miguel, Manila, yielded 1,124 units of 2TB and 4TB external portable hard drives bearing the “SEAGATE” trademark, valued at ₱8,092,240.00. The combined total of the seized items stands at approximately ₱31,459,990.00, marking a significant blow to the local distribution of sub-standard tech products. The establishments identified in the storage, sale, and distribution of these counterfeit items are facing criminal charges for Trademark Infringement punishable under Section 155 in relation to Section 170 of Republic Act No. 8293, otherwise known as the Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines. NBI Director Atty. Melvin A. Matibag stated that “The NBI remains committed to protecting intellectual property rights and ensuring that the public is shielded from counterfeit products that not only harm the economy but often fail to meet safety and performance standards.”

title: NATIONAL BUREAU OF INVESTIGATION
body: NBI OIC-Director Eric B. Distor has ordered the fast-tracking of investigation of cybercrime cases filed with the agency as he assured the public that the NBI will not stop until the cybercriminals are put behind bars and the fruits of their crimes are recovered and returned to the rightful owners. Director Distor also directed the members of his Directorial Staff and cyber-investigators to coordinate with bank regulators such as the Central Bank and other government financial institutions on how we can strengthen the banks’ systems and policies to further curb or eradicate any future plans or attacks on banks. Distor stressed these bold moves in the light of recent hacking incidents of a commercial bank last December 2021 that victimized hundreds of customer accounts. Distor also said thst hackers exploited the vulnerability of the bank process that they were able to find access to bypass the one time pin (OTP) requirement of a transaction that resulted in fraudulent activity. Immediately responding to the incident and under his strict orders, five (5) perpetrators involved in the hacking incident were arrested by Agents from the NBI-Cyber Crime Division (NBI-CCD) in series of operations on January 17 – 20, 2022. Two of the arrested Subjects turned out to be foreign nationals and 3 locals. Following their arrest, the NBI dug deeper in its investigation and has identified about thirty (30) more individuals who will be summoned to shed light on the recent hacking incident. Distor also unveiled his plan for the NBI to spearhead and sponsor a Cyber Crime and Digital Forensic Summit in the second quarter of the year in collaboration with the Department of Justice and Department of Information, Communications and Technology (DICT). “We will call IT professionals and practitioners to join the Summit as we need to have a strong and solid collaborative efforts of the private sector and the government to fight cybercrime. In this age fast technological advance where the world has become a borderless village, we need a united front to fight an unseen enemy”, Distor emphasized.
